review: This is my 5th time since 2006 that I have been in and out of Kotoka airport. The staff showed kindness to people. They helped me at the baggage claim area. They gave a sense of community that make me really feel connected.

The airport was very easy to move, the directions were clear and had enough space to rest and relax. Could do a good shopping and super friendly staff. Good toilets, especially I appreciate the staff in the toilet behind the kaldi's coffee

Addis Ababa is not the worse airport. With a little bit of effort at security it could be much better. Open more security lanes and this would do wonders. It however took me almost four minutes to buy a bottle of water. Card reader not working and then converting a USD price to ETB (why can’t I just buy in birr) requires two cash assistants. Surely they can do better with items of convenience. At least all the toilets are working today. The cleaning staff have a MO of closing for cleaning all the time. Just ignore if so.

We flew Ethiopian Airlines transiting twice through Bole Airport going to and returning from Kenya. Outgoing we had just a few hours between flights so followed the Transit signs to join the mass of passengers queuing to be herded through a badly organised security check with staff proving rude and unhelpful. Our return trip had a scheduled nine hour gap between flights for which a combined 'temporary Visa, transport, hotel and meal' voucher was given. Exiting through passport control proved far less stressful than using the 'Transit' route. A short wait for a bus and we were off to the massive and modern Ethiopian Airlines owned Hotel. Check in was fine, the room excellent and all was well until we went for food. As cattle class passengers we were only entitled to eat from the buffet in the grim basement canteen....it may well have been the staff canteen, it certainly felt like it. A quick look at the food on offer was enough to put us off, we left and went upstairs choosing to pay to eat in the Chinese Restaurant which proved to be surprisingly excellent. Potions proved to be huge and we embarrassed ourselves by accidentally over ordering. The coach transport from the hotel to the airport was again efficient, prompt and clean...then it started going badly again. Three separate Electronic security checks as others have mentioned. On arriving into the third check, and close to our designated departure gate, a uniformed 'gentleman' without explanation demanded and took our and a random sample of other passengers passports mixing them together disappearing beyond the E security infrastructure. I'm well travelled and have never experienced airport staff rudeness of that level. After passing through the E security I noticed a desk with a heap of passports where three security staff demanded I search for my passport. That done, my carry on luggage was physically searched and laptop swabbed and tested....what for I don't know. My wife subjected to the same process was left shaking with the stress. Before the airport experience my wife had long wished to return to explore Ethiopia, that is in the bin now! We will never return. I vowed to do my best to advise others to avoid this really unfriendly Airport.

It's an absolute shambles. You have to pass through 3 security checkpoints at the airport to get to your gate, and then on the last gate they take any water & drinks you bought in the airport off you.

The Airport is enough big for the traffic it has. Shopping is getting better. There are not many shops, but the number of them looks increasing. Immigration is ok. No problem seen. But there many check stops from the police, which may be a good sign of security, but I think it is too much. Bathrooms are not good (no paper towel you may need to have paper towel with you, driers are broken, toilets seen not to be taken care of in terms of repairs and cleanliness, you can find door(s) that don't close easily). Need improvement on that. For the money, you can change your Euro/Dollars to Algerian Dinnars, but not the reverse, just change what you need. But you can do the change in downtown Algiers, or others shops in other cities with much better rate (almost double), but they are not public, you need to ask people to show you.

Atrocious attitude towards me and my daughters, my daughter had a panic attack after very rude and unprofessional staff pushed us out the way. The staff are the rudest people I have ever dealt with nothing about this place wants me to come back here ever again

Special assistance bad, holding pen had no toilets, no access to water, duty free or food. Kept isolated from departure lounge. Has put us off travelling abroad. Hope never to have to go through this ever again.

Its been a long time since i visited the airport and man it changed. They launched Napping area for free, limited place but quiet and has good view. I also liked the drinkable water fountain thought it wasnt free for a second but it was. Internet connection was better than my last visit and loved the new toilets btw Overall airport changed it-self for better

I've been coming to this airport for many years. This has got to be one of the dirtiest airports I ever have to be at. The chairs are disgusting in the airport. It all looks like a temporary move-in situation that's been going on for years. I just happened to look down at my chair that I was sitting on while waiting for my flight and it was and all of the chairs were disgusting crumbs everywhere built up of dirt I felt like I needed to shower. I stopped at one of the stores. I got a small orange juice, two chocolate chip cookies, a seltzer water, and a very small instant coffee for my son and my bill was $56. I know I'm on vacation but there's no place else to eat once you're up in that area. Waiting for your plane but mostly what I want to say is this needs to be addressed with all the money coming into that airport. You should at least be able to make accommodations available that are clean and relaxing after spending All of our money on your beautiful island. The last I want to do is leave your airport feeling gross

Easily the worst airport I’ve ever experienced. First of all, the disorginization is unreal at this place. They tell you to show up at least 3 hours early but don’t even staff people to work at those times. So you end up sitting and waiting for the staff to even show up and work, which is a different time depending on who you ask. They have self baggage scanners and such for if you arrive and the staff isn’t working. They’re not usable because the main conveyer isn’t on. So they just sit there and you can’t leave to move on to the next step in the check-in process. Legitimately should be decommissioned or completely overhauled.

I feel sorry for the Elderly People who have to walk a long distance from disembarking the plane to then make their way to collect their luggage. If you are hiring a car and need to make your way to the pick up zone then good luck. Once again no thoughts for the Elderly or disabled, should they need to walk to the car rental pick up zone you better hope it’s not raining as there is no shelter on your 12-15min walk from the airport departure doors. Horrible set up.

Was really looking forward to visiting New Zealand for the first time heard so much about but my first experience at Auckland airport was terrible. Queues for walking over wet mats, queue in immigration and then some random questions about a form we had done online - it was like going back into the dark ages. If you want to do all theee then at least make the experience good for passengers

Our gate changed at last minute without anyone knowing at the airport, so the staff took about 20 minutes to bring stairs in a parking area far away from the gates. Several buses bus collected passengers for a short ride that lasted over 10 minutes. From landing to luggage pick up it took over one hour. Then I was going to fly out on a domestic Jetstar flight. A transfer to a domestic flight requires you to walk about 2 km without any warning or suggestion to catch a transfer shuttle which is not advertised at arrival. Luckily it wasn't raining but I saw quite a few older passenegrs struggling with their trolley and uneven ground. I looked at my boarding pass after checking online and I saw terminal D gate 22. Terminal D does not exist, Jetstar operates at terminal C. Jetstar staff say it was a mistake then confirmed the boarding gate is 22. One issue it does not exist either, it's either gate 21 or 23. Now i've just been told that the flight is two hours late. one of these days!

Not Verified      It's a nice small airport. When you get off the plane, half the bathrooms are closed. Middle of the day, about noon. Long walk and huge lines. Not cool. Very, very poor maintenance planning.

This airport cannot handle the traffic my last 3 flight Were great until we landed here . All 3 times we had to wait for a gate for over 20 mins. If you can’t handle the traffic reduce the amount of flights.  Stop bragging about you increase in business if you can’t accommodate the increase .
Not a good airport. Not nearly enough seating at SW gates. Few to no priority pass and Centurion lounges. Will avoid through flights in the future where possible.

Not one of the phone charging stations worked and I had a family medical emergency I was dealing with on the east coast with my family. I had to charge my phone in Denver before boarding for my next flight which was late into Houston b/c of weather. The lobby / gate area needs to be updated so badly. I didn’t fly into Denver b/c I can’t predict weather and thought the Loveland pass could be closed in February. I can’t understand why one of the most expensive places to live in the US can’t upgrade their airport.

Exceptional service during a stressful connection We are a family of 5 with 3 kids and were flying from Almaty to Dubai via Baku on 30th May and had less than 2 hours for our connection. Due to an unexpected visa/passport issue with 3 of our visas, we were denied boarding pass. After persistent request and pleas, the Airport transfer manager did all he could and helped us board the flight. We regret not asking their names, but I want to specifically thank the airport transfer manager on duty around 6:00 AM and two other staff members.  The transfer manager was outstanding. He personally took charge, coordinated with immigration, guided us through, and did everything possible to get us on our flight to DXB. All three staff stayed calm, professional, and kind while we were panicking. Because of their help, we made our connection.  Please pass our sincere gratitude to the team working that morning. They turned a potential travel disaster into a smooth transfer and truly represent the best of Baku Airport.

This airport is the worst airport I have ever been to in my life. In multiple parts of the airport there is no AC, there are no clear directions, there are not enough workers here to accommodate the amount of travel. I travelled internationally and domestically from this airport and can confirm that this is the worst airport experience I have ever had

Arriving at the airport, we are met by bossy, defensive and aggressive staff and TSA agents.  Then on to the terminal to run into the same  at “The Club”. 2 hour wait if you didn’t pay to rebook at a place where you paid for the privilege of being there already. So we went to Conina and paid $50 for two drinks and received terrible service from the staff there who spent more time on the phone and got bossy and defensive with her customers. Then back to “The Club” who texted us after an hour and a half instead of two hours and we couldn’t get back in the 10 minute window. After a bit of pushing, they let us in. Then we sit at the bar and watch the line on the right get all of the attention of the single bar tender who never came over to serve us so I went to the line and she was quite rude in serving us. Really bad day for Atlanta.

Approaching passport control the person "responsible" started yelling at people. No answer to our "good morning". More yelling. At the security check, more yelling yet. At the international flight gate, at the speaker we got only pro glorious us army brain washing propaganda every 3 minutes. Delta overbooked, any moment risk of being refused to get on the plane, even if ticket payed and not cheap at all. Strong young army men embarking first while families with small children and old people must wait till almost the end. "Nice" experience !
Athens airport passport control is the worst that I have experienced. It took us approximately 1.5 to get through the line. Absolutely insane! After traveling for 24 hours, this is a nightmare.

The security check is horrible. People cut the line and no one cares. The process for the bags makes no sense and there's no place to sit while they tell you the gate. Arrival was good, but departure was a headache.

I'm fortunate to live in Kefalonia part-time, Brexit meaning I cannot live there full time. So I tend to spend the Spring and late Summer / Autumn there to maximise my allowed stay. This means flying out of season which requires flying in to Athens on an international flight and transferring to an internal flight to get to Kefalonia. This is where the issues begin... Let's start with the good: The staff are all very friendly, if not generally that helpful. The layout of the airport is reasonably straightforward, although surprisingly hard to navigate and large if you are in a hurry. Now for the bad: God help you if you have a remotely tight transfer from an international flight - Customs, while not unfriendly, is spectacularly slow and understaffed. I have seen queues so long and slow that fights have broken out as a result of frustrated people in the process of missing their connecting flights attempting to push through to the anger of others. To make matters worse, international flights routinely arrive late enough and internal flights leave early enough that transfers tend to be very tight. My latest arrival in to Athens left me with an 1 hour 20 mins to make the internal flight is quite 'normal'. Not necessarily an issue as I had pre-checked in, had my tickets, paid for fast-track on my outgoing flight, and had no hold baggage to wait on. I was also careful to choose flights within the same terminal, but I was nearly undone by the immense and terribly slow customs queue, even though out of season the airport was pretty quiet. I button-holed a member of customs to explain my concern, he was very friendly and utterly unhelpful. "As you already have your ticket you might get through in time." With that he smiled and moved on to the next of many concerned people. Once finally through customs I ran through the terminal to security for my flight, and even though I had paid for the fast-track security was still dreadfully flow if quick compared to the huge queue for the normal security. I then ran on to my gate, thankful I wouldn't have to waste time checking the number as the company I had booked with supplied the number and made it to said gate just as it was closing, various people on the bus to the plan staring daggers at me for holding things up - another ten seconds and I would have missed my flight, to look forward to an miserable overnight in the airport at least while I attempted to book another connecting flight and get a refund. Note: Under the circumstances this went about as well as it could have done. If my incoming flight was late, the airport busier, the flights in different terminals, I hadn't booked 'fast-track' security, I had baggagee, or I was less fit, I would have absolutely missed my connection. My best advice: If you intend to book such a connection through Athens Airport, especially if you are not familiar with the layout. Seek out the regrettably very uncommon connections that have at the very least three hours between flights that are both using the same terminal - God help you if one of the flights uses the satellite terminal. If you can't manage that, I'm afraid you are best booking flights with a day or two in between and using a hotel in the airport or Athens itself... be warned that Athens airport is miles from the city!

The airport is design in way which makes it quite intuitive and easy to navigate. Shopping choices were quite good. You have the metro, train and buses, Uber point all quite naturally findable and accessible.

Impossible long queue from London. Two policemen manually checking passports. More than two hours wait. This is ridiculous. Very disappointing. No automatic machine passport checking. No extra staff brought to help.

DMK airport is a very non intuitive airport. No clear signs/directions on how to transfer from domestic arrivals to an international departure terminal. When a person is passing through a terminal that mentions foreign passport, the staff asks you to pass through a different terminal with the same foreign passport sign because in the staff's mind, that terminal is reserved for certain nationalities and the people are just supposed to know about that?

This was by far the worst experience landing and departing. This airport is overwhelmed with passengers arriving by the hundreds in very short time. It took almost an hour to pass thru immigration processing and another 45 minutes to get our bags. The taxi line was also very long and slow. On the departure leg of our trip, more than an hour to get thru security as They only have 2 scanners. Once we finally got to your gate, they had to many departures at gates too close to each other creating real confusion. They even had us go to another gate 15 minutes before departure. They are sadly failing at handling the additional tourism boom.

Our family had a terrible experience which matched the other reviews on here. For some reason, none of the staff smiled and they were quite aggressive with giving orders. On arrival, we had to wait around 2 hours to get through passport checks and get our luggage. For some reason, people who had not completed the pre-immigration form were prioritised and got through around an hour faster than people who had taken the time to follow the correct protocol. On leaving, we had to wait in sweltering heat outside the airport where the check in desks are for over 2 hours as one single staff member from British Airways slowly checked in a queue of about 300 people. However, the country is beautiful and the people are so nice on the streets so still recommend going to Barbados.

After a beautiful trip, it is always good to come back home. Especially when the journey goes smoothly and we had great experiences with the airports in Denver and Toronto. Unfortunately, Schiphol Amsterdam Airport was a miserable chaos once again. It already started with the directions to the passport control. There were closed doors and nervous staff giving all kinds of contradictory instructions. But the baggage handling was the most miserable part. After more than an hour, the first suitcases appeared on the belt. Suitcases from the previous flight were randomly placed in the hall by some employees because the baggage belt was full. The screen displayed that flight AC808 was 'delayed'… but that was nonsense. We arrived perfectly on time. We heard no complaints about baggage handlers other than ours (Viggo, which handles this for Air Canada), and everything else arrived on the belt neatly on time. For a while, things seemed to improve at Schiphol, but it is dropping back to a two-star airport: dirty toilets too, broken toilets. Broken water taps and a lot of overdue maintenance. A pity.
Queues are off the wall exit and departure baggage checks couldn’t be slower if they tried. Staff are rude with no time for customers questions It’s a disgrace for an airport

Airport arrival experience needed more than 1 hour and 15 minutes to clear passport control. I cleared the control in around 1 minutes but queues were too long while only 3 officers were working Airport departure experience was even worse. Luggage inspection needed more than 1 hour while passports clearance needed almost 2 hours. Again, i finished interview and stamping in less tham 1 minute but the queues were too Long with few officers Facilities are dated and staff unresponsive. Schiphol moved from the best to worst airport in few years. My recommendation to everyone is to avoid the airport unless it is your only option
Very slow security and passport control. Airport is overcrowded and dirty washrooms. This airport is outdated.Service personnel are not helpful and look very uninterested.

Try to avoid this airport when entering the EU, especially if you have a connecting flight to another country. If you must go through this airport, plan at least two and a half hours between your arrival and your connecting flight. During the security check, I left my backpack for screening. There are two paths—one where bags pass through without being opened, and another for manual inspection. My backpack was sent for manual inspection, but then the security staff asked for it to be sent back through the first screening lane, causing at least a 20-minute delay. I asked the officer to check my bag manually, but he said my turn had passed and that another officer would handle it. After about half an hour of watching my bag move back and forth, an officer finally opened it and said, “There is nothing. You can continue to your connecting flight.” The management of the security process was the worst I have experienced in 30 years of flying worldwide. Entering a great country like the Netherlands and encountering such an unpleasant situation creates a very poor impression.

It is a huge airport with crazy design and lack of information board. As we needed to transfer here, after disembarking, we had to walk 500m to reach to the information screen and had to keep walking for more than 1km to reach to our new gate. Why didn't they have more information screens? They were expanding or building something new, but have they ever thought of investing a train to connect the concourses?? Boarding was very messy and chaotic. No proper queuing, no specific lane for priority passengers.

I am a Swedish national, and we missed our flight today because of the mishandling of immigration Gates. The immigration line at Gates D,E,F,G, H was too long, less staff, inattentive staff, albeit I repeatedly told the airport staff guarding the line that my flight to Detroit, U.S. was currently boarding, yet the staff ignored our pleas. The chaotic Schipol caused delays and anxiety on my succeeding flight.

The immigration queue for non-EU citizens was more than an hour long and only staffed by 1.5 FTE. People were missing their planes and staff did not care. In terms of departure experience, this was pretty much the worst airport experience I have ever had
Landed 40 minutes ago and still only a third of the way through a huge passport queue.  Auto gates closed. 4 staff for hundreds of passengers. Absolute farce.

After arriving from a transatlantic flight, we were met with hundreds of passengers stuck in an endless passport-control queue. There were no separate lanes for EU citizens, and all automatic passport scanners were completely out of order. If you have a connection, be prepared to lose several hours. Eventually, only one desk for EU passengers was opened. The officer there was rude, aggressive and condescending, screaming at me and even swearing in Dutch when I left the counter. I have never been treated this badly at any airport. On top of this, many travelators were out of service, forcing people to run long distances with heavy luggage. Overall, this was a stressful and degrading experience and absolutely not what you would expect from a major international airport. I will try to avoid this airport in the future.

When arriving from UK and going to EU destination you have to go through passport control. They have the self serve machines but why is it that out of 15 machines only 5 are open and people are standing in long lines. The 2 policemen behind the country that perhaps could open more machines was more interested in their phone than anything else.I had to settle for a bad sandwich and a medium beer which had a cost of 21€. Extremely expensive for what it was. There was nowhere in the huge transit hall after passport where you could sit down and enjoy a steak and a glass of wine. Why are transit passengers treated in such a way.

This is one of the worst airports I have experienced so far. First of all you go early and they don’t let you in the security zone. You are obligated to stay in the entrance lobby which doesn’t have space for everyone and then when you get a chance to go to the security zone, staff is very unpleasant and very aggressive towards you. Once you get to security there is a sudden very large queue due to everyone running in all together. After you get through to the security they obligate you to take everything out of your bag, including laptops, liquids (within normal standards) and even makeup. They also start taking your liquids and jackets and putting it in other baskets without you knowing. My backpack had only clothes and another pair of shoes ( no medication or metals) and still they took everything, and I say literally everything out of the backpack, put it again in a bunch of baskets and pass it again through detector. Only to know that there was nothing in it, and I didn’t even get a “sorry for the mess” and they just gave me everything lose and unfolded, totally messed with and that was it. I had a difficult time putting everything back in place due to everything being unfolded and wrinkled. This was one the worst experience ever. To top that staff at the security (the one that handled my backpack) did not speak English .

It must be one of the worst airports in Europe. Everything is well organised with friendly staff in Paris and across until one reaches the airport departure. From there it is like a joke. No signage, communications, but long queues with no facilities. Clearly a totally disorganised airport. No seats and queuing all the way from arrival at airport to security. Unacceptable. On the other hand arriving at the aorport couldn't have been better.

Absolutely shocking experience at Beauvais Airport. For the first time in my life I see an airport where the check-in desks are closed because the staff are on a lunch break. Around a hundred people were waiting and nobody was there to check baggage. People were forced to stand and wait more than 30 minutes just so the employees could finish eating. Completely unacceptable for an international airport. The organization is terrible and the service is extremely slow. Even worse, there was zero humanity from the staff. My wife was standing in the security line holding our sleeping child in her arms and not a single employee showed any understanding or offered to let her pass first. No assistance, no tolerance, nothing. This level of service is embarrassing for an airport serving Paris. Very poorly managed and extremely disappointing experience.

I have traveled frequently and visited many airports. Unfortunately, during my time here, I experienced disrespectful and unnecessarily difficult behavior from some members of the airport staff. This left a very negative impression, and I would not choose to return.

This airport is a disgrace. At no time were the screens we were looking at said our flight was boarding. After waiting six hours in the terminal we missed our flight despite the doors of the plane still being open. The staff didn’t care and the next flight to our destination (Edinburgh) is five days away. Now have the added expense of a night in Paris and an expensive train ride and the loss of a night’s accommodation. Avoid this airport and its staff if possible.

Worst management of cabs and vehicles. The latest method of sending all travellers to P4 parking is the worst move, as there is no proper system. Shuttles come after 20 minutes. The parking toll booths don't work, and it is a mess. Especially, senior citizens are the worst affected, having to get up and down with heavy luggage. The management has taken a very insensitive move.

Simply the worst airport experience ever in my 35 years of traveling experience. From check in to security, the staff were unhelpful, rude and inefficient, traveler's basic ease is ignored and is a herculean task to navigate. An airport that sets the standards as worst ever.

Simply the worst airport experience ever in my 35 years of traveling experience. From check in to security, the staff were unhelpful, rude and inefficient, traveler's basic ease is ignored and is a herculean task to navigate. An airport that sets the standards as worst ever.

This should be the perfect local airport for me to use, it's location size and convenience are all pretty perfect for me. However every time I use it I come away feeling like I have been abused. Everything about this place is overpriced. Of course one expects to pay more at an airport, that is accepted, but their parking prices are nothing short of price gouging. £100 for a weekend in the poorly finished long stay car park. Nothing can justify that for except operator greed.  They have remodeled their exterior to enforce their passenger pickup fees, turning their grounds into a rat-run, a confusing maze of narrow lanes bounded by fencing. Having done that they charge £5 just to stop long enough to drop someone off. There can be no justification for this. I should love this place. My first flight happened here. I learned to fly here. Their greed has made me love it no more. Dublin is my local airport now, drop off and pick up remains free of charge and for £100 I can park for over a week. I hope Belfast City Airport come to their senses, but I know they won't. Greed is clearly the driving force they respond to. One day a car will break down in the middle of their restricted laneway system and that airport will quickly come to a halt. I'm sure they won't consider that their problem.

It has been many years since I have been to this airport, and I'm guessing that there has been quite a few changes since I was last here. When I was with my friends in Hua Hin, there were some local media reports that airport staff were unapproachable. Personally, I did not find this to be the case. Though the lines were very long, I did actually get through security and border control quickly, and with ease. I was a little confused as to where to get to my vehicle, but again, it has been quite some time since I have been here (around 17 years I think?) There are plenty of shops, and plenty of places to eat. Lots of phone charging ports available, which I believe are a must have today. I guess my only criticism would be that the airport did appear to be not as clean as my last visit there, but I believe that they can have a free pass on this, given how very busy this airport is.

Easy immigration process. Clean. Friendly staff. Architecture and decorations are average. Expensive shops (most things are double the price than in the city). Very bad rates at the currency exchange booths. No smoking area in the whole airport.

BKK is one of my favorite city but I am certainly not a fan of the airport. The departure experience is much better than arrival. I normally travel business class so have access to the priority security/immigration, otherwise the security check might be lengthy. One of the issue I face when leaving BKK airport is the traffic - the motorway is super busy and the road before reaching the terminal building is congested. The terminal itself is huge and blend. Everything is a long queue (especially to get a VAT refund). Aside from that, there are many lounges to kill time and some interesting shops that sell Thai products. Two years ago if you hold a priority pass you were able to use some airlines lounge (Turkish, Oman etc) but that has changed. You are now only allowed to use the "local" lounges. Arrival experience is more hit and miss than departure. The first hurdle is the immigration. Business class passengers on certain airlines have access to fast track lane but it is never clearly sign posted. And all the immigration queues tend to be very long.  The luggage reclaim is also an issue - especially if you arrive on a domestic flight it is a very long wait. The most unpleasant part of the arrival experience, however, is when leaving the airport. I use Grab - they are much more organised now but it is still very chaotic. It takes at least 10 minutes before your car arrives and you have to wait outdoor in this Grab booths. The staff are all super friendly and helpful though. I used to book a private pick up but the arrival hall was so chaotic it took me longer to find my driver than just getting a grab.

While some airports have optimised immigration queues by automating the immigration process, Suvarnabhumi Airport still suffers from long waiting times. This highlights Thailand’s limitations when it comes to welcoming tourists.

Overall the airport is ok but the purpose of this review is to provide feedback on the rental car arrangement (especially with relation to the drop off). I’ve never been to an airport internationally where there is an absence of one sign directing you to the rental car return area. With three levels all directly above each other Google Maps and Waze couldn’t find the area. We asked numerous staff who all just pointed down the road with no useful directions. We drove around for over an hour, leaving the airport, going through arrivals, through departures and every other option. Even when we stumbled across the area there were still no signs and do we kissed our companies drop off area (which is just a piece of curb side obscured by groups of people waiting for buses). For a major international airport this simple signage directing you as you enter the airport is a must. We arrived at the airport with a full tank of petrol and by the time we found the drop off area we no longer had a full tank of fuel so will get charged by the company. Very poor.

Overall, we enjoyed the airport. I would only suggest better signage and better staff training specifically related to the passport control area. Staff were confused and sending passengers to the incorrect queues, causing bottle-necks/pinchpoints. This could turn some people off of returning to the city.

Passport control is awful, but no matter how long that takes your luggage will arrive even later. It makes me ashamed to be European looking at all the foreign passport holders whose welcome to Europe is so terrible.

I arrived in Belgrade from Spain at 1:00 AM. My next flight, which required re-checking my baggage, was scheduled for 7:35 AM. The information board showed the check-in and baggage drop counters at 3:05 AM, but in reality passengers were told to come back at 4:00 AM. It also seemed that only flights to Russia were subject to additional baggage inspection before check-in, as well as an extra security check at the gate. During that check, passengers were asked to throw away water that had been purchased in the duty-free area. However, after passing this additional control there was no place to buy water again. I consider this unacceptable.

The airport has been expanding for years, and in some areas it still feels like a construction site. That said, the central part–the main square is now spacious and offers plenty of seating. The duty-free area has expanded and I particularly like the “Rakija” section, which offers local spirits, and there is now also a bar. This part of the airport looks pleasant, modern, and airy. However, the first impression when you enter the terminal by bus from the plane is a disaster. It doesn’t feel like a proper or serious entrance at all. Passengers are left waiting in the rain, cold, or scorching sun, and entering the terminal feels like stepping into a garbage dump. Does no one clean this area? The toilets are another major problem: they are consistently filthy, with dirt and dust that clearly haven’t accumulated just overnight.

The airport continues as it has done for the better part of 2 decades now to change reasonably significantly, to the extent that there will be quite big changes between visits if you are there 6 to 12 months apart depending on the phase. The commercial aspects of the airport around retail are where most of the changes can be seen. Some upgrading has happened in terms of technology in the security hall after several well publicised events with queues snaking out of the security hall and all the way out of the terminal. I think the improvements have gone some way to fixing the queue times there. The revamped food outlets are decent, not stellar, but solid enough, however as is standard for most airports they are way over the odds in terms of prices across the board. Transport to the airport remains somewhat problematic. There is a decent bus service, if you happen to be coming from one of the well served routes. Many will be coming by car, and this is a gripe. The various on site airport owned and independent satellite car parks are not particularly competitive in terms of price and parking here is expensive. Further, the charge to drop off a passenger at the front door is a ridiculous £5. This is for no more than 10 minutes to drive by the front door. The main issue that could and should be be addressed is the state of the arrivals from the gate to the baggage carousel and the journey in departures from the departures lounge through to the gates and aircraft. Departures takes passengers through a warren of back corridors that are badly dated and down flights of stairs before depositing you on to the apron to walk out to the aircraft in all weather. Arrivals is the same, from the aircraft through dingy corridors up stairs and once through boarder control you arrive at a baggage carousel that takes far too long to return your bags, even if yours is the only flight being served. Finally passengers will leave through a rather anonymous, cramped and dated facility before exiting the terminal for their onward journey… where again a friend or family member is likely waiting outside paying perhaps another £5 just to pick them up.

A real lack of organisation and communication from the check in through to security. Huge queues, despite it being a very early flight, There seemed to be a lot of staff around, but no one really taking any supervision of them, leading to a lot of confusion and delays. The self check in wasn't being supervised enough which meant that there were a lot of confused passengers not knowing what they were doing, causing big hold ups, combined with the issue that passengers weren't being directed to available check in terminals (not really waiting passengers fault as it is impossible to see what is free. Result = big queue Once self you have self - checked in, there wasn't any clear direction of where to go to drop the bags, especially as it involved negotiating the confused check in customers, the endless rows of tensile barriers, to form another bug queue to the unmanned bag drop offs, half of which weren't open. Same issues - lots of staff, but no one really taking charge in directing passengers to the available bag drops, but also hundreds of confused passengers not knowing what to do when they got there. Even those that realised they just needed to place the bag on the conveyor and use the scanner on the desk to read the bar code had difficulty as the scanners struggled to read the bar codes. It was a case of 'just keep trying'. Oh, and I forgot to mention the confusion around attaching the labels. The new labels don't require peeling back to stick them together, you just place the red dots together ad they stick. Simple, as long as you know it! Next issue - going scanning boarding tickets. Not an issue if, like us, you used the old fashioned paper version. For those couples / families using the phone version - well that was a different matter. Some got through ok, and some didn't. Massive issue where one person and both / all passes.

Terrible queues for security, never get chance to actually enjoy the experience as every time I’ve flown I’ve spent over 2 hours queuing and then straight to last call once I’m through security. They seem totally unable to forecast in any way. Plus maintenance is woeful, broken water fountains (multiple), broken toilets, broken escalators. Just nothing works and no one cares.

The special assistance is hit and miss.. there is also a disconnect of communication between the ground crew for the ambi lift and the special assistance team. We had warned special assistance 5x of the need of an ambi lift for the plane. They had not informed ground crew of this resulting in my wife having to wait in the cold on her wheelchair as a vulnerable person for a good 15-30 minutes. The ground crew staff did a good job and took control of the situation despite the above issue. The airport does not follow the radar key system for its accessible toilets. This has resulted in my disabled wife who has needs to use the accessible toilet in having to wait in 3 separate occasions on her wheelchair. The toilets also do not have grab rails or red alarm pull cords. The height of the toilets also vary with being too high or too low. Has management actually consulted with a disabled specialist when renovating the toilets?? Did you know that there are accessible toilets within the toilets? So for me as a male carer, I was humiliated with having to take my wife into a female toilets in order to assist her as the accessible toilets where located in the female and male toilets? There is uniformity of standards with the disabled toilets so its hit and miss depending on where and when you are in the airport. Finally security... the security lady pulled aside my wife in her wheelchair and did not ask my wife for permission to search her privately. The management need to ensure that there staff are properly trained and motivated otherwise there will be a loss of life. With everything mentioned above, all i'll say is there where a few good staff members who helped us when we most needed it. Worst off all ... they weren't even from special assistance.

Nothing pleasant about this airport. Nothing is fluid, nowhere to sit, 90% of the staff are grumpy. Myself and my partner use this airport at least once a month. I recall just once in the past 10 months being greeted with a smile at security. I literally dread having to go there.

A somewhat strange airport consisting of multiple areas build in very different timeframes. Our flight departed from the Gate 51 and up area, which is housed in a modern style mini terminal with comfy seating. To get there is like going thru a maze of corridors. Security check is done in a relaxed way but easily leads to long cues. Duty-free shopping and food corners are relatively modest. Large parts of the airport are busboarding only. Staff is friendly and speaks English.

This review is limited to the Domestic Terminal at Bodrum airport. Boarding and deplaning is via stairway as there are no jet bridges in the domestic terminal. This is a very clean airport with wide open spaces and 6 gates. Long lines for bathroom in baggage claim. Bathrooms very clean and well maintained. Post security there are several small eateries offering a variety of food (breakfast & lunch options), a Starbucks, shopping (perfumes, jewelry, watches, luggage). As is the norm with Turkish airports, one has to clear security twice (upon entering terminal and then boarding gates). The security lines moved rather quickly. No more than 5-7 minutes to clear. I didn't use WiFi but the cellular network had a strong 5g signal.

I want to give a big shoutout to Stanley from TSA at Boston Logan. I got to the airport around 6am for my flight to Marco Island for a really important business conference… and realized I forgot my wallet and driver’s license. Total nightmare moment. Stanley went out of his way to help me. He walked me through the ID verification process super quickly, was calm, helpful, and you could tell he actually cared. When he noticed my flight was leaving in about 30 minutes, he didn’t hesitate — he brought me to the front of the TSA line and helped me through the whole process, checking my bags, carry-on, everything. It might not sound crazy, but he seriously saved my trip. If I had gotten someone slower or someone who didn’t care, I would’ve 100% missed my flight. People like Stanley make a huge difference. I really appreciate everything he did for me that morning.

Not Verified      Just awful. I travel to Salento a lot and Brindisi is the closest airport. It’s all a bit dinky anyway but I doubt the border control meets EU standards. Registration is necessary both entering and exiting but despite this it is all repeated when you eventually get to the gates. The police are slow and surly and the experience is awful. I now fly via any intermediate airport and arrive via the domestic part. It’s a scandal that they are so far behind all other airports I fly through as they’ve had ample time to update.

The worst airport I have visited. It took us over an hour from boarding the plane to clearing security and there was only one planes worth of people. Security were slow and uninterested and the systems were dreadful

This airport has the worst immigration I have ever seen. Chaotic, unorganised (there are staff directing people to the waiting line but they are clueless of what they are doing, just getting paid to stand and randomly say this line that line.). Waiting for over 1.5 when departing from the airport and over 3 hours on arrival just to get pass the immigration. What kind of non sense is this especially coming from the capital of EU. The airport manager should be ashamed of what they are doing.

I had the misfortune of coming to Brussels by air. It was the worst customs entry experience I’ve ever had and I travel the world. It took 3.5 hours to clear. Just crazy with literally over a thousand passengers trying to get through. They are supposed to be putting scanners in and can’t happen soon enough.
Not very well designed. Personnel unfriendly. The immigration agent refused to speak French and French is my native language. . Overall, not a pleasant experience at all.

A rather disorganized airport with too much food courts and duty-free shops instead of passenger comfort. Security check is appalling, staff is grumpy and seating comfort is non-existent. It's currently refurbished and some parts are clearly from the 1960s. Unbelievable for a large capital in an EU-country.

The dirtiest airport I have ever used in my life. A national disgrace. Shame on you for bringing a stranger there. At the women's cosmetics section, three young ladies and one young lady were gossiping. The most talkative of the young ladies “dusted” her sister-in-law with very “spicy” details and the others were laughing heartily. No one paid me any attention if I wanted to buy something or needed something. At a so-called restaurant, I had the honor of being served by the “boss”. He was the rudest and most petty waiter I have ever had. He was doing us a favor by serving us, not us by paying him. And on top of that, the food was horrible and very expensive. My husband, who is of English origin, told me that he had never seen a men's toilet as dirty as the one he used there. Hello, gentlemen directors of Otopeni airport? How do you run this institution? Cel mai murdar aeroport pe care l-am folosit în viața mea. O rușine națională. Ți-e rușine să aduci un străin acolo. La raionul de cosmetice femei, trei domnișoare și un domnișor stăteau la bârfă. Cea mai vorbăreață dintre domnișoare și-a făcut “praf” cumnata cu detalii foarte “picante” și ceilalți râdeau copios. Nimeni nu mi-a acordat nici o atenție dacă vreau să cumpăr ceva sau am nevoie de ceva. La un așa zis restaurant, am avut onoarea să mă servească “șeful”. A fost cel mai grosolan și mitocan chelner pe care l-am avut vreodată. El ne făcea nouă un favor ca ne servește, nu noi ca îl plăteam. Și în plus, mâncarea a fost oribilă și foarte scumpă. Soțul meu, englez de origine, mi-a spus ca nu a văzut niciodată o toaletă la bărbați atât de murdară ca cea pe care a folosit-o acolo. Alo, domnilor directori ai aeroportului Otopeni? Cum conduceți această instituție?

Quite a disorganised airport with not very nice toilets. It has smoking rooms in departures that only café customers can use, although I don't think that any non-customers were kicked out. There is no drinking water. One has to ditch water then buy a new bottle of water in departures. Cost was 13.50 lei several months ago. I presented the exact amount in cash only to be told that the 50 bani bottle deposit applies on top (14 lei = c. £2.50). As the bottles are generally flying with passengers who will recycle them back at home this is a big con and was only mentioned at the till. I posted a couple of postcards in the post box outside international departures. Neither arrived in the UK. The Romanian postal service refused to help as I hadn't paid extra for tracking, despite only asking if mail definitely gets collected from there. I still have no idea so would recommend to post any mail elsewhere.

Nothing wrong with the airport per se, but the public transport to and from the airport is below par for any setting, European or world — one pays nearly €10 for dangerously packed (not an opinion, I am a Safety Officer) buses, both to, and from the airport, with "assistants" screaming obscenities at international passengers. This looks more like a racket than a sincere service, and does represent a health risk. Again, not isolated buses, this is the norm with ridiculous queues at both ends. Clearly there is profiteering at the expense of humane service. The airport itself is fine but transport to and from an airport does, and must count as part of the experience.

Everything was great up until the boarding. I had a duty free bag full of goodies with my sweater on top. The lady told me to put everything from my bag to my backpack as I was traveling Ryanair light), when I told her it was duty free purchase, she said she can see that it’s not duty free.  I understand people do it, but you gotta be a bit more polite when you ask to review the bag .

The security screening was conducted in a chaotic, inconsistent, and unreasonable manner. The requirement to remove our shoes seemed entirely arbitrary. Even more unacceptable was being forced to discard products due to a rigid and illogical interpretation of the 1-liter liquids rule. While passengers are given a 1-liter plastic bag, this rule ignores the obvious fact that liquids are transported in sealed, individual containers.
Passport control was dreadful. You had to queue for over an hour whilst staff laughed and joked. People were making the flight with moments to spare.

The Vat tax line is extremely long. We waited close to 2 hours and barely made our flight. Others in line behind us had a 3 hour wait. Many people gave up in order to make their flight. Is this long wait necessary? Or can it be avoided? Chaos. Confusion. Misinformation. Unhelpful/nonexistent signs. I get the feeling we are being discouraged from applying for the refund. Shame on you!

The Vat tax line is extremely long. We waited close to 2 hours and barely made our flight. Others in line behind us had a 3 hour wait. Many people gave up in order to make their flight. Is this long wait necessary? Or can it be avoided? Chaos. Confusion. Misinformation. Unhelpful/nonexistent signs. I get the feeling we are being discouraged from applying for the refund. Shame on you!

The international terminal is currently being refurbished, and it was very crowded on the Saturday morning of my flight because of areas being worked on. My flight departed from gate 81 but the gate isn't a room, it's simply a door out of the terminal, so the passengers on the flight (which was an A350, so there were a lot of them) amalgamate next to the gate and therefore in the path of passengers heading for other gates. It's a nightmare. Luckily we could use a lounge, but we made the mistake of getting to the gate in "good time", which was really earlier than we needed to only to find there was nowhere to sit. The worst thing about Brisbane Airport international terminal however, is the PA system. There does not seem to be any "zoning" of the announcements so when waiting at gate 81 you get boarding calls from all the other gates. So it's a constant (for example) "The Air New Zealand flight to Christchurch departing from gate 75 is now boarding group 3 passengers. We ask group 4, 5, 6 and 7 passengers to wait until the next announcement". But this is completely irrelevant to passengers waiting at gate 81. Now, some such announcements were fairly melodious and one complimented such speakers able to present the information in a soft spoken and informative way. But unfortunately other such announcements were so loud, raucous and piercing that I waited in dread for the next one. The problem is exacerbated by the fact that some areas of the terminal have fairly low ceilings, in which the PA loudspeakers have been installed about a metre apart. So the sound goes right into your head from about 3 metres away and there is simply nowhere you can go to avoid it. So having spent a very pleasant and peaceful hour in the lounge, I ended up with a headache after just 15 minutes in the public area. All because of these pointless unzoned announcements. I challenge those who are responsible for running and planning the airport actually to use it. Sit in the public area for half an hour with the loudspeaker blaring 3 metres above your head. Please let us know if you also get a headache.

Upon arrival at Brisbane Airport, the first impression was of a noticeably unkempt environment. The floor in the duty-free area was dirty. The standard of the arrival precinct was poor, with a tired and unwelcoming atmosphere. It lacks a welcoming atmosphere. The customs and immigration process is uninspiring and there is no warm welcome to Australia.

I want to say a huge thank you to Mischa from TUI and Damon from special assistance who were so kind and helpful to myself and my husband on 19 April when we were flying to Lanzarote They were compassionate and thoughtful in every way and eased my anxiety about flying.

Overpriced drop off and car park charges and the rudest security staff. Also rip off fast track. We paid for this and the only difference was we were given a different entrance to the security scanners. We used the same ones as non paying passengers, queuing for the trays then took over 10 minutes to return my husband’s shoes (and he told them he was disabled too). Complaints service pathetic with customer mis-services telling me this is still fast track even though we couldn’t use fast track services mysteriously ‘due to operational reasons’. No refund. Don’t use fast track as it is a con

This is the worst airport I've ever been to. I genuinely would not recommend it to anyone, especially first-time travelers. The staff were extremely rude and unhelpful. At one point, I was even told me, "You don't understand," in a way that felt very condescending and disrespectful. Instead of helping passengers, some staff members made an already stressful travel experience even more frustrating. Overall, I had a very negative experience and would absolutely avoid this airport at all costs!

This is the worst airport we’ve been to since Nairobi and that’s saying something. We arrived 3 hours early and you need to. The queue for security was ridiculous, very slow and allowing one person at a time to prepare their belongings. Once through the food choices are poor, the toilets had no hooks or places to put coats or bags. They were so dirty. There is nowhere to fill a water bottle because they want you to buy single use plastic. Our flight was listed as delayed and wouldn’t even be landing until 15 minutes after its scheduled departure time. We kept a close eye on the board and it was still listed as delayed. It then changed suddenly to ‘boarding’ so we immediately headed to the passport control. We went immediately to an agent and showed them our flight details and asked if we would make our flight. He said our flight was still delayed and the plane had not landed yet. We got In the giant, slow moving line. Whilst waiting in the line I asked another agent 2 more times and each time we were told to relax and our flight was very late. We finally made it through passport to find, lo and behold, our flight had in fact left on time. The airport manager took no responsibility, saying we should have gone through security straight to passport control and not use the notice boards. The coward that lied to us was hiding when we had to go back through passport control to get our exit stamps cancelled. No one here cares, everyone is unprofessional. We will never return to this airport.

This is consistently the worst airport I've ever been in. Today we queued outside for hours in the freezing cold (have experienced this also in the summer but different nightmare in winter). No staff stopping people skipping, queues for hours, lots of missed flights. Came well before the recommended time and didn't make a bit of a difference. Avoid this airport at all costs. Also have to pay for the toilet before security which look like they weren't cleaned in a week, as if the whole place isn't bad enough.

Small airport serving the most northerly part of Chile in the centre of the Atacama Desert. The airport is a 2 storey structure build about 10-15 years ago. Arrival via one of 3 airbridges into the main Departure level and down stairs to the arrivals hall which has 2 baggage reclaim belts, toilets etc. Out into one end of the terminal building into the Arrivals which has a selection of kiosks offering car rental, taxis and similar things. The car park is directly in front of the terminal building. Departures is on the ground floor at the other end of the terminal building with a mix of machines and Check-In desks for both Latam and other airlines. There is a small coffee shop etc on the ground floor. Security is up the escalators and quite quick. A general shop selling most things as well as a couple of cafes and other shops. Seating round the 3 piers is limited but sufficient. Boarding is pretty quick by group. The airport is quite busy for it's size being the gateway to the whole region. It can be quite cold arriving int he mornings, even in the summer and the air is quite "thin" at 2,300 meters above sea level - bring a jacket!

Today we sat 100ft from the skyway to get in for over 45 minutes because ground crew at YYC had piled snow in front of where the plane had to pull up. They took over 45 mins to come and clear the way. I understand there was snow - but they’d cleared 4 or 5 other entrances to skyways beside this one where no planes were at and just kept going by this one with the plows. Unbelievable. If I were the airline I’d be livid. So ridiculous.

The airport has improved significantly, with upgraded smoking areas, helpful staff, faster passport control, top-notch cleanliness, excellent staff treatment and assistance, and easy access to any location thanks to clear signage.

Upon arrival you will be approached by men in blue to offer to take your bags into the terminal, ignore them. You will be asked again if you need these same men to load your bags into the primary security scanner, the staff there will also ask you for proof of a ticket booking, even though the airport does not support digital boarding passes. At  checkin you’ll be given your exit document that needs to be presented to border control upstairs. Passport checked there, stamped out and checked again by a guard before you leave this hall. Off to the next security point. Very poor checks. You will be checked again at your gate where staff will take your water or liquids away.

The checkpoint at the entrance was extremely slow and poorly managed. We arrived at 8:57, and it took until 9:25 to check only nine people, while other passengers were allowed to pass ahead of us. All of this delay was only to pass through a scanner and place our bags on the machine at the main entrance of the airport, and passengers were checked one by one without any alarm or device alert. The police officer was rude and repeatedly walked away from the checkpoint. When I politely asked another officer if there was another female officer available to speed up the process, he responded by shouting, “If you are late, you should have come earlier.” For your information, our flight departure time was 10:45, and the issue was not that we were late, but the unprofessional and inefficient handling at the checkpoint.

Cairo airport in the daytime at least has much improved. Transit is well signposted and easy. The actual transit check can be slow and the person checking need to improve their knowledge of basic facts. Toilets clean and plenty and much improved food and drinks outlets. If to wish to take water/drinks purchase on board make sure you get a sealed bag at the duty free to allow this. Boarding can be chaotic but like in lots of places. Also very clean airport and a lot of active staff on hand. It’s a good airport for transit. Quite easy with a bit of patience. WiFi is sporadic .

We arrived there together with two other flights. There was a queue of about 300 people if us foreign nationals being served by two very slow individuals. The general mood was extremely authoritarian. We managed to make our way out after two hourS! And this is not the first time this has happened. This city supposedly lives off tourism and yet they're doing their absolute best to drive people off. On returning I wanted to buy something from the Duty Free and there was only one person 'working' there and doing his best to ignore me.

Waiting for the luggage at T4 was stressful lengthy and unorganized. Carousels did change 3 times and displays were wrong. The whole place at T4 was packed and passenger getting frustrated. No announcement or ETA and took 1 hour to get the bags.

Really poor airport. Multiple international flights leaving on a Friday evening with only two immigration officers to stamp passports. Similar situation at security check. The two lines took just under two hours. A total of 5 people asked to see the passports at different points in the airport.  Finally got to the boarding gate and Delta had another security check point and then the passengers were all huddled up in a staging area waiting to board. Find another airport if you're transiting through Cape Town - they don't care

Poor assistance for assisted passengers. No help at all till check in though we needed to get there early. Left at gates and expected to get to plane on own. (when we arrived 3 days earlier expected to walk from plane across tarmac to buildings) Departure lounge had only one very expensive restaurant which does not cater for gluten or dairy free. I think it abysmal that this considers itself a major airport.

Dreadful, from start to finish. Appallingly long check in process, an hour in a snaking, largely immobile queue through an exceptionally hot and low-ceilinged room. Chaotic security check, followed by a ridiculous delay to have a passport stamped. Even the snack shop after then disappointed, with tasteless offerings, which they refused to heat (there’s a microwave over there). A management tour de force of incompetence

I have just read through reviews dating back to 2018 and here I am in 2026 and nothing seems to have changed or improved. It is a tiny airport to deal with the demands from ski holidays yet airlines continue to operate out of it in high quantities. I am currently stuck waiting to go through security and will now be delayed as a consequence of the delays at this point, unreal! They know the high demand in volume yet they cannot even manage to ensure basics have been covered, such as toilet paper in women's toilets Do not choose this airport, go to Geneva.

For an airport serving many ski resorts in the region, this airport is way below standard. If I had a better choice I would never pass through this airport again. There was no bus to take us to the terminal and we stood on the tarmac in the very cold windy conditions waiting to walk to the terminal for what seemed like ages, then a bus arrived to transport us. It dropped us outside the border control location and we queued outside in the cold as there were so many people in the queue. When we eventually got through passport control we tried to collect our suitcases. There seemed to be 4 flights that had landed and everyone's luggage was coming in on 2 very small conveyors. The area was packed with almost no room to walk due to the number of people in there, which made carrying our suitcases outside extremely difficult. For an airport that is a major gateway to the ski locations and the thousands of passengers that pass through it , the airport is simply just not fit for purpose and is far too small for all areas passengers must pass through. This airport needs a considerable amount of money spent on it to match the sheer volume of passengers who use it and bring it up to modern standards

Horrible experience at washrooms. So horribly kept I have never seen it at any airport. I will say this is not the first time as I frequently travel from Chandigarh Airport being my home town and this is the worst airport for washrooms.

I have passed through Mactan many times over the years, and in my opinion, it just keeps getting better. Check in was very crowded, but we were processed for our flights very quickly. Signage on the international side is excellent. Airport is very clean, and flight announcements are regular. Duty free shopping and choice of eateries is excellent, and prices are very good. All staff have a great attitude from what I encountered. It's just a shame that with recent changes in my life I will not be passing through again. Kudos to the airport management, keep up the good work.

This is the worst airport I have ever been in. The airport I flew in from was Albany, one of the smallest airports with nothing going on. The food and experience was 100% better there than here. 9:30 PM and everything is closed for food on a Monday. Quite literally could not discourage coming here more. T.

Charlotte Douglas International Airport is what happens when you shove 10 pounds of American Airlines into a 5 pound terminal. Every trip through CLT feels like a live fire exercise in crowd density, delayed inbound aircraft, and human suffering. You land. Sit on the taxiway for 25 minutes waiting for a gate. You get a gate. Then walk miles from E to B because your connection was designed by a sadist. Half the terminal is under construction. There are 400 people standing shoulder to shoulder around Gate B12. Need checked baggage? Excellent. You’ll receive it sometime before the collapse of modern civilization. The airport somehow manages to feel overcrowded, undersized, and exhausting at every hour of the day. You are either: sprinting to a 32 minute connection, trapped behind a wall of slow walkers, listening to gate agents announce another delay caused by “late arriving equipment” Charlotte Douglas is not an airport.

This Airport is still in transition: on the outside it looks like a typical Soviet one, inside it's more modern. It's bus boarding only, food & beverages are slightly cheaper than western Europe and the duty-free is stocked with large amounts of booze. Staff is reserved to friendly and speaks English. Security is outdated but border control is okish. Transport to town is by trolleybus or taxis, but be aware of scams. It's annoying they've only 2 small screens with departure times airside.

Chicago O’Hare (ORD) continues to be one of the most frustrating airports I’ve ever traveled through. What should be a major international hub often feels like a constant exercise in chaos and poor organization. The airport’s size would be manageable if the infrastructure and operations kept pace, but too often passengers are left scrambling across terminals with little support. Customer service is a major issue, and communication is often inconsistent, leaving travelers to figure things out on their own. For an airport that handles millions of passengers each year, the overall experience frequently feels disorganized and reactive rather than efficient and proactive. Delays appear to be a near-daily occurrence, connections are missed. O’Hare has the potential to be a world-class airport, but until there is significant improvement in operations, communication, and passenger movement throughout the terminals, it remains a source of frustration for far too many travelers. Unfortunately, when I see ORD on my itinerary, I now expect delays, confusion, and unnecessary stress rather than a smooth travel experience.

Very crowded airport mid-morning. Arrived at Terminal 1 C concourse and Departed from Terminal 5. Since the Terminal Transfer Bus starts operation at 11:30. This meant taking the Airport Transit System Train from Terminal 1 to Terminal 5 for our 11:25 departure. This is a major inconvenience as one is required one to clear TSA security again. The lines were a bit long but we got through in less than 15 minutes. No consistency in TSA operations. At DFW I was not required to remove my laptop and iPad. At ORD, I was required to remove my laptop and iPad. ORD needs to have their Terminal Transfer Bus start operations earlier than 11:30.

Airport free wifi is very poor as people travelling internationally who do not hold an Indian phone number is unable to connect to this service. For example when you try to connect to the wifi it asks to enter an Indian number for an OTP to be sent. This is not possible for people travelling from other countries.

Concrete jungle; old, outdated, bad lighting, difficult to find your way around. I stayed in a nearby hotel and walked around the terminal several times. Signage is bad and overly complicated. Parking spaces everywhere, mixed with walkways, small elevators, narrow staircases.  Access roads are confusing.  Only positive thing is the train station which is integrated with the terminal.

While Cork airport is so easy to navigate. I have to complain about the Craft bar. The food for the price was dreadful. We ordered a fish and chip €24, a cheese burger €23, 1 pint and a gin and tonic. Total Cost €68. The fish was a frozen fish and the chips were over cooked. The burger was just as bad. Could not eat it and chips over cooked too. There is no justification for serving such terrible food. It's such a pity, when everything else is so good about the airport. How hard is it to serve decent food, not frozen. Will never eat there again.

I was travelling from cork airport to Faro on Monday march 2nd Unfortunately after I had cleared security I discovered that I had left a painting in a cylinder at the top of stairs just before security I approached an APO upstairs. He couldn’t be more helpful. He contacted the head of security who successfully recovered my painting I didn’t get the  APO'sname but he was an absolute gentleman and saved the day for me. Well done Cork airport.

Unfortunately it was an extremely stressful experience at the wheelchair accessible area for all my family. We travelled from Kildare where we usually go from Dublin but decided to make a holiday on the way back in Kerry for a few days and went from Cork airport. Once we arrived at 1pm (which was advised online to be there waiting in the wheelchair area two hours before our flight, which was at 3pm) we were greeted by staff who had a very poor and unprofessional manner about him! He was extremely unapproachable with no communication skills. He took our boarding pass details and went off. As a family, we were unaware the next procedure but we waited patiently for nearly an hour on our own (my disabled mother, elderly father and myself, their daughter) until we started to get worried as our gate was closing at 2:30 and it was coming onto 2pm. I saw a security man and he advised me to use the phone that was on the desk next to where we sat, which no member of staff had been sitting at since we arrived. I picked the phone up and Owen answered. I explained I was concerned why no one had come to assist us and he said: ‘You need to ring on the phone to tell me when you’re ready.’ Next, the staff appears from behind a glass office next to where I was standing, didn’t say anything, looked at me and walked off. About five mins later, another staff came to assist us and brought us to catch our flight. If it wasn’t for that later staff, I think we would have missed our flight. Furthermore, my mother can hardly walk and she had no time to go to the bathroom so she had to go on the flight, which was extremely upsetting on her as she was so nervous and nearly fell going into the toilet, with such a confined space using the toilet facilities on board a Ryanair flight. We had to rush from check-in, security and get to the gates in less then 30 minutes. My poor father, who I also asked for wheelchair assistance for him as he can’t walk long distances, had to walk to the flight himself which caused further stress. I will never forget this extremely anxious and upsetting experience upon the start of our holidays. It’s one thing to have no professional mannerism or people skills or even know how to do your actual job in assisting disabled people but to actually have to take it on your own to ask to be assisted when you were briefly spoken to and left for nearly an hour with no communication, I wouldn’t wish it on anyone.

Arrival into Colombo was good, minimal queue as Immigration and the bags were already on the belt, when we got there. Toilets in the arrival area were a bit nasty. Once passed customs there are numerous banks and mobile provider booths and can be a bit chaotic, but seems to work ok. On departure we arrived at the airport at around 7am and it was already very busy. Bags need to be screened before you enter the check in area, but this worked quite quickly. Once we had checked in there was a significant queue for emigration clearance. However there is a priority lane at the left hand side if you are travelling Business or First Class. The choice of shopping is fairly limited and it would be nice to see more places offering more local produce, rather than just tea and dried fruit! The main duty free shop has a lot of international products like chocolate. One disappointing aspect of the airport is the security screening at the departure gate, which must cause delays in flight departures and does not permit passengers to take bottle of water, for example, on the flight. Overall the airport works ok, however with tourist numbers increasing you sense that the airport is stretched to the limit and needs investment for upgrade and expansion.

Terrible queues at immigration - it was worse arriving into Danang when we queued for 1.5 hours. When we finally got to the immigration desk, the officer spent a very long time looking through every single page of my passport. There was no organisation at immigration - the queues were random and there were only 3 officers on for multiple flights arriving. We had the same experience when leaving Danang. We queued for over an hour. No organisation and officers opening lines and then closing them again so that passengers who had queued for a long time missed out as others further back in the line went first. Air side, the food was so expensive.
Wifi did not really work, all prices in dollars and very expensive. Food machine that specifically do not give change. I'm not very happy with this airport

There is a severe lack of information, maps, signage and personnel to assist passengers. The layout of the airport is terrible with few moving sidewalks and long distances between gates. The Passport control was the worst ever experienced. No information or direction given. Extremely slow and indifferent to making or missing your flight. Avoid this airport at all costs.

Our flight departed from Terminal 2. As we were flying on Business Class with a Skyteam airlines, the agent told us that we could use Fast Track to save time. Unfortunately, we could not scan our boarding passes. It kept saying that an agent would come and assist us. But no one showed up, and then a woman in security uniform came, unfriendly looked at us and told us that we were not allowed to use Fast Track, no matter how we explained and showed the Business boarding passes but she did not care. Then finally another agent came and rescued us. The security screening line, again, for Fast Track, was not moving an inch for minutes. Ridiculously, it was a Slow Track. At the passport comtrol, it was even worse. For non-EU citizen, there were 2 booths opened and the staff were slow, unfriendly. They kept chatting with each other, ignored passengers to sign documents. No separated lines for wheelchaired passengers, Business passengers, or families with infants. The Customer Service staff were there but helpless. The only thing that they could do was directing the EU passport holders to their lines. The lady at passport control even asked us to show her all boarding passes/tickets that we used for travelling around Europe. So waste of time and inefficient! Should the airport management dismiss the Customer Service team at the immigration??? Took us an hour, instead of 20 minutes as showed on the screen. We walked to the gate and were luckily the last passengers to on board, thanks to the slow immigration process. Denmark is a beautiful country that we really love, and the Danish is among the nicest people in the world. Unfortunately, CPH airport gave us a very bad impression. It needs to be improved so much more, specifically in aecurity screening and immigration process.

This airport has an insanely long wait for a passport check both to get in as well as out of the airport I flew into and out of Copenhagen Airport recently with my family, including a pregnant passenger and a young child. On arrival, passport control took over 1 hour with only a few booths open (one was closed) for hundreds of passengers. The same long wait happened on departure which makes no sense. Because of this my flight was delayed Baggage security and screening felt very outdated compared to other major worldwide airports we've used. Additionally, we were forced to check our flight-safe pram/stroller, which has flown with us all over the world without issue on many airlines. This caused unnecessary inconvenience with a toddler. The combination made the experience stressful and inefficient. Copenhagen is an expensive destination, and the airport processes fell far short of expectations for a modern Scandinavian hub.
The passport stamping lines are horrendously long because they don’t staff enough people. Had a 1hr wait to get to the official. Disgraceful!

I use this airport frequently and you never know what to expect: Some weeks ago you didn't have to take laptops and liquids out at security, this time you did because they had decided to use some separate screening area instead of the usual ... so you can get screamed at in Danish for taking your things out, and for not taking them out.I frequently note how staff are very kind toward Danish-speaking passengers (like myself) and rude toward foreigners, and everything is about taking your money!
