Forget drinking water fountains and go buy an expensive bottle of water, and then dispose of the bottle in the designated containers. Avoid this place if you can.

Not Verified      The worst airport I have been to. The toilets had no running water. Pre security they didn’t even give you hand sanitizer in the toilets, fortunately you could get this in the other badly maintained restrooms after security. They make you pay an airport tax of around 785 pesos which is cash only, you need to pay this or they will not let you through security.
Pricing for food very high. Need more toilet spaces Number of security checks(4). Saw a passenger having a bag swab on the way through in full view of passengers going through.

While DAL was such a breath of fresh air when it first open, they have allowed Southwest to far exceed the passenger capacity. There is inadequate departure lounge seating, it is almost impossible to find a table to sit with food at mealtimes, and worst of all, the restrooms are among the most overcrowded in US airports - such that that likely violate public health standards for peak volumes. Even men cannot find a real toilet if needed without a long delay and potentially missed connection- then sentenced to the underpowered and dirty Southwest on board facilities. This is one thing DFW clearly does better. On the plus side, their TSA team is generally excellent. Once you pass TSA things go downhill, however.

By far the worst airport I have had the displeasure of using! It is an unmitigated disaster from arriving and being put in a queue, in the baking mid day sun, coupled with the pleasure of waiting for the 4 passport control staff to process 7 flights and not a sniff of a drop of water for over 2 hours. Then there is the baggage reclaim, by the time you get there it will likely be spread all over the terminal as multitudes of flights unload to 3 carousels. A game of luggage hide and seek may appeal to some, if so, this is the place for you. As for departure, we had to queue outside just to get into the terminal building, in the mid day sun. Once we made it in and joined our 2nd queue this wasn’t too bad, only 45 mins to drop the bags and head to security, managed to get straight through and head to the relative calm of the retail area. This presented some concern with a queue extending as long as the eye could see. Beyond was the dreaded snake queue, coupled with airport staff telling us not to join the legendary queue until our flight was called. We sat and obeyed the forthright instructions. However, be warned this is fatal, you will be too late to get in line and spend an hour stressing if you will make it on time to board or get home at all. THead to your gate and get through security asap and ignore the don’t queue instructions. Other points to note 1) food average and prices extortionate, 2) seats a bit uncomfortable.

While I understand that the airport is relatively small, I faced a few avoidable inconveniences during peak crowd hours. There were insufficient security trays available and no clearly designated place to collect them, which caused confusion and delays. Queue management was also not properly maintained, as some passengers entered the lines from the middle, leading to unfair waiting times. Additionally, there was limited staff available to guide passengers regarding security procedures, making it difficult for first-time travelers. Only one female security checking line was operational despite heavy crowd, resulting in long waiting times. Lastly, although announcements were made asking passengers to sit, there was clearly insufficient seating available. Proper seating, especially for children, should be ensured during busy hours.

Overall the airport is a decent airport but if you are on business and need to be here then I hope you don't need the wi-fi. This is absolutely horrendous. Worst wi-fi I've encountered in any airport. Fails to connect, once it does it's slow, inconsistent and drops. You're better off tethering off your cell and using data. In this day and age this reminds me of having to use a 2400 baud modem to connect to the internet. Just horrible.

Departure from Terminal E and arrival at Terminal D. Terminal E's concourse is wide and brightly lit with a variety of eateries and shops. The renovations to the restrooms have been completed. Clearing TSA-Pre took less than 5 minutes. Didn't use the Airport free WiFi as I spent most of my time in the United Club. On arrival at Terminal D, there is long walk from the gates to passport control. The MPC app (Mobile Passport Control) is a boon for travelers. We were able to avoid the lines and get through in less than 2 minutes. The restrooms in the baggage claim area were very clean. DFW deserves kudos for designated zones for rideshare pickup in all of its terminals.

Early morning departure from Terminal D. The terminal was not crowded; however all sit down restaurants, fast food and shops were open. DFW is 24/7 especially Terminal D. Restrooms were very clean. The only negative was TSA Pre-Check. The only location was a D30 so we had a very long walk to D1. That's on TSA for having only one Pre-Check in Terminal D. Return was to Terminal B. Our delayed flight arrived to a very empty and clean terminal in the wee hours of the morning; however, true to its 24/7 reputation, there was a Subway sandwich store open with the aroma from the bread being baked permeating the concourse. DFW deserves kudos for a superb system of picking up rideshares with designated zones in all of its terminals.

Despite all the roadwork, signage to the terminals is very posted and clear. My departure was from Terminal E and arrival at Terminal B. As I spent most of my time in the United Club Terminal E, I will make a general comment about DFW. Concourses are wide and brightly lit. Restrooms are for the most part very clean however on our return the restrooms in Terminal B near our gate could have done with cleaning. SkyLink is excellent. We parked in Terminal E and returned to Terminal B and then took SkyLink back to Terminal E and to the garage across from the Terminal. Clearing TSA was a breeze with TSA Pre. Did not use Airport free WiFi.

What a terrible place. 50 minutes line to the immigration with an extremely rude officer shouted at travelers. Another 50 minutes line to the security. Everyone was unpolite, except one lady in the lounge. Don’t look forward to the return trip.

I’m giving DFW Airport 1 star due to the extreme disorganization I experienced during a 12-hour overnight layover. While the Skylink is quick and easy, and there are plenty of restrooms and dining options, the logistics were a nightmare. My departure gate changed four different times, each in separate terminals (A, B, D, and C). This forced me to constantly ride the Skylink throughout the night with no chance to rest. The final gate change happened less than an hour before boarding, adding unnecessary stress after an already long travel day. As a frequent traveler, this was the most chaotic and poorly managed airport experience I’ve ever had. DFW seriously needs to improve communication and gate planning to prevent situations like this in the future.

This is a very small airport with A gates on the lower level and B gates on the upper level. The airport was not very busy, so notwithstanding the narrow width of B concourse, there was ample room to walk by when passengers line up to board their flights. On the lower level, there is plenty of seating with power strips on each row, however, only select rows had power strips connected to an outlet. WiFi was easy to connect to an fast. Restrooms were very clean and going through security (TSA-Pre) took less than 5 minutes. Kudos to Emerald Coast Grill for re-opening after our flight was delayed by almost 6 hours.

Mixed experience at Bali Airport. The arrival was really good, very short queue, the food is overpriced and my croissant was soggy at the bottom. Arrived at our gate 6A only to find there were not enough seats available for our party of 6. So we sat in 6C where they had an abundance of seating only to be moved on as that was for another flight. Ended up sitting on the floor until we had 3 seats become available!

Small but clean airport. Time from door to gate was less than 10 minutes. Airport appears to be clean, modern and well lit. Staff was friendly and helpful, and airport was intuitive, but it could use some small restaurants or cafe’s outside of the security area.

The airport is a mess. I had to wait for shuttle bus from remote stand under the heavy rain. The security wait time was long. The sitting area provides too few universal power sockets. You need to get the access code for Wifi at a designated machine and it frequently got disconnected. Wifi was slow.

The TSA lines at this airport can be over 90 minutes long, wrap around the entire lower level and even outside. It is a known issue and they have been working on it for years with no reported date of completion. In addition, some airlines (ahem, United) do not have enough people to help with problems with self checking baggage. United's kiosk not being able to scan our passports, not being able to get anyone to help, and bag check in took 35 minutes. Then the TSA line was so long we missed our international flight. I timed the TSA line. We were in line for 82 minutes and didn't get close enough to see the security check in point. We arrived at the airport 2 hours and 15 minutes before our flight departure time and still missed. We are considering driving up to Cheyenne, going through security there, then transfering planes in Denver.

Horrible airport experience. If Dublin Airport accepts overnight transfer passengers, it should have a process in place for handling them. Instead, we were told we couldn’t remain in the airport, then discovered security was closed and we couldn’t re-enter for hours. That left dozens of travelers stranded with nowhere to go during an overnight layover. To make matters worse, airport staff were waking up exhausted passengers who had managed to find a spot to rest on chairs or the floor. If there are no sleeping facilities available and passengers are stuck waiting overnight, what exactly are they expected to do? The lack of information was just as frustrating as the situation itself. There was little guidance about where transfer passengers should go, when security would reopen, or what options were available. The entire experience felt disorganized and poorly planned.  If Dublin Airport cannot accommodate transfer passengers after midnight, airlines and the airport need to stop scheduling connections that leave travelers stranded overnight.

I have been travelling through Dublin Airport two or three times per month for 6 months. I find it efficient, and clean with good WiFi. You get through the security and screening quickly. There is a wide option of eateries and shops. My only gripe is that the gates at 332 don't have enough seats and the catering is very limited in that section. Otherwise a pretty smooth experience!

We arrived at the airport well in advance of our flight to Toronto (TS233). The lineup for checkin was chaotic and very slow. Passports were checked. Then the trek to security clearance was a very slow, very long lineup that took forever. Then came the walk and snaking lineup for Passport Clearance. Why do departing passengers who are not travelling within the EU have to have their passport checked? Passport check on arrival is the normal practice, but on departure? Especially after the airline (Air Transat) already checked the validity of our passports. This airport is one of the worst designs of people management we have ever encountered. As we approached the departure gate, the arriving passengers were walking in the opposite direction. We were shoulder to shoulder passing in a narrow corridor, banging bodies and luggage. This airport is so poorly laid out we will make sure we never travel through here again.

If your using Faro allow at least 3 hours. We arrived 2 hours before our flight when the airport opened at 4AM. Even though we were on an early 6AM flight, and the airport wasn't that busy. It still took an hour and a half to get through Passport control. Half the automatic barriers didn't work, 3 manned barriers in slow motion staff checking every page of your passport. We just caught our flight. we are Portuguese resident having lived there and love the country and the people but won't be back for the foreseable future, it's as if they are trying to discourage visitors.

The delays here at security but above all passport control for departures where we queued for almost two hours. Most counters were shut and the officers were at best desultory. We only just made it to the gate in time - and this was with no refreshment stop other than the toilets Allow PLENTY of time!

Passport control is a disgrace, people missed their flights due to passport control mismanagement of queues, putting EU passport holders in 2 queues and everyone else in the others when they realised their mistake they just slowed the process down more. This is the 4th time this has happened.

I was returning home from 4 days of golf the arrival passport control was slow (photos and fingerprints) but the departure experience was another level. 12 kiosks for all passports 4 manned, the rest empty. Self check ins approximately 8-10 at least 3 of those were not working. We arrived for our return flight in good time around 16.30 we managed to get through the passport control for 18.15 to be the last passengers on the flight which was leaving 18.30. No time for toilets, drinks or food and no time to browse duty free if we wanted to. There were countless people on stairs in the halls heading to the passport control (100's) and 100's more flowing in from arriving disembarking at their gates having just arrived. I felt really sorry for what they were going to experience. Its unacceptable to be treated this way it's not as if the airport weren't expecting all the departures and arrivals. Get more staff in to work, man the immigration passport control kiosk's we go to spend our hard earned money as tourists so we deserve better. Regarding the scores out of 10 I would give the scores of minus 10 I won't be recommending the airport or returning myself again i'll go elsewhere.
The passport control queuing is an absolute disgrace. It took more than an hour to get through. It left us no time to get breakfast or use a toilet before being rushed to Final Call at the gate.

RSW seems to be a good airport unless there is a weather event. So there was a ground stop due to bed weather. Went back to the gate and had to wait 3 more hours. The D gates are not equipped with all planes returning to base. Long lines for food and sold out restaurants. Waiters send home and service was very limited at all locations who sell food. Seating was unavailable and area was packed. There was no plan B or special event management.

Be ready for long waits generally unhelpful staff . My plane was delayed and had to wait for 5 hours before being allowed to enter the international departure lounge. For a major hub in Brazil the lounge is ridiculously small. The process to enter when arriving is pretty similar in levels of inefficiency incredibly slow passport control.

Security was closed without explanation for at least 45 minutes. The tiny Business Lounge (don‘t queue at the wrong one - and, of course, no mentionning on your boarding pass) was qwickly Full with no Access for many Business Class passengers. Of course, the flight to Lisbon was 30 min. delayed. Compared with European or Asian Lounges, the food was simple. If you don‘t get access, you don‘t miss anything.

At LHR, we are called to board and told the flight is diverted to Pisa. Departing back to Stansted the following Saturday, was very bad. Checkin was rammed, security slow, rude staff with an attitude, especially if one has a laptop. Not much post security. None of the airports 11 gates have jetbridges, there are buses lined up outside each gate, each one just as useless as the other because the plane is parked almost always 30m from the actual boarding gate. This airport is too small and unfit for purpose. At least, in only 10 years, a new state of the art terminal will be built to complement the existing one.

War time is the best time to travel. Dubai Airport was quiet and didn't feel like a crowded shopping mall like it usually does. Our arrival and departure flights were on time. We didn't feel nervous at all.

Terminal 2 is an absolute joke now, old security machines, boarding pass didn't scan, rude staff everywhere. No public transport to T2. Terminals 1 and 3 used to be among the best in the world, now the business class lounges are very dated, there are queues everywhere and it's just starting to feel very tired and disfunctional. Add the the traffic and overcrowded public transport and it's just an unpleasant experience to fly through DXB nowadays. It's also been removed from Google reviews since the negatives were now outnumbering the positives so the government forced removal. Here is the only place to review DXB.

Absolutely horrendous staff at the connections. They couldnt be bothered to regulate the queue, having people cutting in front. Lady staff who was in charge of the queue was absolutely rude, barking orders while being condescending. Was pushed at pace and had no time to take off my belt and watch, and was yelled to get back in the queue when the metal detector was tripped. Experience was no different to that of livestock in a abattoir.

When in transit unless one has a c to c charging cable there is no means to charge a cell. All USB charging station are not functional. Power at plug in points are off, and when airport ataff are questioned, they have no response.

Absolutely shambles. If you travel with kids you must go through passport control. Which is nothing but a farce. There are plenty of the new machines which the adult queue flew through. We waited over 90 mins as there were only 2 police on checking passports. Kids were crying adults stressed, as it has not improved one bit since last complaint. When we were queuing staff were calling for customers fir flights that were already delayed. When we finally boarded our plane, 20 mins late, we missed our slot and had to wait more, then just after take off, one of the passengers took bad probably through stress, had to be diverted. Hope they are ok. It's about time the airlines complained about the service, or lack of.

Total disaster queued for two hours to get through passport control after a 4 hour flight lots of machines out of order. Staff unhelpful very rude made to feel like cattle getting herded through no air con working and then after walking 100 yards had to go through whole process again -  a total farce, will not be back

Beware it’s Absolute chaos! Travelled with my sister and partially sighted 86 year old mother, arrived at the airport 4 hours before our flight and nearly missed it due to the really poor passport control area! Took us over an hour to get through, staff were rude, machines not working, no one had a clue what was going on. Staff were allowing queue jumpers and did nothing about it! No toilets, nowhere to sit staff did not care.! You really need to improve this will put us and many other people returning again, which is a real shame as it is a beautiful place. Stressful ending to a lovely holiday, shame on you.

The only thing that lets this airport down is security. The size is inadequate for the size of the airport and the amount of tourists that travel through the airport. I hate to see it in the summer. Security staff were very rude as well as the staff that are helping with the Non EU registration machines, for us Brits it’s a right faff and very frustrating experience even worse with very impatient staff. The arrival process was fairly quick can’t fault it but I just wish there was more immigration staff available to alleviate the queues. Overall it’s a nice airport but the staff let them selves and the airport down.

Absolutely horrendous. Overcrowded & overheated. Avoid like the plague. Staff grumpy. Prices poor value for money. Transiting - trying to get to zone B was like a trip to Mordor. In the name of god, get rid of the stupid lifts and fit escalators. Up and down and walked for miles.

A total terrible airport. Passport control is a joke in and out of the airport. Queue management and staffing inadequate at all levels. Passengers queue jumping and out of control due to not enough airport staff.

After having passed through their scanner, I was kept waiting for 25 minutes for my 2 carry on bags which had been pulled aside for examination, along with many other people. This airport have been euligising the fact that a passenger can now travel through security with 2 litres of liquids but in my opinion, this has now slowed down the whole process. I have never witnessed what I saw yesterday on my journey through Edinburgh airport, without doubt my worst airport experience in 45 years of travel. Staff kept allowing passengers to come through security when they should either have opened new queueing or closed security to new entrants until the present situation had been resolved. I saw a woman who had a new bottle of perfume in a box wrapped in cellophane with her and the whole package was taken apart to examine the contents. I myself had a tiny bike tool taken from me even though I had travelled to Edinburgh from another airport with this in my hand baggage with no issue. I had been doing a cycling event and have travelled with this many times in my hand baggage, with no issues. Going forward, given the time wasted and the hassle endured, I would just check in my bag as it cost about the same as Priority boarding. I'm not sure as to whether I ever wish to travel through Edinburgh airport again, given this experience.

The new security check area is a disgrace. You cannot see you bags and laptop etc as they pass through the scanners. Anyone could just steal your belongings and you wouldn't even realise until they were long gone. The long stay car park bus is another issue. It used to drop you off and pick up directly outside the terminal building. Now you have to walk the entire length through a multi-storey car park following a very poorly sign posted route. Edinburgh used to be a fantastic airport under BAA. Now it is one to avoid.

The new security check area is a disgrace. You cannot see you bags and laptop etc as they pass through the scanners. Anyone could just steal your belongings and you wouldn't even realise until they were long gone. The long stay car park bus is another issue. It used to drop you off and pick up directly outside the terminal building. Now you have to walk the entire length through a multi-storey car park following a very poorly sign posted route. Edinburgh used to be a fantastic airport under BAA. Now it is one to avoid.

Upon landing, it took about 2 hours to clear immigration. It's an amazing experience I didn't expect at all.  Despite the massive congestion, the staff appeared remarkably indifferent, moving at a glacial pace without any urgency to address the mounting queue. There was a complete lack of flow control and professional oversight, reflecting a systemic breakdown in service quality. ​As a traveler who has navigated various international hubs, I find this level of incompetence unacceptable for a major global gateway. Unless there is a significant overhaul in their management approach, I strongly advise fellow travelers to avoid Frankfurt Airport as a point of entry if at all possible.

Frankfurt Airport is one of the most disappointing airport experiences I’ve ever had as a parent traveling with children. We currently have a three-hour layover here with two kids, and I am genuinely shocked at how poorly organized this airport is for families. We searched the airport website for a Baby Room and got the message: “There is no match, there is no result for your searching.” For an airport of this size and importance, with this level of passenger traffic, that is simply unacceptable. There is practically nowhere to properly feed a baby, warm a bottle, breastfeed in peace, or change a child comfortably. Some toilets have fold-down changing tables attached to the wall, but that’s not the same as having actual family facilities. The food options are also far below what you would expect from a major international airport. There is one small airplane play structure for children, but if one child is a toddler — like in our case, almost two years old — and the other is around five, there is simply nowhere for them to properly spend time during a long layover. After five minutes, the play area is no longer enough, especially for younger children. No proper support for parents, no available strollers, nowhere to safely place or rest your baby during a transfer. And if your stroller is checked through to the final destination, what exactly are families supposed to do for hours between flights? I honestly cannot understand how one of Europe’s biggest airports can be this badly organized for families. Everything feels chaotic, uncomfortable, and incredibly unfriendly for people traveling with children. If you are traveling with kids, I strongly recommend avoiding Frankfurt Airport altogether. I would never choose to transfer here again with children. Fly through somewhere else if you can.

Frankfurt airport is the absolute worst. When connecting to my home destination (Boston, US), I was shocked by the inefficiency and total indifference of airport staff toward the time crunch that lots of the connecting passengers were at. When trying to reach the Z concourse at the Terminal 1, which is where my gate was, I got stuck at a passport control, along with hundreds of other passengers. There were only 4 officers at the control. This section of the airport was grossly understaffed, considering the volume of passengers that were trying to make it to their gates on time. You could feel and hear the despair of the passengers that were about to miss their flights. People's desperate appeals that they are about to miss their flights, were met with either a total silence or an occasional "wait here" grunts from the airport staff. There was not attempt at all to prioritize those passenger whose flights were about to depart. Additionally, the 4 officers took forever to screen each passenger, as if they were stoned or plainly just doing it on purpose. The only reason I made to my gate on time was the fact that my flight was delayed by about 50 minutes. This was such a disheartening experience, and unfortunately not my first one at the Frankfurt airport. I am not expecting the famed efficiency that Germany was once renowned for, but I would like to at least feel secure about making my second flight when my first flight lands on time, and I have a 2-hour layover. Am I asking that much?

FRA is a construction zone. To find a working escalator is a hit and miss. Long walks and 1 hours wait time for luggage. Departing from the B62 bus-gate is a mess with crowded boarding area. Boarding the bus to drive 1 min to a C gate to climb up the stairs to board via C sky bridge was stressful. Will the new T3 bring any relief to the misery at FRA?

I had a truly appalling experience at Frankfurt Airport. Only a single security lane was open for a massive queue of connecting passengers. When several of us approached the staff to explain that our flights were boarding and requested they open another lane or prioritize those with urgent departures, we were met with complete indifference. One staff member dismissed us, telling us to "wait patiently" in the only available line, despite it being clear that the current pace would make us miss our flights. I will be avoiding Frankfurt for connections in the future

If you stay at one of the hotels  Marriott, Sheraton, Hilton) and need to get to Terminal 2, plan ahead and figure out where to go. The signage is horrendous. There is no clear markings as to where to get the bus and allegedly there is a Skylink train, which wasn’t aware of. Then when it is actually time to check in, it is all self service with again.  After that overpriced food, and half the men’s bathrooms were shut down.
Worst airport I have ever been in. Long queues not moving, awful staff, lack of info screens. Flights held due to passport control leading to long queues. Avoid at all costs.

Very disappointing experience at passport control. I was shouted at by a member of security staff because I did not respond immediately when my name was called (it is admittedly difficult to pronounce). Instead of calmly clarifying, he repeatedly and aggressively said, “Are you not [name]?” while continuing to mispronounce it. I had my young children with me, and they found the interaction upsetting and distressing. The tone and manner used were completely unnecessary and unprofessional. To make matters worse, our flight was delayed by over an hour. While delays can happen, the earlier incident left us feeling stressed and was a poor end to what should have been a lovely family holiday.

Worst and most chaotic airport I have ever seen. Over 1 hour queuing - security staff make you unpack everything - and made me throw off liquids because it doesn’t fit in their bag which is smaller than the 1 litre allowance, they made me take off shoes. I would recommend Grenoble to friends and family but with this ridiculous airport I will not and I doubt I’ll visit France again.

Security screening departing the airport is painfully slow. Even though the line was very short, screeners in security are in no hurry. One of my bags got pulled to the side for extra screening (turns out for a spiral notebook?) and it took 20 mins for them to get it and look inside it. The person in front of me brought an excessive amount of liquids, and I had to watch her and the security screener weight the pros and cons of keeping vs. disposing of every product she had in her bag. Please read the room. No additional staff came over until about 10 people were lined up behind me also waiting for their bags. People have planes to catch. While friendly, incredibly inefficient.

Hamad International Airport offers a smooth, efficient, and high-quality travel experience. The airport is modern, spacious, and exceptionally clean, with clear signage that makes transit easy. Security and immigration were well organized, and staff were professional and helpful throughout. There is a strong selection of dining and shopping options, along with comfortable seating and plenty of charging points. The airport authorities have assistance available at very nook and corner, which makes travel less stressful. The airport vibe felt calm and well managed. The airport restrooms has all the amenities and cleanliness that any passenger would desire. Kudos for consistently maintaining the level of service and customer satisfaction.

It was one of the worst airports I have ever experienced.I arrived there from Haneda and had to transfer to the another flight to NAIA. I was waiting in front of the transfer ticket office for an hour but nobody in charge appeared. I thought I was waiting at the wrong place so I went out immigration and proceeded to check-in counter but nobody was there either. The airport was totally crowded and there were nowhere to rest and what made matters worse there were no wi-fi connection available.

This is the worst airport I ever been to! Everyone that works in the Check in is horrible at English! I was going from check in, to check in stand and all of the check in workers told me I was in the wrong one, even though the first on was the right one! After 1 hour and thirty minutes they finally took there time to look me up in the system and I could get my boarding pass. And enter the Gates, here everything was fine and the people that works in the shopping area were excellent at English. I almost missed my flight and nobody really cared about it - if you ever go here, be on good time, like 3-4 hours before or use the check in app instead of trying to get any help from the people that works there!

Although the queues at Ho Chi Minh Airport were long, they moved surprisingly quickly. The staff were efficient, and helpful, especially considering the pressure they were under. I agree with other travellers about the use of US dollars for food and goods — it feels unnecessary and inconvenient. Prices inside the airport were also very high compared to what you pay throughout Vietnam, which was disappointing. Overall, the airport runs smoothly, but be prepared for expensive purchases.
Terminal 2 at the airport is very hot, no AC in departure & immigration area. The washroom is not clean. The chairs in boarding gates are also not clean.

Ho Chi Minh City Airport is one of the worst transit airport experiences I have had. There is no visible effort to improve capacity, comfort, or basic service standards. Transit passengers are treated poorly. I have never once been allowed to use an aerobridge. Immigration is another major issue.  Interactions feel hostile, dismissive, and unprofessional, creating unnecessary stress for travelers who are simply passing through. For a major international hub, the experience is outdated, inefficient, and unpleasant. I avoid transiting through Ho Chi Minh City whenever possible.

My experience at Border Control was shocking, although I understand it is important for customers who are catching a connecting fight or are transferring to another destination, I do not understand why they continually jump the queue in full view of your customers at Border Control. An easy solution, to alleviate our frustration, would be to open a kiosk or two just for the people who are making a transfer rather than leave the already queueing customers watching in disbelief as their waiting time is further extended.

Easily travelling to city centre by train. Security check was fast. Baggage claim was also fast. WiFi was free, and no need to register to use. The airport was clean and easy to navigate. Boarding areas were quite small. More travelators need to be installed.

Horn Island is located just to the north of the very tip of the Cape York Peninsula of Queensland, Australia - the pointy bit near Papua New Guinea. It is the northernmost airport on the Qantas domestic network, and is the hub for the Torres Strait Islands, which are the islands between Papua New Guinea and Australia, but which are all part of Australia. It is an international airport, but is only used for international routes to PNG by charters. All scheduled commercial flights are within Australia. The major route is from Cairns, with QantasLink flying two to three return flights daily using the Dash 8-400. Hinterland Aviation and other smaller airlines then serve the islands of the Torres Strait with Cessna Caravans and other smaller planes. The airport itself is basic. Most of it is not airconditioned - so given that the climate is equatorial, it is fairly warm and humid all year round. On arrival you walk from your flight across the tarmac to the Arrivals gate, and then walk up into the terminal, through the check-in area, and outside to a covered area to wait for your baggage. This is a fairly slowly process but eventually the tractor carrying your baggage on the trailer will come around and you get to the locate it and take it off the trailer. There are then coaches waiting (they can be pre-booked) to take you and your baggage either to the wharf for movement by ferry to Thursday Island (the main town in the Torres Strait) or to Horn Island accommodation which is about 5 km away. If you are transiting through Horn Island Airport then you just take it straight to your next check-in counter. There is no transfer of luggage through Horn Island - you need to collect your luggage and then check it in for your next flight. On departure, the reverse. If on Thursday Island you find your way to the wharf, catch the ferry across, onto the coach to the airport, and check in. If staying in accommodation on Horn Island, you can organise transfers with your hosts. Once at the airport, you queue at the check-in (no priority lanes for Qantas - just a queue snaking out of the check-in area!). If traveling on the small local carriers you just wait around till the pilot calls your flight. If travelling Qantas, you can go into the airside departure lounge which is the only airconditioned part of the airport, and wait until the Dash 8 has arrived from Cairns and is ready to return home. As you enter the departure lounge you will go through the usual security checks and scans you would get in a larger airport. There are about 80 chairs in the departure lounge (enough for the 72-seater Dash 8), but not much else. Airport facilities: a small canteen in the check-in area. Toilets adjacent to the check-in area and in the airconditioned departure lounge after security, and usually reasonably clean. Wifi - nil. But mobile reception is good, so you can tether to your mobile phone. Summary: a warm and sweaty experience, executed at a casual pace, island-style! If you expecting Changi or Sydney or Cairns you will be badly disappointed: but it will get you onto your plane and to where you want to be.

Terrible experience, 2 automatic passport gates functioning to get all the passengers on board for a Manchester flight, one of which kept a man waiting 10 minutes to get through. In the end the gates all flashed exit and let the passengers through in a free for all. There was no signage to indicate EU passengers needed to use a different gate, so after waiting to reach the gate I was told I was in the wrong queue, after joining the right (much shorter) queue , I was next in line for the automatic gate when the gates all opened to allow the free for all. This airport is either inadequate or a shambles or possibly both.

The ticket machines to the city center only accept WeChat Pay and Alipay, not cash or credit cards, which is very inconvenient! On the day we went, the three of us wasted over half an hour trying to buy tickets because we couldn't use the above payment methods, and were forced to go to another customer service counter and wait in a long queue again! I hope the ticket machines will be improved soon by adding more payment options and clearer information for people from all different countries!

Overcrowded. Staff that spoke Cantonese and expected the world to understand it. Very bad for a major world city. We were halfway through the check in queue and were redirected by a ground staff to another queue, that turns out to be a wrong queue and then we waited in another “expedited” queue that took so long that we spent an hour for the whole ordeal. We didn’t know where to go and staff speaking Cantonese made the situation worse. We have two young children in tow, and they could have given us a priority queue but they didn’t.  They should just build a second terminal bearing in mind customer volume.

After going through the long security line, I left a 1/4 cup of water in my metal bottle. The rude man told me I had to throw out my metal bottle or go back through the line. I couldn’t drink it. He wouldn’t dump it. He was not polite.  I went through the long line again, at which time I swallowed the water. I get back up to the security point, and next thing I’m getting a detailed pat down and had to have my shoes xrayed. If I could avoid this airport, trust me, I would. A few weeks ago no one told us terminal B was closed for construction, and the shuttle driver from the rental place didn’t speak English so we didn’t know what was going on. We went all over the airport, trying to find B. Riding a tram. No b. Finally a woman tells us it’s closed and we need to go to C. Really? This info could not have been given out before this? At this point we’re getting anxious. We need to go back through the airport with all our luggage. I had to lug a 50 lb suitcase up two flights of stairs because this airport can’t even keep escalators running.  I’ve been to many airports and have never been treated this way.

This review is limited to Terminal E. This is a very busy airport. Arrival from DFW was at Gate C43. Short walk to the E gates for our connecting flight to LAX. Terminal E has wide open spaces with a variety of sit down restaurants (BBQ, Tex-Mex and Asian). The concourse is wide enough to host kiosks and restaurants in the middle. Did not use Airport WiFI as I spent most of my time waiting in the United Club. At the gate area, there was a dearth of sitting.

I flew from terminal 1.  Most of the times Hurghada airport isnt so bad, security is crazy and takes ages but its everywhere in egypt.  I hate the security check with all luggages on arrival more than on departure as it doesn't make sense as all was checked on airport where we're flying from. Prices on airport can go high but Istanbul is worse.  And they need free WiFi. The one what is offered supposed to work for 15 mins but never able to be connected. In 2026 its a shame.

Security was extremely disappointing today around 5:10 a.m. One of the agents moved from her screening lane to direct passengers to a faster-moving lane. When I didn’t move quickly enough because I didn’t realize she wanted more people to switch over, she loudly said, “Well, if you don’t want to move and stay in that lane, do it. You can make a longer line, I don’t care.” That was very unprofessional and unnecessary. As I moved toward luggage screening, I also observed a passenger with one arm being rushed through the process. A security agent abruptly tapped him on the shoulder to remind him to empty his pockets, even though he appeared confused and was clearly trying to comply. It was uncomfortable to watch. I chose a different lane after that because the overall tone and treatment from staff made passengers feel as though we didn’t matter. Staff need better training on how to communicate professionally during busy mornings and how to treat travelers with respect and patience. I travel frequently, but today’s experience was completely out of control.

Found this airport quite frustrating coming in and departing. I understand it’s winter and ski busy however it really doesn’t fit the Austrian model of efficient and reliable. There is snow every year and people will travel there because of its proximity to the slopes. There’s lots that needs sorting at this airport and it surprises me that it is so antiquated. It says that this is a great airport, not from a customer point of view

Indianapolis International Airport has been my home airport for many years. It is clean and easy to navigate and the tsa lines usually are efficient and speedy. However, this is my 2nd flight this year and my second time waiting on their maintenance crew to do something minor on the plane and taking forever to do it! We have been delayed over 45 minutes and most of that is waiting on them to finish the paperwork! I’m probably going to miss my connection as it is. Also Most of the gate personnel are not friendly and some are downright rude. And most of them are late getting to the gate. Indy, you need to work on your efficiency.
This has been probably the worst airport I have visited. Staff is rude and unfriendly.  The airport looks extremely messy. Impossible to connect with wifi if you don’t have local number.

The AI way of creating check in is a good initiative but they are not proper and wasted our time to get the boarding pass after too much struggle have to stand in the queue to get our boarding pass. There are multiple EV vehicle running in the airport but with no help for urgency, had my wife and my kid with me our gate number was 01, the airport was massive but when asked for help no one don't know who books all the EV vehicle which were running in the airport none came it's one of the most horrible moments we had we had to run because of AI check in and because of the EV vehicle.

Security screening is very slow and unorganized. Security personnel are rude while talking to passengers, there is no separate queue for staff, all are mix up and screening delay with long queue. Departure side washroom cleanliness is very poor. Apart from that everything thing was very good.

They went above and beyond to locate and deliver my phone within an hour from the taxi drop off to my gate. I cannot express my gratitude for their care and kindness throughout this process. Information at gate 250, and the staff from gate 241 should be rewarded for their professionalism, prompt work, and great service.

Stay away from T2, especially after Asiana’s move from T1 to T2 in January 2026. You would think that the terminal with Korea’s two flagship carriers would have the best service, but you would be wrong. Those two airlines are great, but the airport experience is not. Lines to get through security are quite long, but that is because they only open a small fraction of the xray machines. I live here, and I have seen the same problem go uncorrected for a long time. Lots of brand new security machines that are not even used. For inbound flights, the wait for baggage to come out at T2 is longer than at T1. Why? Korea prides itself on short waits and prompt service, but the management at T2 did not get the memo.

I was repeatedly passed between different counters at Terminal 2, with no staff member willing to explain the process. Multiple staff members refused to escalate the issue to a supervisor when requested, showing zero concern for passengers. Terminal signage was unclear and confusing, and  service desk was unstaffed when needed. The operational coordination appeared chaotic, with staff acting independently and inconsistently.

I would give it -1 if it would be available! Worst airport I‘ve seen so far. Incoherent airport indications, very careless/indifferent security staff. When it comes to passport control -it's even worse - there was no officer to control the passports and people were stranded in between security control and passport control with no designed places for waiting so pleople are just waiting standing or in the floor! It's like they don't want you through their airport at all. They even confiscated a jar honey, even though the EU regulation has come.into effect in the first day of 2026. So, now stuck in this area without water and a place to sit. And no explanations presented anywhere! I guess it's good for only arriving, but not for departures. I'll make sure I never fly back though this airport again.

Ronaldsway Airport does have some positives. The airport itself is generally clean and tidy, and its small size makes it far easier to navigate than many larger airports. Although amenities are limited — for example there is only one drinking fountain past security — the compact layout does at least make getting around straightforward and less stressful. The airport is also very well connected for public transport. Bus stops are right outside the terminal with regular services across the island, and the steam railway station is only a short walk away when trains are running, which is a nice touch for visitors. Unfortunately, the security experience seriously lets the airport down. Passengers should be extremely careful about what they pack. I have personally witnessed security confiscating toiletries and items that passengers had originally flown into the island with without issue, which creates confusion and frustration when travelling home. The behaviour of some security staff is also deeply concerning. Staff often come across as openly hostile and unnecessarily confrontational towards passengers. On multiple occasions I have seen travellers left distressed during security checks while staff appeared dismissive rather than helpful or professional. Security procedures feel disorganised and inefficient, with long delays, chaotic queues, and what appears to be outdated scanning equipment leading to excessive manual bag searches and repeated swabs or secondary checks. Luggage is also handled carelessly, so I would strongly advise against packing fragile items. Most disappointing of all is how unwelcoming the experience has become. The Isle of Man is normally known for friendly, polite, and approachable people, yet the atmosphere at the airport now feels like the complete opposite. There also seems to be very little empathy shown towards passengers with mobility difficulties, anxiety, or nervous flyers. It is a shame, because the airport itself has the potential to provide a pleasant and convenient travel experience, but the attitude and organisation of security staff consistently undermine it.

The airport is overwhelmingly crowded—perhaps too small for such a volume of people. The restrooms are one of the biggest problems. Each one is relatively spacious, with two sinks but only a single toilet, which usually results in a long line. The sheer crowding and confined spaces create a suffocating feeling, especially if you’re in transit with no access to open areas. It’s truly terrible and inhumane.

We travelled with Saudi airlines in October and transited through Jeddah. I completed the online form to request a wheelchair for my elderly mum as she cannot walk far. When we went through Jeddah on the way out everything was fine but on our return journey we had a really hard time getting a wheelchair. When we got off the plane they said we had not informed them even though we had. After a few minutes of requesting they let her sit in one of the wheelchairs that were waiting. All the way through the airport the man pushing the wheelchair kept telling us we had not booked it.

The airport is alright. It is big, spacious, with shops and a big fish tank. But when I returned to the UK I flew with Wizzair and the boarding agent was using her mobile most of the time which gave a bad impression, and was very rude and unfriendly way. Luckily, my experience in the country has been positive and I found very nice people during my trip. That lady is an exception. I assume she has had a very bad day and she may have been stressful but she must know how to control her emotions and work under pressure. I was shocked such as behaviour and I think it is important to let know. Saudi Arabia has an 2030 vision and Tourism is one of the factor. Staff like her is damaging the reputation of a great country.

Arrival from gate 6 to exit doors must be getting on for a mile and thats hard work for anyone with walking issues. Departure is a similar distance to get to departure gate, Facilities are basic due to so called rebuilding and renovations hint here demolish the whole place and start over again with some characteristics that benefit the passengers who have to pass through the place. It sort of sums Jersey up really, an attitude and resentment towards those visiting the place.

Jakarta Soekarno-Hatta Airport’s Terminal 3 is the only modern international terminal, while Terminals 1 and 2 are mainly domestic/low-cost. They’re making the airport more beautiful, but the urgent issues remain: the check-in waiting area is overcrowded, immigration and security lanes are small, and taxi/ride-hailing pickup is chaotic, with multiple services competing at once. International arrivals baggage claim is crowded, with only 5 belts for regular luggage and 1 for oversized items. A Terminal 4 is urgently needed to improve passenger flow and comfort.

A large airport and generally comfortable with ample facilities and plenty of shopping. The Gautrain connection to Sandton is excellent. Plenty of lounges as well. Departure to LHR was not a pleasant experience however. Security was very busy, and insufficent gap between there and Border Control, which was also queued massively. No aircon either. So arrival, easy, international departure not.

The airport is very nice and the people are very friendly. Security was very quick. My only concern was with the bag screening. When I got home, I opened to find that my suitcase had been searched, which is not unusual. However, they opened my toilet kit, portable mouse case, and portable spaceball case and did not close them. Toiletries were spilled out, my heavy spaceball was completely free from its case and bouncing around loose, and the tiny dongles for the mouse and spaceball were loose in the bottom of my suitcase. I was very disappointed to see my personal possessions treated so disrespectfully.

After clearing security, which was operating efficiently, all international passengers were directed into a single passport control queue. The queue was extremely long, with approximately two hundred people waiting. Despite the volume of passengers, only two passport officers were present. For a significant period, one of the two officers was occupied for nearly 30 minutes assisting two passengers with documentation issues. This left only one officer processing the entire queue of international travelers. There was no visible system to control passenger movement or enforce basic queue order. The line quickly descended into chaos. Over the course of approximately 45 minutes, an estimated 30 to 40 passengers bypassed the queue and walked directly toward the front. The behavior was clearly self-reinforcing. Once a few individuals successfully cut the line without consequence, others followed, creating a continuous stream of line cutting. The absence of staff supervision effectively signaled to passengers that queue rules were optional. Security personnel were not monitoring the line during this period. There was no intervention as the number of line cutters increased. The situation escalated into open frustration among passengers, and only after passengers began raising their voices and confronting those cutting in line did security staff appear and open an additional processing channel. A man was raising his voice at a younger woman who was protesting the cutting behavior. The overall experience reflected not a minor staffing issue but a systemic failure in passenger flow management. The combination of understaffed passport control, lack of queue supervision, and delayed intervention allowed disorder to spread throughout the line. This level of operational collapse is unacceptable for an international airport serving large volumes of global travelers.
Food very expensive.  Food court meal USD30. Trolley not free. No wheelchair while waiting in terminal. My mother in law ended up walking to gate.

This is one beautiful airport. We used both Domestic and International parts of the terminal. This was our first time using domestic side. For domestic departures, there is a short walk from security to the G gate departures. As with the international side, there is a wide a variety of shopping and dining available. The self baggage check was very easy to use. The bathrooms overall are very clean; however, the bathrooms at gate G3 for our departure to Bodrum had an unpleasant odor. Didn't use WiFi but cellular network strong with a 5G signal. On arrival there is long walk from the gates to baggage claim. Transferring to international flights is very easy. As we had carry on luggage, we accessed the separate business class check to go through security. The distances in the international departures can be rather long given the size of the terminal. For an early afternoon departure, the airport was very very busy. One sees a smorgasbord of people from around the world. Both the domestic and international terminals are brightly lit, cleaning and gleaming.

Chaotic and overpriced. Unfriendly staff. Don't use it, don't connect and if you have to be prepared. If you depart, stay as less as possible, if you connect, bring food and beverage from the departing airport.

I had to walk an ungodly amount of distance to get to security, which was another surprise since we were transit passengers who had cleared security and were in transit. Extremely rude staff at security. The Turkish Airlines counter person was not very helpful and could not explain a simple thing like what do we do next. Shocking surprise was lack of lounge chairs anywhere in the main area (not boarding area).  The prices of items were extremely high. Simple items like coffee and water were 300 Lira to 600 Lira 6. There was not enough information source for our gate - which was only announced an hour before flight time. In an airport that is so huge, it takes minimum 1/2 hour to go anywhere. It is very disconcerting to not know your gate till an hour before flight time. We were tired and exhausted after Istanbul airport. The two-wheeled vehicles that the staff zip around in, are a safety hazard. The bathrooms were shockingly dirty. I miss the old airport and this new airport needs a lot of work before it can become warm and welcoming.

Never and nowhere have I paid 15 euro for a beer, or 20 for a simple airport fast food snack. This makes me so angry and sad. You have to actively search for the directions to the gates while this should be obvious at first glance. And what about charging people for a trolley while pretending to be a high-end airport? It seems like a poor  mentality to squeeze the last single lira from people in a vulnerable position.

As other reviewers have commented, the assistance for disabled passengers is horrible. On our way to Egypt ten days ago, we had a decent experience and my wife was able to accompany me in the airport. On the way back home to the U.S., we both got on the golf cart to travel to our gate, but they made my wife get off to make her way through the airport alone as she is not disabled. I refused to abandon my wife in this huge airport where she had no idea where to go, and climbed off the golf cart. The driver of the cart laughed at me and loudly stated that I had declined services. Overall, the airport staff we encountered were rude and dismissive. i have memory issues related to my disability and rely on my wife to help me navigate issues. There were multiple checks of passports and boarding passes. The TSA at the gate was overzealous, the most invasive bag checks and body checks of any airport I have visited. My two diamond nail files in various bags were confiscated, like this 70 year old woman is going to stab someone with a 2.5 inch nail file. Be warned that any item you travel with and that you don't absolutely need on the plane should go in your checked luggage if it could be potentially confiscated. They made me remove my Kindle from its cover to check under the Kindle. My husband was forced to remove his leg brace which they proceeded to remove from his shoe. Initially they wouldn't let him sit down to remove the brace until he explained that he couldn't stand up and remove it. This airport experience was truly awful and humiliating.

Modern airport but no seating areas unless you go into a cafe or bar. Prices are insanely expensive just for basic food (simit) or tea, and coffee is stupidly priced. Toilets were unclean. Duty free prices were much more expensive (30-40%) compared to Manchester airport in the UK. Overall,my experience wasn't good but better than Istanbul's other airport.

Airport security classed silver collar stiffeners as a Knife. Ushered us away when I challenged them. £400 binned. I had passed through Dublin, Tokyo, Osaka & Istanbul (on the way out) with no problem. The inconsistency is a problem. Be warned. Istanbul airport is a beautiful place but terrible customer service. Will avoid in future.

The biggest hazard are the electric bikes whizzing around and the drivers believe that they have right of way and you must get out of the way or be mown down. No alerts like a horn are used, just keep eyes in the back of your head. We transited and having gone through security we made our way to the lounge and then the gate. At the gate, security was ridiculous. You showed passport and boarding pass before entering the queue to enter. Again boarding pass and passport to enter into the departure lounge and immediately after, within two metres, we had to show them again where a jobsworth decided if you could enter or be sent for a bag search and pat down!

The child feeding room at the airport urgently needs a massive makeover. The condition is extremely disappointing and unacceptable for a space meant for families and infants. The wheels of the bassinet are broken, making it unsafe and difficult to use. There is no proper, secure changing table, which is a basic necessity. The couch is filthy, the walls are dirty, and there are bugs everywhere — completely unhygienic for such a sensitive area. This reflects a serious lack of maintenance and care. There is also a serious privacy issue — the door is partially transparent because the blurry covering has peeled off, which makes the space feel exposed and uncomfortable. To make matters worse, the WiFi wasn’t working either, adding to the frustration during an already stressful travel experience. At one point, a bug nearly got onto my baby — I had to act immediately to remove it. This was alarming and completely unacceptable in a facility meant for infant care. Shame on the management for allowing such conditions in an international airport. This facility needs urgent attention and proper upkeep.

I was shocked that there was no potable drinking water available after entering the departure area/gate. Having disposed of my water before security, I was then advised that there was no drinking water airside as the airport water pipes were old. There was no water fountain or filtered tap provision to compensate. Instead had to spend £1:50 for 800ml bottle water.

Our departure experience at Kefalonia Airport yesterday basically ruined a perfect 10 day holiday on the beautiful island. There were so many flights due to depart the airport with only 5 minute intervals between them, but no facilities in which customers could wait after they were processed - hence the queues were basically holding areas. We stood for about 10 minutes outside the main door of departures, we then queued for another hour and 25 minutes for baggage drop. We then waited in line for security to be available for our flights and then again a long queue for Passport Control. (PC itself was extremely quick, probably only 2 minutes max per person) In total 2 hours and 40 minutes without sitting down or daring to leave the various queues to buy a bottle of water or use the facilities.  Surprisingly our flight was only a hour late in taking off and I cannot fault the airport staff, they just had no where for us to wait! In short we will not be returning to Kefalonia again.

Passport control for non-Schengen citizens here is awful. The international layovers are never long enough to make you feel comfortable. That said, they do usually hold the plane for most of the people (not all) coming through that nightmare,  meaning the international flights are almost always delayed leaving Iceland. The airport staff are not helpful (airport staff were just standing nearby staring as my mother was clearly having an issue with her boarding pass after passport control). Icelandair, as a side note, is a truly awful budget airline. You pay for everything except water on a transatlantic flight. The water you also don’t get enough of for how high they keep the heat in their tiny planes. Avoid Iceland Air and Reykjavik for international legs as a non-Schengen traveler for sure.

This is a nice looking airport, but it does not function well. We had a flight from Chicago to Reykjavík and a connecting flight, on the same airline, Icelandair, to Copenhagen. We only had about an hour and a half layover, but Icelandair sold us the ticket, so I’m assuming they figured that we could make the flight. No way. We did not arrive at a gate, but rather out on the tarmac where we needed a bus to get to the terminal. The first bus filled up quickly and we had to wait for the second bus. Then, we had to go through passport control. We waited in the passport control line for more than an hour. This was very frustrating. They have about 60 electronic passport control kiosks. None of them were working. Instead everybody on several flights had to go through passport control by facing off with a passport officer. They took their sweet time. Even though Icelandair knew we had arrived on our initial flight, and knew we were in the passport control line, they did not hold the flight, so we missed the flight. Then we had to spend several hours in this airport.  The personnel at Icelandair have become frustrated with passport control as well. Avoid this airport if you can.

Nice small airport, playing as the gateway for entering and exiting Iceland, with many working stations, restaurants and shoppings. The airport is generally clean, and easy to navigate. However, boarding was messy as flights' queuing line cut each others, and staff checked passengers' passports thousands times. On the another side note, I appreciated how staff tried to help passengers to go through immigration and passport control as fast as possible in early morning when connecting passengers were flooding the floor.

Looks nice, but a disaster of an airport. Had a 5 hour layover thanks to Icelandair changing our reservations. They seemed to have 1 terminal open and everyone was jammed into there. We found seats a but were quickly bombarded by masses of people, none of whom found seating. And here we are waiting 5 hours for 6 hours flight with nothing to eat. This was a connecting flight so we had already been traveling for 6 hours when we got there. They close the food courts at 5 pm even with many departing flights still scheduled, stranding you with nothing for hours. Do better if you want tourism!

Is Iceland the only country in the world with no public transportation connecting its international airport? Most Icelanders I’ve met admit that public transportation is a source of national embarrassment, yet there appears to be no plan to address it. The only way to reach the international airport without a private car is through a single bus service which is overpriced. It is a basic, often overcrowded bus that departs from the main bus station. They technically offer pick-ups, but these cost extra and still require a change at the main bus station, making it nothing like the seamless bus, train, or metro connections you’d expect in any Nordic capital. The result is a stark choice between an expensive private car or taxi, and an uncomfortable, inconvenient, and wheelchair-inaccessible bus service

Outstanding support and professionalism at Kigali International Airport During the recent widespread flight disruptions across Europe — particularly through Amsterdam due to severe weather — our family was rerouted via Kigali. Because of knock-on delays on the Amsterdam side, our transfer time became extremely tight and we were at real risk of missing our onward flight to South Africa. What followed was nothing short of exceptional. The operations team at Kigali Airport, in particular Innocent and Walter, went above and beyond anything we could have expected. They proactively located our family on arrival, personally guided them through all required security and transfer checks, and ensured they were escorted swiftly and calmly to the correct departure gate — all just in the nick of time. Their professionalism, kindness, urgency, and genuine care turned what could have been an incredibly stressful experience into one that felt safe, organised, and reassuring. It is rare to encounter such dedication and human-focused service in the middle of complex operational challenges. Innocent and Walter are a true credit to Kigali Airport. We are deeply grateful for their support and will always remember the extraordinary assistance we received. Thank you for setting such a high standard of airport operations and customer care.
Close to city, short train ride between airport and downtown, fast security check. Totally overcrowded, poor shopping, lack of seating, lack of eateries

No clear signage to security, lack of seating but one of the worst things was the queues. On arrival at border passport control it was 45 minutes and the 50 minutes on departure! People missing flights and rude unhelpful staff. The next major issue was the gate staff representative for Ryanair, I don't think I have every been treated with such aggression and rudeness.

On 13 February 2026, I flew from London to Krakow. Upon arrival, we were directed to passport control, where we faced the longest queue I have ever seen at any airport. We had to wait for more than four hours. There was no communication from the airport staff - no explanation of what was happening, no information about the expected waiting time, and no visible effort to manage the situation properly. The conditions were stressful and exhausting. Because of this unacceptable delay, I missed my connecting train to Ukraine. No one apologized or offered any assistance. The entire experience felt completely non–customer-oriented.

It has been a very bad experience from several points of view. The airport is obviously not ready for such high volume of travelers. Had to wait more than 45 minutes to collect my luggage. All areas both at luggage collection point as well as at the gates had very limited number of seats. Worst part was at the security check. The hand luggage of my son has been stopped and the security person claimed that a toy was a prohibited item. I have asked her several times why it was prohibited, but she just kept saying the same thing: it is a prohibited item. At some point, I have shown her the list of all not allowed items on a Ryanair flight (the company we where travelling with) to prove that the specific toy (or similar) was not in the list. Despite of this, she kept saying that the item was not allowed and that the only way for us to bring it was to go out and check in the luggage. At the end, I had to give up and through the toy. I have full respect for the airport staff and appreciate the importance of them being strict, but this does not mean that they can do whatever they want or basically invent rules.

Kuwait International Airport is weird.  The entry experience is not very smooth, with a bunch of overcrowding at the entrance. The walk all the way to the check in desks is okay, it's spacious so not much going on. Always had an issue with check-in for some reason. Airside is okay besides the expensive duty free. They handle queues In a way that's terrible. They make you line up at the gate to sit and wait for the plane, sometimes these queues getting so long they clash into other gates. Boarding is okay and overall arrival experience.

We had a particularly difficult journey departing from Lahore last November 2025. Every time you go there they change the rules, this time you could not get in without showing a printed ticket, they would not accept an email confirming the ticket but luckily I had copies of our tickets printed out. I would recommend taking everything as a paper copy including copies of all travel documents like passports, visa etc. Outside we could not find any wheelchairs and when we asked they said the airline would have to give us one and of course they were inside. When we finally got inside it took the airline 20 minutes to find a wheelchair. The check in desk said they could not find our booking even though we had booked months before and we had printouts of all our paperwork.  I am used to the staff at Lahore trying to con people into bribing them to get checked in but this was the worst time I have ever seen. Sadly I will have to fly there again as we have family there and the other airports in Pakistan are no different. Its sad to see how hard it is to visit, how can anywhere prosper if you cant do something so normal as check in for a flight.

Quite an old and airport with OK signage, however a lack of seating and charging points. The WiFi worked Ok making it easy to connect and the speed was reasonable. Restaurant prices were quite fair for an airport location.

I genuinely would avoid Lanzarote. Ive been coming for years. The airport is terrible. Im still in the queue and its been 3 hours. So disorganised. No staff to say what is happening... something to do with a new system....

Absolute joke of an airport. 2 hours to clear customs with passports being checked 3 times. Bus transfers further delayed due to queues in passport control and taxi queue ridiculous outside the terminal.

This airport is a total disaster. They are under construction so go figure. There is a lot of traffic due to the exterior color metrication. The TSA pre-check was fast. Once in the terminal there are a few restaurants and a couple of stores. Food and beverage prices are a little high, your typical airport prices. The airport crew can be a little nasty and not helpful. They didn't allow me to start inside the terminal as my flights kept on being canceled and got stranded there for 3 days. The construction means that some areas are closed, and everything feels right.

This airport is a total disaster. They are under construction so go figure. There is a lot of traffic due to the exterior color metrication. The TSA pre-check was fast. Once in the terminal there are a few restaurants and a couple of stores. Food and beverage prices are a little high, your typical airport prices. The airport crew can be a little nasty and not helpful. They didn't allow me to start inside the terminal as my flights kept on being canceled and got stranded there for 3 days. The construction means that some areas are closed, and everything feels right.

The security process is an embarrassment only one security screening line open and 6 flights checking in. It is a 30 minute plus exercise at one of Australia’s small regional airports. No aero bridges here. The only airline that has anything resembling a lounge is Qantas but it isn’t manned has inadequate seating and nothing of any substance to eat.

My experience at Las Vegas Airport security was extremely concerning and left me feeling unsafe and disrespected. While traveling as an active-duty military family, my husband and I were subjected to additional screening after leaving the USO and re-entering the security area for our delayed connecting flight. It was around midnight, and we had remained inside the airport the entire time. We had even spoken with airport personnel and law enforcement officers to locate the USO. During the screening process, multiple TSA agents approached us and referenced concerns about explosives, yet very little information was provided about what was happening or why. I was holding my service dog, answering every question asked, complying with every instruction given, and fully cooperating throughout the process. Despite this, the situation continued to escalate. What disturbed me most was the lack of communication. Agents attempted to separate my husband and me and discussed taking us into separate rooms without clearly explaining the reason. We repeatedly tried to provide information about our movements within the airport, but it felt as though our explanations were being ignored. After extensive searches and questioning, nothing was found. Only then were we given an explanation, which did not align with the facts we had already provided. The entire interaction left me feeling targeted, intimidated, and fearful. As someone already dealing with significant personal stress—including the recent loss of my father, a cross-country move, and travel to attend my daughter’s graduation—the experience was overwhelming. I fully support airport security and understand the importance of safety procedures. However, travelers deserve clear communication, professionalism, and respectful treatment. What should have been a routine screening became an unnecessarily stressful and frightening experience due to the manner in which it was handled. I hope airport leadership reviews these procedures and emphasizes better communication and de-escalation practices when travelers are selected for additional screening.

United, Terminal 3, flying in from SFO and out to ORD. The airport is probably fine for most purposes, but it's hard to figure out why it's built to be so spread out: The designers did not seem to prioritize passenger-friendly spatial design. When you arrive, you have to take an airport train to baggage claim; when I got to the carousels, I learned that mine was something like the 12th carousel from the entrance, and it's a surprisingly long walk: The 20-30 carousels are all arranged in a line, as if to maximize required walking distance. Then, to pick up a car rental, you have to take a bus to the Rental Car Center, which is miles away. Our bus seemed to drop us as far from the entrance to that large building as it possibly could. (And for a couple rental car companies, you then have to take a second bus!) If you have heavy luggage, small children, mobility limitations, or jet lag, the airport can be an exhausting place to arrive.

Immigration at arrivals was chaos. Long queues and not enough staff. Passport machine readers either don't work or take too long to process information. Over zealous security staff at departures might as well ask passengers to strip naked. Food outlets in departures are all overpriced. I suggest taking your own snacks and an empty plastic bottle. There's a free water dispenser hidden in the terminal. Ask staff where to find it. Toilets are too small and passengers were queuing to use them.

I've never had major complaints about Larnaca airport. It is quite compact and decently organized. I also understand that low-cost airlines like to minimize the airport fees they pay for parking bays, aerobridges, etc. Lately, however, I have on several occasions experienced boarding whereby from the gate, passengers are herded into a humid, sweaty, unventilated tunnel or stairwell, and then kept there standing - in the almost unbreatheable air - for 30-40 minutes. In addition some of the younger staff have no qualms about playing with their phone while speaking with passengers and avoiding all eye contact.

The main airport of Cyprus, well accessible by car and buses. It's of a modern design, efficient and has a large amount of duty-free stores. Border control in 2026 requires document scanning, print a slip and have it manually checked. Service provided by the staff varies a lot, but grumpiness is quite common.
Nice, small, easily manageable airport. Plenty of food options. Acceptably clean. The WiFi, however, is almost worthless. The connection is very unstable.
Super little airport. My 92 year old mother was helped by a charming young lady at the airport who has just started work there, she was at the check-in but helped my mother in a wheelchair.

Certainly the worst airport I have ever encountered. While building work goes on people waiting to meet international arrivals must wait outside (and it was zero degrees and snowing at 9.30 am on 11 January 2026). "Welcome to the fourth world" I said to our visitor. How can any "manager" not make temporary internal arrangements? Oh, and I am still waiting for a response about a £36 car park booking the day before. I paid £2 extra to make it cancellable but the website does not permit this, though it says it does.

Flew to ZRH in LX Business Class. Prices at the outdoor café were very expensive for Slovenia. An espresso cost over 4 EUR. The food selection didn’t look appealing, but the prices were steep.
