The security check was efficient and quick. The food in the business lounge was unappetizing—greasy instead of light and high-quality. On the lounge terrace, 8 tables sat with used dishes for over 30 minutes, which the staff did not clear away. The strong wind blew napkins out onto the tarmac. The flight was delayed. No boarding information on the gate screen, nor any announcements. During boarding, there was an incomprehensible announcement. There was also no separate line for Business Class passengers. Seating was limited, and the gate area was dark because the lights weren’t turned on. All in all, typical LJU Airport. Instead of small and cozy, just below average.

This is an airport run by typical bureucrats: their only purpose in life is to oppress with massive amounts of paperwork; serving the public is not part of their training. I'm talking about the transfer fee rubbish, not included in ticket prices. And then they don't even provide a fiscal receipt in the email, online forms don't work (if they even give a fiscal receipt or just a new copy of the QR that doesn't even indicate the price), so you have to beg for one through complaint forms. Let's see how much paperwork I still need to provide to get on. And after payment, there's not even water fountain.

Apart from bad logistics the habit of letting one know the gate 1 hour before departure causes stress as the nominal gate closing for most of the flights (all those operated by TAP for example) is 50 mins before departure … and one finds oneself having to run for no real reason. This associated to the bad signage and the elongated structure which forces km of walk without any moving walkway makes it one of the worst airports I have known
A terrible airport. Check in given as 3 hours before the flight. Toilets inadequate and the whole place us dirty and in a state of disrepair. I will never use this Airport again.

This has to be the worst airport in Europe. Over two hours to get through passport control. The EES system makes no difference as you still have to queue to get through passport control, which restricts numbers and treats non-Schengen area citizens as scum they have to deal with. The staff are ambivalent and not identifiable by e.g. high visibility jackets, and then don’t help or give you any information that’s useful. Once you get through the ridiculous queuing, you have a 15 minute walk through the whole airport terminal to try and find your luggage, which as you arrived so long ago, is not even listed on the airport screens. Having recently been through Valencia airport two weeks ago, this is a joy compared with the chaos that is Lisbon airport. I will never fly into this dreadful city airport again.

Absolutely horrible immigration experience. It took over two hours both on arrival and departure. For departure in particular, the staff showed a complete lack of professionalism and service mindset. The queue was extremely long and poorly managed, putting passengers at serious risk of missing their flights—even after arriving at the airport three hours in advance. This is far below acceptable international standards and easily one of the worst airport experiences I’ve ever had.
The worst airport I've ever been too! 2hrs to get through security/passport control. Hot/sweaty airport with horrible staff. Avoid airport Taxis that will charge you X3 times the correct price.

Utter disgrace. Unorganised. Staff are rude and don’t care. Waited 1 hr and 20 minutes at passport control. Only one kiosk open. No staff available to help. Passengers started queue hopping and pushing through. When I politely asked a staff member why the queue was so bad he replied that ‘it wasn’t bad, we were all late.’ After I’d been stood there for well over an hour! When I asked who I could complain to he said ‘why are you still talking’ So much for being encouraged to visit Lisbon. Never ever again.
Incredibly bad. 2 hour queue to exit passport control. No idea what on earth is going wrong, but easily my worst airport experience.

I came 2 hours early at 7:00 to try and be prepared, security and baggage drop went fine but the passport line took multiple hours. Horribly organized and under staffed (5 staff members split between EU and non-EU lanes), people tried rushing under the queue markers multiple times. The only thing stopping them from running through the doors were other passengers waiting in line who were also late and didn’t want the whole line in front of them. They pushed upwards of 3,000 people through ten automatic passport checks. I didn’t even make it to the terminal and I wasn’t the only one. I overheard the majority of people saying they also missed their flight because of how long the line was. The entire security check point had people on their phones trying to find and call their airlines customer service to reschedule or refund their tickets. I would recommend avoiding this airport if possible and if you truly can’t fly anywhere else, come at least 4 hours early or at odd hours.

I got to the airport two hours before departure got lunch and left one and a half hours for passport control.Started queuing and waited for that full one and a half hours for passport control and more missed my flight because apparently the airport decided to put one person at work as a whole group of other police staying behind passport control talking and laughing. So now I have waited for around two hours still person working and I have to buy another plane ticket just so I can go back home on a brand new flight wasting a ton of money. If you ever want to come rethink before you do it (go to anywhere in Europe other than Portugal such as France or Spain)

The airport is chaotic, nothing works, the seating is filthy especially outsude S22. The TAP Premium Tejo Lounge is unbelievably shabby and serves poor quality food. I’ll never fly from Lisbon Airport again.

At Lisbon Airport, I was instructed to use the automated electronic passport gates (eGates), as the system indicated that my passport was eligible for electronic clearance. I queued accordingly. After waiting in line, the eGate machines repeatedly failed to recognize my passport. Multiple passengers holding the same type of passport experienced identical failures at the same time, indicating a systemic malfunction of the airport’s immigration system rather than an individual document issue. Airport staff then explicitly instructed affected passengers, including myself, to leave the eGate area and re-queue at the manual immigration counters. By that time, the manual control lanes had developed extremely long queues. As a result, I was required to queue again from the beginning at manual immigration under the direction of airport staff.

This airport is miserable hardly anything is open. at night, it's not very warm and it's quite run down. A beautiful city as this should really do a lot better than this, it's a disgrace. They are currently doing renovations but I doubt that it will make much difference. They really do need comfortable seating but I assume they keep these cold metal seats to deter the homeless. There are security guards at the doors, it's very depressing.

This airport should not be allowed as much traffic as they have. Airport is too far beyond capacity. Seating area always packed with passengers occupying floor path. Too many shops they should be converted to provide better support to people. Only 2 minuscule lounges also always packed and with waiting queue. Horrendous experience
Most chaotic, unprofessional airport I have ever been. No ways of proper doing, no responsibility, no order, no procedurę. Nothing. They are the best in destroying plans of passengers.
Avoid flying into Lisbon Airport. If you have to then allow at least 4 hours to get through immigration. The place is a shambles  It would be easier to fly into Porto and get the train down.

Worst airport in Europe. Almost missed our flight because the queue to go through immigration was several hours long. (Because the electronic passport reader wasn't working and told me I had to go to the immigration queue) So I walked to try to get put through as I would miss my flight.  Some airports will actually call for you to come forward if your plane is about to leave, but not in Lisbon. They hate customers. When I managed to sneak through I had to run with my wife to the gate but she had a severe asthma attack and couldn't run. Also the signage is almost non-existent so you have to constantly ask people for directions. You need to allow about half a day to get through Lisbon airport.

Immigration area was so packed that we had to wait 20 minutes forever at all being allowed to access the lines. I have digital passport and decided to go for that line (digital immigration), after one hour in that line my passport was refused, the counter tried several times and gave up, the he put me all the way at the back of the line for the manual line, another 2h was burned off, and I lost that flight. I was rebooked to a later flight, which by the way was postponed another 2h - total airport time extended from 2h to 9h. And at the gate, when asking if the luggage was on this flight, the answer was no, it is not - wow! My last time at this extremely chaotic airport. I’ve been using this hub over 15 years, it’s getting worse and worse and now it’s horrible!

I am currently sitting on my plane, which is delayed because we are missing 30% of the passengers. ​There were hundreds of people waiting in a line for over two hours at passport control. This chaos was caused by having only three border control officers working the booths, despite having five flights scheduled to depart at the same time. ​It is a shame because I love Lisbon and Portugal—it is a beautiful country with so much to offer visitors but the airport organization needs serious improvement.

Such a beautiful city and country — but what a horrendous airport. First of all, it is very outdated and in desperate need of renovation. The airport feels stuck in the 90s. Lines are chaotic, and employees keep sending passengers from one line to another. Do yourself a favor and get the online visa, or you may end up standing in three different lines. The immigration system was down, leaving travelers confused and frustrated. The staff appeared grumpy and exhausted. Upon arrival, you’re immediately approached by taxi and SIM card sellers who aggressively try to get your attention. I would definitely avoid this airport if possible — such a shame for such a beautiful city.

No electrical outlets, no phone charger stations. At Terminal 2 there are 26 spots to board. with power charger outlets. There is 1  located in 23A with 8 cell phone charger outlets, which will always be completely full because there are at least 2,000 people in this area, probably 3,000. Avoid at all costs. And the food outlets have extreme pricing.

We arrived from SFO at night and had to disembark onto a bumpy ramp only to be sent to board a bus to get to the baggage gate. Then we had to search how to find a taxi or Uber only to wait for what seemed forever to get on a bus far away to be delivered to a place to wait for a taxi with a driver who not only ripped us off but drove dangerously on the freeway. Today we came to fly back to Philadelphia and after passing through check-in, baggage, and security (no problem) found ourselves in a newly remodeled area with only a Starbucks and a Sammy’s Pizza where the loud heavy metal stick-needles-in-yours music assaulted our ears as we ate a $30 10” pizza. Not any other acceptable items on the menu here at Gate 42A with a total of maybe 25 seats for passengers. Remember this is a recently remodeled area. You’d think LA could do better

Terminal 7 is a wide and brightly lit concourse. Very busy airport even at midnight. Signage from gate to baggage claim and ground transport is very good. Vehicular traffic even at midnight is a nightmare. It took the rental car shuttle 10-15 minutes to clear the terminal. If I had a choice between the many Los Angeles area airports, LAX would not be my first choice.

I arrived at the airport at 10:30 am for a 1:15 pm flight. After taking the train to Terminal 4S I got off the train to find myself in a mass of people trying to get through passport control. There was no managed line, only a huge crowd. All were trying to get to an escalator to the next floor. Upon finally reaching the next floor I came to another snaking line which ended in another room with yet more crowds and barely any semblance of a line. Police were present to control the crowd, which should suggest the degree of mayhem present. By 1:20 PM I had cleared passport control, but still had a very, very long walk (run, actually) to the gate. Fortunately, the flight was delayed because so many passengers were held up and late. The flight left an hour and half late (but I was on it - Thank you American Airlines). Because the flight was late I had to reschedule my connecting flight in the United States (for which there should have been ample time to make the connection but for the delay). I won’t be back to Madrid.

The airport is beautifully designed. Check in was done by lovely Iberia representatives. Security was well organized and smooth. The prices for food and drink are expensive, but the staff who were working were lovely. It is a shame that Madrid airport charges outrageous prices for everything - even in the Duty Free.

Arrival traffic and departure traffic are on one approach so car and bus bottle neck-make getting there on time difficult. There is no signage within the arrival area to tell you which way your airline desk is. You have to hope you are walking the right direction and if not, you have to turn around. All the sliding doors from the drop off area into terminal 1 were locked except for one and there was 1 security guy asking everyone to show their id etc before you even enter the building. The delay at the security line was very very long and the indifference to our tight take off time was disgusting. We asked for help many times and they shrugged and said so what? At one point the equipment to scan the carryons stopped and we were all at a stand still. Information from employees to update everyone was yelled out in Spanish as the worker walked away. Workers hardly even would talk to us. I couldn't believe this is even an international airport. They were so unorganized and seemed to not care about travelers. I will never fly here again.

Dropped off my wife at usual drop off/pick up point at 5.30AM on 20/4, only to be charged £15 for a 60 second stop. Whoever thought this was a reasonable and respectful way to treat patrons should hang their head in shame and retreat to whatever hole they emerged from. Truly shocking.

I have arrived at Luton Airport many times, always travelling with small children, and it is consistently a very difficult experience. Walking through the extremely long corridors to passport control and baggage claim with children and hand luggage feels exhausting and unnecessary. Luton is the only airport where, for some reason, baby push-chairs are not returned at the aircraft door. As a result, parents are forced to carry children for a long distance. To add to this, the airport’s assistance push-chairs which are supposed to be available along the way, are never there actually. Travelling with children here feels poorly thought out and not family-friendly at all. I really hope the airport considers improving support for families, especially those arriving with young children.
Lyon airport: poor service everywhere, including security. The overall experience was disappointing from start to finish. I do not recommend this airport.

Lyon airport (Aka St Exupery, aka Satolas) has great architecture. But that’s all! It's poor in all passenger areas. The worst is the Border Control. Having a Permanent Residence card I should be able to use the EU gates as in Geneva & other European airport. But not in Lyon airport so I joined the line of about 200 passengers waiting to be approved by a single agent. There are about 6 gates but only one was open. The sad line included children, babes-in-arms, elderly folk. No seating , no ventilation (oh yes there was an overhead fan, not working!). I know France well and this typifies much of the French bureaucratic attitude.

I wanted to say thank you to all those involved with Lost Property at Malta Airport. When I originally submitted my lost property form, I did so  not thinking anything would come of it. So I was amazed when they advised me that it had been found and still with my dollars cash inside - so also a big thank you to the person who handed it in.  I have worked in travel and tourism since 1989 - as an Adventure Tour Guide for 10 years and as a Tour Manager for 10 years - so have dealt with lots of my own clients with their lost property. Once again thank you to all those involved.

Be careful! If you forget something at the airport they will charge you 25€ to pick it up. Even if it's kids items. They want to make money off children forgetting their rucksack. Terrible customer service from  the manager at lost and found. So disappointed. I had to pay 10£ for parking as well!

Filthy, everything apart from the eating tables is nasty, Very stressful, very poorly organised and signed. A single lane arrival so all passengers are crammed into a queue. Prepare to wait ages because everything is also broken. Smoking areas very poorly defined, a no smoking sign was on the cigarette bin. Toilet doors broken, staff seem stressed out. All in all an awful experience.

My flight was late in the evening around 22:00, and I arrived very early so I can finish my custom procedure for tax free-refund only to find out that there is no custom office at all at the airport. There is some Forex office but only open until l15:00. No machine or scanner instead of stamp-nothing! That was money straight out of my pocket! The toilet facilities for women was closed-no explanation. On security control you have to get all liquids and gels out - even your lipstick.  We came to passport control an hour and a half before our flight- they told us to come later. When? They would't say. So, all in all - I'm never flying through Malmo again!

Absolutely awful airport. No organisation at all once through passport control on departure. Awful restaurants options. Dirty and unhygienic. No option to refill water other than begging staff at restaurants. Avoid at all costs.

Terminal 2 is by far the worst airport I have ever been in. The departure area is too small with only one small eating area. There are not enough seats and if there is any air conditioning they choose to not use it. Once you check in and pass security you are corralled into an area that is too small for the amount of people they have checked into fly. There is an overpriced airport shop, and I mean overpriced by a lot and a couple of eating spaces. Again the entire area does not have adequate seating and no air-conditioning. There is no smoking area in terminal 2 and no access to terminal 1 to use the multiple smoking areas. When the time comes to go to your gate for boarding, be aware that the boarding is done before you enter a tiny room, again with not enough seats to accommodate all the people on a flight and no access to toilets..so once there you are stuck. This airport is worse then some airports I have passed through in what would be considered third world countries.This terminal has been designated low cost airlines only so they believe you can be treated as cattle.

I fly to Marseille 5 times a year to visit family. I hoped that providing fingerprints and photos in December would ease arrival using EES. I tried the express passport entry lane . On scanning my passport it was declined and I had to join the queue for clearance. Was half term holidays in France andUK, queue had many families & children who cant use egates. Only one booth open for the whole incoming flight from Stansted London. Every everyone behind had to wait 45 minutes for another officer to take over. Luckily our baggage was still circling the reclaim area an hour after landing . The worst experience I have ever encountered, unfortunately the only route I can use to visit my family.

Easter Island Airport (Rapa Nui or Mataveri Airport) is a tiny airport with a huge runway. After landing the aircraft turns at the end of the runway back to the small single storey terminal building stopping on the apron. Steps are brought up to the aircraft and you walk across the tarmac to the terminal building, down a covered corridor, serenaded by local musicians, passed what can be passport control if you are on an international flight and a single baggage belt. Before leaving all bags hand/hold are X-rayed and then you are on the arrivals ramp greeted by what seems like half the island. It seems chaotic but works fine for this small island. Departures is similar, no automatic check-in, you queue at the counter and have your details checked and a formal Boarding Pass is issued. A short queue passing through a passport and Island authorisation check, then hand luggage security - water bottles are OK. The Departures is a large area open on one side facing the runway via a low walled garden occupied by various hens clucking about. You can watch the aircraft being serviced. There is a small coffee stand and a couple of small kiosks selling souvenirs and similar things. All very relaxed. The flight is called by boarding group and you walk down the covered walkway across the apron and up the stairs to the aircraft. Currently there are only domestic flights from Santiago to Easter Island, 2 flights a day in the summer and about 4 flights a week in the winter,.

I traveled through Terminal 3 in January 2026 and had an appalling experience with security that nearly caused my family to miss our flight. My bag was flagged because it contained a 100ml skincare spray bottle without a lid - within regulations and inside a plastic bag as required. Instead of a quick check, my bag disappeared into secondary security for 10-15 minutes with no communication.  When I asked security staff repeatedly for updates, I was told to “calm down” and “just wait”. The spray bottle was eventually verified and returned to me, but the process was unnecessarily slow, poorly communicated.  Terminal 3 security is rigid and understaffed.
Delayed flight due to congestion around Heathrow. Food and drink quite expensive in T2.
Worst transit place ever! We were blocked at Terminal 5 with no way to get out having a useless 20€ ETA Visa application. No smoking area, no outdoor area. It’s a shame.
One of the worst airports in the world. A complete mess, Filipinos are naturally friendly and welcoming, they, and the entire world visiting your country, deserve a better airport.

I have travelled to many airports and never experienced such chaotic experience such as the security check in to immigration. No seating areas. Having to queue up to go into the toilet and they call this an international airport. There is only selective Lounge access or options available. Davao airport is much cleaner and much more organised

No clear signage to find your way around. Ridiculous that you have to drag your cases on a bus from one terminal to another. Pathetic internet services in all areas. Internet check in for overseas visitors is convoluted, and makes no sense. I had a couple in front of me that took at least 30 minutes to make sense of the menus. This is ridiculous given that English is taught in school in the Philippines. Over zealous security staff. (Had to go through 7 separate security checks?!  Other staff would rather bury themselves in their cell phones than help. Hundreds of meters of waling just to get to a bus from one terminal to another! Eateries that close before midnight. If you really have to go to the Philippines, try your best to avoid passing through Manila if you can.

Terminal 1 at Ninoy Aquino International Airport fails at basic capacity management. Immigration lacked clear signage despite overwhelming passenger volumes. When concerns were raised, staff responses were cold, intimidating, and mocking. Arrival and shuttle areas were chaotic and congested.

Arrived at NAIA Terminal 3 thinking I had enough buffer time—only to be swallowed by chaos. Immigration piled up. X-ray security with poorly managed merging lines that went nowhere. No airline staff. No last-call announcement. No escort—just all of us stuck at security while boarding quietly closed. We ran. Still missed the flight—along with about 20 other passengers. Our bags were already on the plane, yet no one questioned why none of us showed up. The response was effortless: ‘Just catch the next flight.’ A seven-hour wait, no accountability. Defeated by a system that failed its passengers.

Travelling back yesterday and all ladies and gents toilets have no toilet paper. The Duty free cashiers are rude and pushed my partner out the way. Then after waiting in a cramped area waiting for a delayed flight we were singled out in front of the entire area for a random frisk and drug tests. I was so angry I’ve never been to an airport in the world that was so unhygienic, unhelpful and just awful, it finished a great break in the most horrid way . No power points plugged in so don’t look to charge your phone.

I was surprised by Melbourne Airport's service and facilities. Upon arrival, the security checkpoint lacked enough scanners, leading to a long queue. One of the scanners malfunctioned, requiring me to seek assistance from an officer, which is understandable. However, the baggage claim process was excessively slow, and the conveyor belt was dirty. At departure, I experienced an issue with the security staff. I usually travel with my cameras and accessories, but this time they refused to let me pass with my glass ball, insisting I needed to check in my luggage, which is already checked in. I have traveled for years with this glass ball, and today in Melbourne, I had to discard it because of the safety rules that apparently didn't exist a few months ago. The staff is new and was not particularly friendly, simply saying, "It is what it is."

What a poor experience it is to arrive in Australia after traveling throughout many great airports around the world and have to deal with the below par arrival at Melbourne Tullamarine. As usual, the e-scan passport system that greets arrivals was a shambles. From scanners not working (I've never not experienced a faulty non-working scanner) and the insufficient number of e-passport readers. Once again I chose to go to the human passport control, which was far quicker that having to wait for the e- option. Then, walking through the terminal to baggage claim, I waited 45 minutes from landing until the baggage came through the carousel. That is an unacceptably long time to wait for luggage, and is the longest wait I have experienced throughout visiting over 9 airports in the past 12 months. The state of the carousel was also a disappointment. It was dirty, covered in paper, tags etc and I felt ashamed that this was how Melbourne presents itself to the world. First impressions count!!. Finally, the pickup area was an abomination. There were no officials directing traffic in what could only described as chaos. I've seen more organised traffic flow in some 3rd world countries than what Melbourne Airport dished up.

Management of manpower to handle bags when several planes arrive close together needs great help. They obviously do not plan sufficient manpower as I had to wait an hour from departing plane to having luggage and moving toward my car. They even apologized as so many planes landed at the Same time causing delays on handling. I have many decades of flying and would put their baggage handling in the “F” grade category. This long delay has been repeated many times flying into MSP.  New baggage management would be a wonderful solution.

I have found transferring from an internal to an international flight at Linate confusing and messy. There are no clear indications about transfers on arrival, and you have to go through generic security. Inside the terminal, seating areas are limited (but shopping areas are available in abundance), and departing to a non-Schengen area is also very messy, as though the gate may be announced, border posts are closed until border guards feel like opening, which could be a long wait. I will gladly avoid this airport for a future transit.

By far the worst airport; there is no transit zone you have to do queue for security check again. The airport looks old, quite limited food options, but the worst part is that there are not enough areas for you to wait comfortably for your flight. There are lots of shops with no customers but people are crowded in small unpleasant areas before boarding. One lounge zone which is way too small and needs refresh. You can tell they only care about getting rent money from shops and not about the passengers.

Being a UK passport holder, I was worried about the reports of lengthy queues. We arrived on a Saturday afternoon and passed through the self-scanners easily. There must be 25 machines. Leaving on Wednesday afternoon was just as easy, we cleared security and passport control in less than 15 minutes. Airtime facilities aren't as good but that's the same everywhere. Yes, I would travel here again. Transport links are very very good to.

Arrived on Jan the 6th, possibly the busiest day of the month, being the end of Christmas vacations. The negative side was that we parked at remote stand and had to disembark by stairs and use bus. After that everything was good. Passport control had a queue, but with all postions were open and it took less than 15 minutes. We came to the delivery area and our luagage were already delivered

A vast, modern airport with strong design potential, but very poorly staffed. Disorganized, long queues and unhelpful, non-English-speaking workers contribute to a frustrating passenger experience. Both official and unofficial worker strikes can disrupt operations without warning, causing sudden bottlenecks and delays. Queues are poorly managed, leading to chaos and frequent line-cutting. After a long flight, we waited over three hours to reach passport control and collect our luggage. There are no special provisions for families with children or mothers with babies, creating unnecessary stress and distress. Overall, the airport has significant potential, but the workforce and operational management seriously undermine the experience.

I didn’t love when Air Canada designed a connection with 30 minutes between arrival and boarding between two international legs but was told over phone and again at gate it should be ok. Plane came in 10 minutes late then jockeying the snowy runway for another 5 and de boarding. tobaggoning with the kids was not on my tabingo card. Now to the customs and connections, which I see an arrow and sign, let me follow it, and then another arrow and sign, let me follow that, too. I am spectacular at following directions so this rules! Now I’m on an escalator going up thanks to a sign. Let me do that, then another escalator with a sign going up, let me do that, then another escalator with a sign going up let me do that. Of course, I’ve got three children with me on this expedition sumitting Everest. We get to the top and four paces later another opportunity for us to do the boarding passes in a second gate machine.  Made the flight at last call. It’s very understandable to have customs and connections and everyone can understand that could be tedious, but it’s necessary. If you have 15 signs and four escalators and twist and turns- is it possible for somewhere on those signs for a time reveal?   It’s possible the airline can prepare you that better. I saw the sign for my gate after we went through the 15 minute walk, but there were restaurants and shops before we got there.

The process for non-US transit passengers is particularly appalling. It's hard to understand why we have to go through carry-on baggage checks again, given that they've already been done at the departure airport, but this happens everywhere else too. The problem is that there's only one x-ray machine, which is slow, outdated, and completely inadequate. The staff can't manage the line, repeatedly checking our boarding passes, and it took us over an hour to get through the barrier, so we had to hurry to avoid missing our next flight. In fact, all flights were delayed, ours by over an hour. And we'd already had to wait over 30 minutes for the previous flight to reach the gate. Finally, the WiFi system doesn't support my phone.

Beware this airport. We arrived at Manchester airport from a long haul holiday to Australia and New Zealand. The airports at Sydney, Auckland and Singapore had excellent facilities to change terminals using buses, trains and even monorail. We needed to change terminals for our final leg back to Spain to find that at Manchester Airport you are expected to walk. Following a 12 hour flight and being in our seventies this was not ideal. So we paid £17.80 for a taxi to drop in the wrong place. Is this the second class facilities you should expect from a first class airport like Manchester? Their complaint site is also not working I wonder why?

£1.3bn spent on new T2 and yet Domestic Arrivals is far, far worse than ever it was at either T1 or T3! Clearly no account was taken of any arrivals from within the Common Travel Area. You land and taxi for 10+ minutes from the end of the runway to the most distant gates on T2, get off the plane via an airbridge and then have to walk down stairs, onto the tarmac to climb onto a bus. This takes 10-15 minutes to tour the airport to a small back entrance marked UK Arrivals. You walk along what was a service corridor (not designed too be used by passengers) to the single baggage reclaim belt and then an exit into T2 arrivals following a similar service corridor. The whole point for a domestic arrival is that is should be quick and easy. Arriving at Manchester Airport on a domestic flight is neither quick or easy taking 25+ minutes from the end of the runway to the arrivals hall! I would give it ZERO out of 10 if the system allowed it.

Terrible design no thought given to those with mobility issues. Arrived on a short flight from the Isle of Man, both my wife and I have mobility issues, my wife on crutches and myself using a walking stick, we had arranged for help on arrival but did not realise how far the walk was from the aircraft to baggage reclaim and had only ordered one wheelchair assist. Luckily we managed to find another wheelchair and one of our friends did the pushing, had we not done so there would have been no way that we could have made the journey from the aircraft, no moving walkways, nothing at all to help those with mobility issues. It took us nearly an hour to reach the arrivals hall, we only had carry on baggage and on an internal flight so would have expected to breeze through but we were held up with the facial scanning, why are we scanned both getting on and off the plane and again at border control? Ridiculous another hour spent trying to find our lift and exit the car park. Two hours in total from exiting the plane to leaving the airport in car, and it was a quiet period. Absolutely terrible, we will be flying from Liverpool in the future

All traffic moved to T2 before sufficient facilities available. Followed big signs from drop off for list, got to correct floor to find there was no way into the terminal. Toilets already showing wear and dirt. No room in lounge unless pre booked as insufficient capacity (travelling at a not busy time). Corridors to gates look like a long portacabin inside - why not make them glass and nice walkways in a brand new terminal? Same on arrival walk ways with no windows or travelaties at all. All looks and feels cheap. On arrival, usual very very slow baggage, 90 mins after landing for bags to arrive, and no customer service staff or announcements to find out when it would be available. Plenty of airport staff in immigration, why not have someone controlling the experience in baggage and helping customers, and kicking the subcontracted baggage handlers over their always slow service ? Manchester's main problem has mot been the facilities, but the staffing issues and total disregard for any level of customer service across the whole operation. Until they sort this, it would continue to be a miserable experience for customers.

Terrible! The renovation of the terminal 1 causes a total chaos “, only one lift working to take you to departure and no stairs opens - absolutely ridiculous! Staff very rude and lazy. Security control is a disaster. Took us over an hour (with a toddler) from arrival at the airport to bag drop. I'm utterly disappointed
Volotea flight boarding started while the plane was delayed, boarding room too small, people packed like children and wait for more than one hour.

My recent visit to the prayer room located in the Domestic Departure area near Gates 40–45 was concerning and not reflective of high standards. The ablution area requires urgent attention. Several taps are malfunctioning, the flooring is slippery, and there are visible signs of fungus growth. Additionally, the carpet in the prayer hall emits a strong unpleasant odor, indicating that it may not have been cleaned or maintained adequately for a long period. Prayer rooms are essential facilities that serve a diverse range of passengers, including international travelers.

It’s been 30 years since I last flew through this airport. This airport is very inconvenient design. It has 3 levels. To get to baggage claim and rideshare, we had to take the escalator to level there and then take the MIA Mover train in between terminals. Then take the escalators down to baggage claim. My review is limited to Terminal D. Rideshare is on the outer curb and there are designated door numbers for rideshare pickup. Restrooms were clean. Concourses were bright and shiny with many shops and eateries open.

This airport is a complete joke. It’s like they looked at how other airports do things and then decided that by doing all those things twice or three times, they will somehow be doing it right. I lost track of the times I had to scan my cases, show my passport, show my boarding pass all before getting to a crowded, overheated waiting area at the gate. So inefficient it’s eye-wateringly painful. Some staff were friendly but others walked around nearly tripping over their self important egos…though I have no idea why - children pretending to “play airports” would have done a better job. Absolutely ludicrous experience from start to finish.

This airport needs to improve capacity. I understand it’s incredibly secure and the numerous checks in place are there for a reason. But with only three immigration counters and two security lanes it’s congested (and I was there at a quiet time). The initial sniffing dog check to enter the building needs better organised as many non Kenyans or those not familiar try to bypass and all sorts of confusion ensures. Inside is fine. Air conditioning could do with a service. Make sure you are arriving at least three hours before. Incidentally arrival is absolutely fine in NBO. No issues.
I enjoyed passing through this airport most staff friendly and it’s very efficient and clean. Experienced the Omani hospitality from arrival renting my car to boarding with Qatar.
A very good airport. The design was modern. It takes no time to pass through border control and security check. There were plenty of stores at air side.
Terminal 1, D gate was small with couple of shops. WiFi was free and fast. Nothing was special. Baggage delivery was such a disappointment. It was so slow and our bags were damaged.

Arrived early morning on a flight from Singapore with about 3 hour transit time to find a virtually empty airport where everything was closed. Very bad seating in establishments. There is only one Lufthansa lounge in the departure terminal for EU flights. I will certainly avoid this airport for connections in the future. Only positive aspect was that waiting time in immigration was okay.

The best airport in Europe. In T2 security they have the new scanners, so you just place your bag onto a belt, don't have to take anything out, can take large bottles of liquid. It is so quick. The airport is huge, so it may take longer to get to gates like K/L1, but the mini train between gates G/H and K/L departures every 2 mins and takes just a minute. Love this airport.

Me and my husband arrived into Naples airport last evening at 8pm to a chaotic experience and on arrival we were herded into a makeshift tent-like construction to join a long queue to reach the automated machines, not all of which were operational. There were people to help, and a lot of people needed help to navigate the screen. We managed to complete my husbands and he was directed to the passport e-gates, he was through in 30 minutes. My attempt failed even with help and I had to go to manual passport check. I was greeted by a queue of hundreds of passengers. There was 1 kiosk open with 2 customs officials checking passports.  I shuffled along that queue for 3 hours with long periods not moving at all. The airport ‘closed’ at 10:30pm but at the time I got through there were still probably over 200 people waiting to be processed, that was 11:30pm. I love Italy and have visited many many times, but we won’t be coming any more unless this situation is resolved.

May 2026. When we landed we had to immediately join a queue of people waiting. Not knowing what the holdup was, I assumed it was just a short queue. Absolutely the opposite. When we turned around the corner we were met with what I can only describe as a holding pen. A massive snake of people, I would estimate around 300 people all waiting to get their passports checked and fingerprints scanned. Boiling hot. No toilets. Air conditioning units that didn't work. And staff that clearly were overwhelmed. It took an hour to get through. When we then went to collect our suitcase, it was nowhere to be seen. No staff, and due to the fact that it took so long to get through, all the suitcases were stacked up on top of each other. It took 30 minutes to locate our suitcases. I dont moan about many things. But I felt like a sheep being herded in a pen. When I complained to staff it was a simple shrug of the shoulders. The reason why we had to wait because of the new EES.

This is probably the worst organized airport I have ever been in. Once you walk in the main doors, there is only a screen to show you your flight with no additional information - no gate, no boarding time, not even an area to head towards. The staff look miserable and no staff available for directions or questions either. There is minimal seating and people are crowded in areas just standing. You are only given a gate number 25 minutes before boarding. The train station in Naples is much more organized and less crowded - take the train if possible!

I have been standing in a queue to board the plane for over 2 hours. My flight has not been delayed or cancelled and no one will tell us anything 1 person has managed to make it through so far I am not a parent but I have watched as multiple families struggle to take care of their children as there is no seats for anyone. This ridiculous.

This is a very small airport with one terminal building and undergoing expansion. As is the practice with all Turkish airports, one has to clear security twice (upon entry into terminal and then for airside). Because of the construction, temporary bathrooms have been set up near an outdoor baggage claim. Within the terminal there is one bathroom in the check in area and two in the waiting lounge. Seating at the gate are hard and uncomfortable. No power ports to charge phones except along the wall next to the mosque entrance. Small eateries airside for coffee/snacks. Overall, this small airport is very clean and busy hence the expansion of terminal building.

We had a horrible experience. My husband & i flew with our 3 kids 11, 6 & 4. Our youngest has autism & a developmental delay. I set up TSA Cares in advance & was told i may or may not get a email from the airport. I didnt, so when I arrived, I asked a TSA person I saw on my way to the TSA check point. I told them I set up the TSA Cares & she told me to let the person at the TSA check point know & they would get the TSA Cares for me. So I did & the person at the Checkpoint basically told me no and I could just go through. Ok whatever. So we start going through & im putting stuff in the bins. My daughter (the 1 with autism) stuffed animal got into 1 of the bins & she starts freaking out & screaming. I grab the stuffy outta the bin & I told the person working at that spot that I would put it in at the end (so she would stop screaming) & he informed me that since it had already been in the bin, I couldn't have it back (even though it was currently in my hand) & I had to put it back in. 4 out of 10 of our bags got flagged & they had 2 scan (or whatever they did) before we could get them back (they kept skipping em & checking other peoples. we had to wait over 10 mins with my daughter screaming the whole time because her stuffy was in 1 of the bins that had been flagged.  The bathrooms are very nice & clean

I came back from Malta on 29 December about 5pm. Although there were problems with some of the Assisted aid, I eventually found I think his name was Steve in the airport. He was very kind and helped me to the taxi and I appreciated him being there. Please pass my thanks onto him.

The departure area post gates is horrific, they have 6 food options spread across 3 terminals and all of them have an hour plus wait, if you want food stop before the airport and don’t bother buying it here, Orlando airport is unable to serve its patrons and fliers properly, Newark, Miami, Tampa, JFK all have much better outlooks…. Do yourself a favor and visit just about any other airport.

One of the worst airports I have flown out of recently. There are lines for everything. Food, TSA, shops, and even the Rest Rooms are the smallest I have seen at an airport in the USA. I felt like I was back at the theme parks, there were lines for everything I wanted or needed to do and everything was expensive.

I had a very frustrating experience at Orlando International Airport involving both TSA and flight communication. Going through TSA was uncomfortable and poorly handled. As a first-time traveler, I followed instructions and even confirmed with one officer that I could keep my hoodie on due to a personal comfort issue. However, another officer repeatedly interrupted me while I was trying to explain and spoke to me in a rude and dismissive tone. There was also a clear lack of communication between staff, as the officer who approved me did not step in when the situation escalated. I was even told to go to the back of the line after complying, which felt unnecessary. In addition to that, there was very poor communication regarding my Spirit Airlines flight delay. The app showed the flight was delayed by about an hour, so my group adjusted our arrival time accordingly. However, when we arrived, we were told the flight was already boarding and some members of my group were told they might have to take the next flight 8 hours later due to baggage. After rushing through security, we made it to the gate only to find that the plane was nowhere near departure. The flight, originally scheduled for 7:33 AM, rdid not leave until 10:34 AM due to delays. This entire experience was stressful, confusing, and avoidable with better communication and professionalism. Travelers should be able to rely on accurate updates and be treated with basic respect, especially in high-stress environments like airports.
I had broken my toe and needed to have a wheelchair. They pushed me through the whole airport, right to the door of the airplane. Very courteous. Very helpful. God bless you all.

Ridiculous that all the advance check in machines were switched off for an event. it would have been easy to leave them on and slightly reduce the event space. hours waiting unnecessarily for this nonsense and a very poor service no alternative was offered.

I live in cayman and every time I go away, the employees are always so rude. I understand that it is early morning but that gives no excuse to be rude. If you do not like your job, I’m pretty sure there are young caymanians who would want the job.

This is a quaint and beautiful airport with a lot of outdoor space. From TSA to the Gates, one has to go through an open air courtyard. Once inside the gate area, there are a few shops and one restaurant that has outside and indoor seating). The departure area itself is indoors; however, because of the open air areas, there are many small birds flying in and out. There is a charging wall with several electrical outlets and USB and USB-C ports to plug phones/devices. Restrooms very clean. TSA Pre was a breeze to go through (no more than 2 minutes). The walk from the rental car return to the terminal is not very long. Its manageable.
Well connected to the city by bus and train. Quick security, good choice of shops and restaurants . Clean and not too crowded. Nice views of the sea. Overall a good experience

A reasonable sized airport serving Palermo and the rest of the island. It's generally modern and nicely designed, security isn't the fastest (manual checking of boarding passes), staffs friendliness depends on their mood and boarding is a bit messy. Connections to palermo are offered by coach or train in the basement. Food and beverages are expensive but high quality.

Small airport with an excellent regular bus service to Paphos town. Only €2 Euro. The airport shops are expensive like most airports. I recommend taking your own snacks and an empty bottle. There is a free water refill machine inside the departure lounge. Only bargains in the Duty Free shop are cigarettes and tobacco. The perfume the same price of not more expensive than shops outside the airport.

I came in from London on March 24 into Terminal 4 with a connecting flight to Orlando in the same terminal. Why did I have to go out of security and back in for a connecting flight? We arrived at 12:30pm and my flight was at 3:40pm. Needless to say, I missed my connecting flight as did hundreds of others. I was in a security line for 4.5 hours Any TSA person you tried to ask a question through said I can't answer that keep moving, I don't know keep moving. They were merging lines upon lines upon lines. For the thousands of people there at the time there were only 5 security lines open. There were limited ICE personnel there, but they were just standing around. They were not assisting TSA with the security lines. Worst airport ever. Thank goodness for Delta they were able to get me on the last flight to Orlando as I spoke to them while in the security line.=

Our plane arrived at the American Airlines terminal (Terminal 8) from Tokyo. It was a 13+ hour flight and we left Haneda 3 hours late due to a mechanical problem. After arriving at the terminal, we were told that there was a problem with the skybridge and were asked to remain seated for one hour while repairs were made. A major inconvenience that could have been avoided by sim0ply moving the plane to another gate. Upon leaving the plane, passengers were greeting with old, filthy water-stained carpeting. As an American, I felt ashamed that international visitors enter the USA at such a dirty and unattractive terminal, while passengers arriving at Narita and Haneda airports in Japan enter terminals that are bright, attractive and spotlessly clean.

I transit this airport 12 times in last 4 years. This time cleanliness was little better. But food price wise this airport is the worst of the worst. 1 small bottle of coke is 6 dollars canadian. If one wants to eat 1 time meal then prepare for $50 for fast food only. Facilities wise not so much, this airport is a big super market, that's it.

They don't have free Wi-Fi, many waiting areas in Terminal 1 near the gates are dirty, old, and staffed with unhelpful people, etc. It feels like a Third World country. Panama: you can do better! Aeropuerto Nivel Rata No tienen WiFi gratis, muchas salas de espera en Terminal 1 cerca de puertas de embarque estan sucias, son viejas, con personal desinteresado, etc. Se siente como pais fel Tercer Mundo.

I arrived bright and early at 6:00 AM, armed with optimism and the belief that I would gracefully glide through the airport like a seasoned traveler in a Scandinavian tourism ad. To the airport’s credit, the arrival experience was impeccable. Border patrol had zero lines.  What Oslo Airport does brilliantly is create the illusion of simplicity. From the outside, it looks modest, even cozy. But once you start walking, you realize the place operates on a vast circular labyrinth design. Departing security (TSA equivalent) was impressively smooth. Midday crowds didn’t seem to faze the system. The security staff were efficient, professional, and everything moved quickly. However, the true adventure begins when you attempt to connect flights. At some point I passed through border control twice because the airport’s layout basically nudges you into doing so. The terminal is arranged like a giant loop where you can enter one way and exit another, but heaven help you if your connecting flight happens to be on the opposite side.  It's an impossible transfer. Another challenge is the lack of airport helpers or guides stationed throughout the terminal. At Oslo Airport, you’re largely left to navigate the terrain yourself. If you’re unfamiliar with the layout and short on time, this can turn into a surprisingly stressful scavenger hunt.

There were no mother-and-baby clearance counter at this airport. My husband, who has a foreign passport, and I had to queue at the manual counter with our infant, who is less than a year old. My husband was told to queue in the foreigners' lane. Going through customs alone with a small baby is very difficult and chaotic. I hope the airport can improve and establish mother-and-baby-friendly customs counters.

The worst airport i have been to. The check in was moving so slow it took us 50 minutes just to check in our bags even though it wasn't that many people there. The security control also chaos. No compassion what so ever from staff when you are stressed and need help, we missed our plane because of getting no help from staff and everything moving so slow.

Phu Quoc airport is quite poor. The air conditioning is not working. No wifi. Worst is all shops are expensive and pricing is USD which is 3 times more expensive. Very disappointed by the airport specially for a city which is trying to attract tourists. Danang, Hanoi are much better airports.

This time I was actually able to pass through security screening in good time, and without being harassed. Also managed to get through quickly this time. We could probably do with some additional food options at Perth, and duty free .. well we are most certainly limited there. Upon return from Singapore I was able to pass through security without over zealous Border Force officers this time, so that was a plus. I needed to inform family and friends of my whereabouts, but unfortunately I could not find any kind of public USB charging station. I think that this is something that the Perth Airport Commission should consider installing.

In my opinion, Perth still rates as one of the worst airports in the world. It shows no real signs of recovering either. Every  time I have departed this airport I have been checked for explosives etc.  My phone and tablet computer were scanned, took close to 2 hours. I was advised that if I did not give them pass codes, I would be detained until I did. For everybody out there, please know that the contents of my devices were copied, and I quote: "The copy is now the property of the Australian Federal Government." This is something that is not in the public domain. I suggest if you are passing through you back up your device to an online storage and then wipe your device. I met another guy who had been detained as well. Same age group as me, he told me this has happened to him five times before. As I left, a family of about 4 were being taken aside. I wrote an email of complaint to Border Force Australia, and it was ignored.

Flight to Melbourne. 5.30am departure on Monday 19th Jan. I arrived 1hour 15 mins ahead of departure. It was chaos and I had to stand for 1hour 10 mins just to bag drop. I stood in line because apparently automated bag drop takes ages.

Passport control was not difficult. The tech worked very well (both face recognition and prints) and there were many staff available to help. The queue was around 20 minutes both on arrival and departure.

Much less stressful than I was expecting; new passport and fingerprinting technology worked flawlessly and there were no queues for security scanning. The gate area was spacious and airy with plenty of seating and food options, and the Duty Free shop felt much less invasive and claustrophobic than those in the UK. I would have given this a 5-star review but for one male passport control member, who, after being rude to me, was so angered by my response (a solo female traveller) that he jumped out of his booth, shouted at me, and jabbed his finger in my arm. This man needs to lose his job.

The restaurants here are a joke. Little to no actual table seating for mobility impaired flyers. All the seating seems to be counters with stools which will not accommodate a person in a wheelchair. The governor announces that this airport is the "friendliest" in the USA. I truly beg to differ. As to customer service for mobility impaired flyers, it is bare minimum at best. A far cry from the extremely friendly and helpful service we received in Wichita. Too bad we had to fly from here to SLC. Waiting areas are small and overly crowded. Not a great experience.

This airport is awful. Way too many people and very little seating, no outlets for charging, very minimal food and shopping and it was absolutely packed everywhere you went. There was no escape. Our flight was delayed hours, and I’m currently stuck on a plane that is waiting for a pilot…no idea why they took us out of the air conditioned terminal to sit on a plane in 100+ degree weather to roast while waiting for a freaking pilot. Saw a ton of gate changes causing mass confusion, and as others have said, they have AC, which is about the only positive thing I can say besides their staff being incredibly nice.
Here to pick up family at arrival. Only vending machines. Dirty, staff rude, Very limited seating and American at several terminals that requires walking outside. Worst place I have been.

Awful in every way. Fast track security is a joke. Too crowded generally and if you try to minimise your time sweating in the departure lounge sweating like everyone else don't but fast track as it is unmonitored and you have to fit with people in the normal queue who think you are pushing in. Very stressful.

This is the worst airport I have been in for the last 10 years. Total shambles at arrival with 2 hours to clear passport, 2 staff on duty shouting at passengers to do this, then stop, don’t do that. Border agent taking 3 minutes to slowly flick through a passport despite using an electronic machine to take biometric pictures and finger prints. Same shambles coming back, lengthy queue at passport control to again take biometric pictures and fingerprints for everyone. I have never know an airport to be this slow, disorganised and rude. The terminal itself is dirty, lounge is dirty with very poor choice and standard of food. I would give Pisa Airport a wide berth and fly anywhere else

Arrived 4+ hours before flight time and the passport control process was a nightmare. The automated equipment failed, worked briefly, then went on an extended coffee/lunch/dinner break. The personnel managing the lines kept making random changes to the flow of passengers, so that later arrivals kept ending up in front of people who had been in line for a half hour or more. No humans arrived to take over for the failed machines. Then, their inspired solution was to send everyone in line for the automated machines to the end of the line for the EU passports where actual humans were available to process passengers. No thought was given creating a merging of lines now. Once with the passport control officer, the fingerprint reader failed to register my prints, and the camera took three or four tries to work successfully. Surely there were people on duty for whom this wasn’t their first day on the job. More likely still, the idea of providing equitable service to the public is clearly not part of CDG’s or passport control’s ethos. Next, we went on to experience security screening. Despite being required to remove everything from my pockets, including tissues, the screening alerted upon my passage, as it did for the next eight people in a row. Having finally been wanded, patted down and checked, the gent screening us couldn’t be bothered to say OK, or nod or gesture to let us know to move on. This, while the automatic screener had to be stopped because so many people were waiting to be screened manually. What a despicable mess. We will avoid CGD like the plague in the future. Use Switzerland as the point of embarkation in the future. Sadly, this experience reconfirms the stereotype of France’s poor to execrable customer service.
Why are there no post boxes? I have already attached stamps on my cards and want to put them in the Poste….but there are no boxes?

Arrived at Terminal 2A instead of 2C as informed by the airlines. It was a bit confused with us and took us some more times to double check and find our ways to meet our friends who were waiting for us at Terminal 2C. The immigration, however, was a big positive surprise to us as it was not crowded and we even completed the process faster than the EU passport holders in the other lines. Bag delivery was also very quick and efficient!
It is clean and large. The efficiency of immigration and security is not high. Employees are friendly. The WiFi connection is good. Signposts are clear.

Our flights were scheduled to depart De Gaulle from Terminal 2E. When the 4 of us learned that we would have a 6-hour layover there, we expected to spend a few hours at an upscale, full service restaurant or a nice bistro. We were very displeased to find that there was no traditional restaurant with seating at all or bistro. Instead, the concourse was equipped with kiosks, vending machines, Yo Sushi and a Pret A Manger. The exception was a gourmet shop that sold 2 kinds of baguette sandwiches: ham and cheese and brie cheese. They also sold cheese, wine and desserts; but, again, there was no seating for dining. So we bought 2 ham and cheese sandwiches, a few small bottles of wine, and sat on the seats in the concourse and wished we were at the airport in Rome or London.

After a long-haul international flight arriving in Terminal 2E, I had an 11-hour connection with an early morning departure (6:45 AM) from Terminal 2F. I expected to be able to access the transfer area and wait near my gate to rest, but the internal transfer between terminals 2E and 2F was closed overnight. No clear information or alternative was provided. I was told by staff to “come back at 6:10,” which is exactly the boarding time — an unrealistic and misleading instruction that could have caused me to miss my flight. As a result, I was forced to spend the entire night in an area with very limited seating. In the morning, when the transfer finally opened around 5:30 AM, the situation was poorly managed. Passengers were waiting without clear instructions, and a staff member spoke to us in a very rude manner, telling us we were not allowed to queue — despite no signage indicating this. Only after I asked her in French, calmly, to speak respectfully did her attitude noticeably change. Overall, this experience reflects very poor organization, lack of clear communication, and inadequate consideration for passengers in long layovers. This is not what one would expect from a major international airport like CDG.

I arrived at CDG at 1910 from LGW via Air France. VEverything went well until we got to passport control. There was an IT outage. First mistake was not letting people know what's happening for a very long time (2.5  hours). No one including EU travellers were allowed through. All the recording said was that it was due to a peak period and that continuous updates will be provided. My family and I were standing in queue for nearly three hours. At 2.5 hours delay a man dressed in a police like uniform said EU passport holders were allowed through. I had to ask another support staff if Australian passports are allowed through and finally we were allowed through. The counter staff just checked the passport ID page briefly and looked at our faces to let us through. Why was this contingency plan not initiated earlier. For example after 15 minutes delay, inform people what is happening, after 30 minutes delay start letting people through by manually checking passports. We were treated like livestock waiting to be boarded onto a ship or something. Absolutely appalling.  It was our first visit to France and what a bad first impression.  What surprised me was the lack of contingency plans to deal with such disruptions. We could have been diverted to another exit point even.
Shocking passport control, had to use the under 12 queue because we were travelling with children and the queue took over an hour! Every other queue seemed to move except this one

Terminal 3 is not the best airport I’ve came across. Rude staffing at checkpoint. Inspected our carry on bags and Took a lotion from me and my party where 1 lotion was all the way empty but didn’t pass the 100ml point. And 1 that was full and exceed 100 ml by a little bit. Once I told the staff comments one of them proceeded to give me my purse with all the items I had inside on the tray and told me to hurry up and fix it. I really hope they can get re training on how to interact with people and not be so mean.  No charging area in terminal 3 before check point. Restrooms were clean and very clean. But if you do fly out of here be prepared for chaos and rudeness. Also signage could work also if they put it in Spanish.

Upon arrival at CDG airport from Singapore, I had left my passport and boarding pass on the plane when I disembarked, and only realised when I reached immigration. The team at the immigration area was super helpful and friendly, and contacted the supervisor working in the Singapore Airlines team at CDG airport. Initially, they couldn't find my passport at my seat area, and I was asked to possibly visit the embassy and change travel plans. But the Singapore Airlines supervisor was persistent and he requested the engineer to dismantle the entire seat - and lo and behold my passport was indeed wedged in the seat. I am just so grateful for the kindness and generosity of the supervisor as well as the very helpful and friendly staff at the immigration section. Also should mention the immigration area and entire walk through was very fast, and looks very modern and clean. Thank you so much!

I have just had the great misfortune to use CDG which reinforced my view that it is by far the worst airport in the world. Even with Sky Priority it took 45 minutes to get through security in terminal 2F, all because of a camera with a separate lens in my cabin bag, something that has been halfway around the world and back without a problem. The signage is confusing, toilets few and far between, the staff are miserable and the lounges are the worst I've been in. There are NO positives other than the RER B metro line to get to and from Paris centre.

Being made to wait 1 hour for passport control upon departure is unacceptable in a country like France. 3 booths only out of 8 were operating. Surely the authorities are informed of the numbers of passengers and should be able to provide an adequate number of officers. Passengers pay a not insignificant tax when flying out of CDG and a decent service should therefore be provided. It is a pity that so many people's last experience of France is to be put through an ordeal that even 3rd world countries rarely exceed. I prefer to fly out of Marseille where at least one feels like a human being and not like cattle as in CDG T1.

Unprofessional, rude, and aggressive behaviour from security staff at the Terminal F security checkpoint. Luggage inspections were unusually slow, with no explanations provided to passengers. One staff member was visibly angry and was cursing while collecting the trays that had accumulated. He handled them in an aggressive manner and forcefully slammed one down right next to my son. This was intimidating, completely inappropriate, and unacceptable behaviour towards passengers, especially in the presence of a child. This incident reflects very poorly on the airport’s standards of passenger safety and professionalism.

I was most impressed with the kind and proactive support of the airport staff who greatly facilitated my progress through the airport generally but then all the formalities (security, passport control, etc.) I was using a lanyard to communicate that I need extra help and it was delivered kindly and proactively. My dignity was respected and it was as painless as navigating through a large, complex environment can be for someone with an invisible disability. It was a very positive experience.

Missed my connection here even though I had plenty of time. Signage poor and lack of information desks was the cause. Had to book a new flight the following day and travel back to Dublin through terminal 1. Arrived at 7:15 and the airport was carnage. Total lack of information desks, sent in the wrong direction multiple times by staff. In some cases it was the staff themselves that were the cause of the queues. There was one lady whose job seemed to be to stop people at the bottom of an escalator for no apparent reason, backing people up unnecessarily. I don’t know how many times we used escalators to change levels. Passport control was automated, but we were sent round in a big circle back to where we started from passing through the same automated gate twice. The security was very badly managed, the staff were in the wrong place to speed things up. The food choices inside were poor, plenty of designer outlets though. The seating area at the gate was very nice, but not as comfortable as it looked. Typically French inefficiency, with rude staff that either did not know what they were doing or were being deliberately obstructive. I strongly recommend a significant investment in staff training, and maybe hire some people that can smile. A horrible experience, I will avoid this airport for connections going forward at all cost.

Two staff at passport control with 100 people in the queue. Other airport staff just hanging around. No organisation. Took an hour but could have taken 10 minutes with better organising. One passport control lady was scrutinising every passport to the enth degree - does she not realise people are leaving not arriving?

I had a very negative experience at this airport. The check-in staff were rude and unprofessional, and the check-in area was chaotic and disorganized. We were among the very few passengers who nearly missed boarding because the check-in agents did not understand how to process our documents. They kept asking for a visa, despite the fact that it is impossible to have both a visa and a residence permit at the same time. This was an extremely frustrating and stressful experience.  The staff behavior was simply terrible.

The airport immigration queue is over crowded and they charge a 200 bath express fee. This is tip money and illegal. Hence they have all the incentive to slow down to create demand for express service. What a shame in the Thailand tourist environment. non official payment

Check in was very slow. The Lounge of the airport is of low quality,  small and run down. The airline flight boarding was slow, as we had to wait at the passenger bridge for approx.25-30 min. The airport cannot handle the travel intensity

They have done a great job of rejuvenating this airport to look very nice but it seems like administratively the same problems still exist. Twice the airport has snapped off a wheel on two different sets of luggage. The past four times I've landed here a plane is still at our arrival gate so we have to sit on the tarmac. And once there was no individual available to bring the arrival tunnel to the plane so we waited at the gate for 15 minutes. It's the little things, but there also isn't another option if you live in portland so I guess it is what it is.

Toilets are outside, smoking cabins inside! That’s a complete disaster. The smell of cigarettes is polluting the whole waiting room because the sliding door opening and closing all the time! There are 2 toilets at the waiting room but they both outside. Why the smoking room isn’t outside? There’s a lot of phone charging points but none of them works!

The main level has better seating and speakers. The lower level for gate 20 is terrible. Fancy seating that takes too much room and seats few people. People were standing everywhere. Lucky if you find a seat. The speakers are terrible and hardly understood a word they said. Shame on you
Gross costs for food. 'No' water fountain available. Ridiculous high price for bottled water over $10 ! Avoid buying anything there; plan ahead.

I travelled from Pune to Delhi by Indigo by flight 6E166 on 5th March26. During security check , for hand baggage my two small sealed masala packets were not allowed by the CISF (?) personnel & asked me to put up in check in baggage. This was not possible as I already got boarding pass. I was senior citizen female, travelling alone so no any other option but to part with masala pouches for which I. didn’t get any receipt or asked to sign in any register. I am frequent international & domestic air traveller so always very particular what to take in check in & hand baggage. I checked the website again but didn’t find any mention about masala packet not allowed .Is this latest Pune Airport added security dangerous hazard?

On arrival at the airport, we were met with huge queues to identify ourselves. There were no signs or explanations to direct us. No staff to guide airport customers, it was like a big cattle shed. We queued 45 minutes to digitally enter our passport and fingerprints. After trying to enter our details, the machine could not recognise us and we were told to proceed to manual immigration and another queue for 50 minutes. We were so long trying to pass through immigration, our cases had been removed from the carousel and stacked up the wall. We thought it would be better on return and leaving the airport for home. But it was twice as long and stressful. We queued an hour to drop off our cases. People queuing everywhere, no direction from any staff. The belt broke down for 20 minutes. We then proceeded to security, where we queued for another hour. Only one gate was open. But that wasn't the last of our queueing. Our flight was due to leave in 20 minutes. But the immigration queues to get out of the country were so long, it took us another hour to have our photo taken again and show our passport again. No direction, no urgency for people who had flights leaving very soon. By this time we thought we had missed our flight, as it was due to leave 30 minutes ago. We were now extremely stressed. A bus was waiting at the gate and there were about 10 of us still not on the flight.We saw the back steps being taken away from the aeroplane. The flight waited for us, closed the doors behind us and prepared for take off. This is an absolute disgrace of the way people are treated at an airport. We are frequent travellers, but have never in our life been treated so appallingly. A beautiful country, lovely people,but a shambolic airport.

Things have started to get worse at this airport now that it is used more and more by low-cost airlines. To use the wifi, you need to log on using your own internet to get a verification e-mail which is a very stupid and 2005 way to handle things (what if you don't have internet on your device and that's why you want to use the wifi?!) and yep, you guessed it, you get disconnected after just a few minutes! Note to Prague airport: Wifi is not a luxury nowadays, you're actually supposed to provide such things!

Prague city especially in December was magical but with the airport experience in arrival and departure I dont think I will ever come back In arrival we have stayed almost 3 hours just to go to border control. In my line was a man that only for one passenger took 30 min. When our time came after 3 hours he has checked one by one all the stamps of my husbands passport and called 3 other officers to checked , and took a microscop to check the chip of the passport. Wen I asked if there is any problem , his answer was no just for fun I am checking. In departure Ryanair delayed the flight as many passenger could not catch it. We wait 4 hours to scan the ticket, border control etc. Unfortunately Prague was beautiful but from my trip I remember a nightmare
Really bad airport. No restaurants. Only a pub for hot food and no menu in English . Had to collect my food. Will try not to fly through Riga again.

I get to Queenstown to depart 3 hrs before and checkin as required when checkin and baggage drop opens, then go to go through security checkpoint to find on a sign that states it only opens 2hrs before departure. Plus the airport lounge is past the checkpoint, so you can't get to it either, then there is insufficient seating available with two airlines opening at the same time. We went and sat at one of the coffee shops outside and were then asked to move as we weren't eating and other people who were, could not sit.
Passport control completely overwhelmed. Queue the length of the airport. Hardly any staff and they were unable to give clear instruction or explanation.

Very impressed by the new business lounge at KKIA. The old one was very small, cramped, and one had to leave it to go to the restrooms. The new one (branded CATRION) is super spacious, with excellent seating, amenities, and an expansive buffet. The rest of the airport is unchanged, but I've found it very easy to handle, especially with the metro connection which opened a year ago. Only drawback is that to go from metro station to the Saudia business class check in, one must go out of the airport and walk about 50 meters or so to enter from another entrance. A bit inconvenient, especially when the weather is bad.

The EES system at Ciampino doesn’t work. We arrived 3.5 hours earlier but passport wasn’t even open until around 2.5 hours before. I queued for the EES system, which then rejected mine and many other passengers passports creating a large queue for the one manual guard. This moved too slowly with the queue only getting bigger and the call to board the aircraft was called after nearly 2 hours in the manual queue and still no sign of getting through. Myself and many Manchester bound passengers raised our concerns over an hour earlier when the line was not moving.
