The very reactive nature of not increasing passport staff with a very poor EES system just caused frustration, anxiety and anger that just wasn’t warranted if the airport had acted to increase passport control staff when a serious system failure was occurring. It didn’t help when the Italian passengers were then upset as we were called to the front to rush us through. Again this could have been avoided by proactively increasing staff over an hour earlier instead of increasing to 3 passport officers while the last call for boarding was happening. It may of stopped some of the anger towards British passengers who were moved to the front. Overall this experience has soured my view on travelling through Europe with this dysfunctional EES system.
Just come back from Rome and the airport security was first class. No queues, no drama, helpful polite staff. Cannot rate it highly enough Rome overall is an amazing place. Well done Italy

We have been in the arrivals line for more than two hours and have at least an hour to go. The customs area had no communication, none of the kiosks were up and running, and none of the staff was able to communicate what was happening and why there was such a delay. People were cutting in line, pushing to get downstairs, and they separated families with children under 12 so their wait time was even longer. People were yelled at for getting out of line to use the restroom. Overall, an awful experience.
We stood for 2 hours with my children for the passport control. If we had known, we wouldn't have come. If you don't want to be disgraced, don't come

We took the bus from Vatican to the airport and it parked right in the middle of T1 and T3 which was quite convenient. The airport was well organized, clean with many working stations, as well as food and shopping options though the food was so pricey. WiFi was free and fast. Easy to navigate to the gate too.
It took me nearly 2.5 hours to exit the airport as I did not have EU passport. They make you stand for 2 hours in immigration queue.

I wish to extend our thanks to the Special Assistance staff at Fiumicino & Catania Airports today. Both my parents require wheelchairs through the airport from check-in to the plane. And then off the plane through arrivals. The service offered was seamless and faultless. Every member of staff was efficient, professional & polite. They went out of their way to make this a stress free experience and we are very grateful to them.

My experience as a transit passenger was a total nightmare and passing through immigration in Terminal 3 was the worst. ​The staff was unprofessional, rude, and aggressive to me. The automated passport gates failed for about 15 of us at different times in the queue. Instead of providing clear instructions, a staff member screamed in Italian, ignoring the fact that we we did not understand her. Another forced us into the middle of an already crowded manual queue, causing unnecessary tension and anger from other passengers who were already waiting. After leaving immigration, there was no one available to give directions. When I finally found a staff member at an official service desk near the baggage area he refused to help.

On arrival, the immigration process was chaotic. You have to scan your passport multiple times—first to register, then again to pass immigration. No other airport I’ve traveled through has this kind of entry procedure. The lines were massive everywhere because the scanners didn’t work properly. I saw people trying three different machines without success. After registering your passport, you must scan it again at immigration, where I waited an hour and a half due to faulty equipment. The airport staff presence was almost nonexistent. Only one person was managing a line of more than 1,000 people. Departure was even worse. There are signs directing certain passport holders (Korean, in my case) to automatic customs clearance, but staff redirected everyone into a single general line. That line took at least an hour and a half because only two counters were open. The airport was unbearably hot everywhere, with no functioning air conditioning. Will definitely avoid using it again.

I have been living in Rome as a non-EU student for several months. I hold a valid Italian multiple-entry Type D visa, and I have an ongoing residence permit application, for which I possess the official receipt (ricevuta). I have previously traveled outside and re-entered Italy under the same legal conditions without any issues. During my departure, I presented my passport and ricevuta as required in order to receive an exit stamp. The officer asked whether this was my first residence permit application, and I replied that it was my first application under my current status. However, she referred to a residence permit application I had made two years ago during my Erasmus period, which is no longer valid and has no legal connection to my current visa or application. Despite my documents being complete and valid, the officer repeatedly insisted that this was not my first application, creating unnecessary confusion and stress. Communication was particularly difficult, as the officer spoke very limited English and relied on single words rather than clear explanations. Throughout the interaction, her attitude was dismissive and unprofessional. Eventually, the exit stamp was issued, confirming that there was no legal issue with my documents. However, the manner in which the situation was handled caused significant and avoidable distress. I am not contesting the procedure itself, but rather the officer’s behavior, communication style, and lack of professionalism. I believe border control procedures should be carried out with clarity and respect, especially when dealing with international students who are complying fully with legal requirements.

The rude, degrading, and demeaning behaviour displayed by security staff toward myself and the group I was travelling with was awful. The experience was unacceptable and deeply unprofessional. There was no clear or adequate signage explaining what was required of passengers prior to entering the security screening area. As a result, we were left to guess what procedures were expected. Instead of being provided with guidance or an opportunity to rectify any mistakes, we were publicly singled out and made examples of for not “knowing” procedures that had not been explained. Compounding this issue was the way we were treated for not speaking fluent German. We made a genuine effort to communicate and had taken the time to learn basic German courtesies and niceties. Despite this, staff made no attempt to communicate clearly or meet us halfway. Instead, they simply raised their voices and repeated instructions more loudly in German. This behaviour was intimidating, dismissive, and entirely inappropriate. Shouting in a language passengers do not fully understand is not effective communication and does nothing to educate or assist. When we attempted to ask for clarification, we were shut down and spoken to dismissively. At no point were clear instructions given, nor was there any willingness to assist. All three members of staff involved were rude, unhelpful, and unprofessional in both their tone and behaviour. If Infinite expects passengers to follow procedures that differ from those used at most European airports—such as not allowing bags to go through unpacked—then it is essential that clear signage is provided. This should include visual, picture-based instructions so passengers can easily understand what is required before reaching security. The current lack of guidance, combined with hostile staff behaviour, creates unnecessary stress and confrontation. A basic level of courtesy, professionalism, and cultural awareness would significantly improve the process for both staff and passengers. Manners and clear communication cost nothing and would make security screening far more efficient and respectful.

I’m a 2 million mile traveler and have been to most US airports and many international airports. I was first very excited to hear that SLC was growing and building a new airport. My excitement ended the first time I flew into this marathon airport. The amenities are good and it’s clean - that’s where it ends! If you like to walk, and I mean walk, this terribly designed airport has you covered. If you fly into B gates and need to connect to A gates or baggage claim, prepare yourself for a mile walk. Even from one end A or B concourse is probably over a half mile long. Whoever was the architect firm that designed this, they should ask for a refund and prohibited from designing any other project. I feel sorry for elderly or disabled flyers. The moving walkways are slow and a joke. There are little to no electric carts to ride on. They need multiple carts just to ferry people through the tunnel from A and B concourses. Again, what was once exciting has turned out to be a nightmare.

Your duty-free items will be confiscated. This shop sells non-ICAO-compliant security bags (STEB). Despite explicitly asking before purchasing two expensive bottles of rum, the staff assured me that the bags were internationally recognized. In Toronto, the goods were confiscated because the bag does not meet global security standards. The result: Money and rum gone due to deliberate misrepresentation.

I want to share a very upsetting experience we had at San Antonio Airport. Our flight was delayed due to technical issues and we had to change aircrafts. We landed after midnight, already exhausted. When we reached the airbridge, we were informed that our twin stroller was broken into two pieces. We had also checked two infant car seats, but because it was raining, only one car seat was brought up—leaving us with even more baggage to manage. We were told a gate agent would help us. Wheelchair assistance was arranged, seemingly to help us move our belongings. However, the staff member refused to assist, saying the wheelchair was “only for one person.” I understand policies, but it was 1am, I had a 15-month-old and two 3-month-old twins, and it was just me and my mother-in-law trying to manage broken equipment, car seats, and luggage. How can a mother with three babies be left in that situation with no compassion, no alternatives, and no support? Only after I became very emotional (which I am not proud of) did the wheelchair assistant finally help us. The other staff member walked off making unprofessional comments. This was one of the most disappointing displays of customer care and humanity I have ever experienced.
Lovely airport, especially the international terminal. Spacious and open with lots of art to look at. Love the place and can’t see why so many seem to be negative.

This airport can only be described as “uncontrolled chaos.” There were so many people there and no one to direct you where to go first. I have never seen an airport set up this way. Nothing made any sense and there was no method to the madness. The far and few airport staff members that we could find were very short with us. The space was very tiny and lacked any place to sit. We were there very early and needed every bit of our time just to try to figure out the process. This airport is in desperate need of new management.
Excellent airport, from parking to the gate took 15 minutes and every staff member encountered had a smile and a joke. Love this airport so much, it's an absolute dream!

Do not land or depart from this airport unless you have TSA Pre or Clear. If you are reasonable and get to the airport 2hrs before you flight, it’s a guarantee miss. The TSA agent to passenger ratio is horrendous! There are 2 officers per 200 passengers moving at the pace of a snail. Staff do not communicate well for the volume of passengers. Multiple staff workers say that other check points are moving faster but they are just blowing smoke. Due to this, I missed my flight due to this and was forced to stay another night. The signs that list the approx. wait time are not accurate at all. Next time you come here, look at the wait time and multiply that by 5 for a more accurate wait time.

Absolutely disgusting place. Our autistic son asked two separate TSA agents for help and both (separately) laughed at him and called him retarded. He was nothing but calm and polite asking for help. One woman said it's all his fault, and walked away, and another man laughed and said can't you read what the sign says? Be ashamed of your workers.

Not Verified     I'm very angry at the moment. We have to wait here for three hours till the desk opens where we can check our luggage in: There are no seats, no waiting area to see or signed. I had a long walk with my disabled father and saw other people sitting on the floor with their luggage around. I had to deposit my father in this ugly disabled-corner. As he does not accept to be left alone - and I do not accept to sit on a disabled-chair: I opened my luggage, put out my plastic bag with the dirty clothes as a pillow, and made it as comfortable as possible on the floor, using as much space as possible, putting my shoes off, arranging bottle, knitting etc. around me. Sitting here for almost two hours: Nobody cares!

The airport is very crowded. No staff can help when you ask, they don’t know, there is one or two cafes and the place where the gate numbers are supposed to be are all broken. The screens are broken and The security staff are absolutely horrible and take no care and pride of their guests. There was one line at the very start of where arrivals enter of maybe holding 600 people and one security guard standing there. This is an atrociously terrible airport. People are waiting 9 hours for the flights due to no reasons given by the airport itself. Awful airport.

Worst airport I have been to. Absolute chaos when we arrived there and when we departed. The staff inparticular the passport control staff are very rude, they just want to take advantage of people for money. We got stopped for more than half an hour, although we had British Passports, the man claimed he wanted to see my partners 'foreign passport' as his parents are from a different country, despite us saying he was born in the UK and they can see it on the passport he insisted we get a copy of my partners foreign passport which is nonexistent. We went back and forth a number of times, he was being aggressive and spoke to us in a demeaning way asking us a number of times to repeat what our full names are, he didn't like the way we pronounced it and insisted we pronounce in an Arabic way. He was after money which we were not giving. He took our passports and would not explain what the issue was, he told my partner to write on a piece of paper his full name in Arabic which we did not understand why. After minutes of standing around he gave up, stamped our passports and ushered us to go away without explaining what the whole problem was, it tainted our view of Egypt as this was just when we had arrived. When we departed it was absolute chaos, very long waiting times, staff were all telling us different directions to go, no boxes to put our valuables in to get scanned then when the boxes did appear they would throw them at the tourists, very rude service I was in disbelief. We got questioned if we were Muslim and Arab which I don't see why. There were countless security and bag checks it was never ending and disorganised. I couldn't wait to get out of there. Worst experience of my life and I've been to Hurghada and Cairo they were just as bad, but Sharm was the worst of them. It needs major improvement.

This is the worst airport I've ever passed through; after a lovely 10 days holiday, leaving was a horrible experience. Security checks are confusing, performative and numerous. The luggage scanning is baffling, with no trays to put valuables in, everybody yelling, and tricky to navigate for my 76 year old dad. He asked a boy for info, the boy helped us through a check, magicking up some trays, then demanded a tip. He did not want egyptian pounds but dollars, and rejected 5 dollars as too small. When I went to be scanned and was sent back because of my sunglasses, I was confused as there was nothing to put them in. I asked for a tray, eventually the woman threw it at me. The majority of staff seem to deeply despise passengers, and make sure you know it. It was a 6pm flight during Ramadan, so this may have been a factor. We had a lovely time in Dahab and were keen to return, but are unlikely to after this dehumanising experience.

The most awful airport I have ever travelled through. Whilst this airport portrays that it is very secure. I was far from impressed. At 2 points during security I was asked for money by the security officers when checking my bag, I was of the impression that this would have avoided being checked. I feel it’s only a matter of time before another serious incident happens at this airport. Will avoid Sharm El Sheikh ever again due to my experience at the airport. It was awful.

Our first experience at arrivals was a man in uniform stopping people enter the main terminal. Another man, not in uniform was offering fast track and a group agreed a Five pound charge which quickly inflated to €10 and the group were allowed to push past the waiting crowd into the departure area where the man then wanted more money to take them further which they refused and he disappeared! The official on the door was clearly aware of what was going on and assisted the whole scam. Management at the airport are obviously aware of this dangerous situation where backhanders open doors. We moved through the many stages of security with reasonable ease but can only agree with many comments regarding rudeness, disorganisation and incompetence. After passport control was another queue with 2 x uniformed officials shouting 'Come' to everyone. They were presumably there to double check the passports were stamped but didnt even look at my closed passport and ushered me through with 'Go!' The chaos and slack attitude throughout will sadly lead to another tragedy one day

My experience at Sharm El Sheikh Airport was abysmal. The airport was severely disorganised, with a complete lack of structure, communication, and basic passenger management, which made the entire process unnecessarily stressful. The most disturbing part of my departure experience was an encounter with a security guard at approximately 6:30pm on January 30th. She shouted at me, repeatedly saying “hurry up, move quickly,” and spoke to me in a condescending manner by asking, “do you not understand English?” Despite my full cooperation, she aggressively snatched a grey security tray containing my personal belongings from my hands and attempted to intimidate me through her hostile and provoking behaviour. I have travelled extensively across many countries and have never experienced treatment like this at an airport. Behaviour of this nature—whether from this individual or anyone of a similar calibre—is completely unacceptable in an international gateway. Individuals who conduct themselves this way do not deserve to be in positions that involve direct contact with travellers, as their actions leave a lasting negative impression and actively damage tourism.  While the resorts themselves may be nice, an experience like this overshadows everything else. Unless there is a serious improvement in professionalism, respect, and accountability, this country does not deserve to benefit from the currency and goodwill of international tourists.

Had a magic week at the Four Seasons in Sharm with superb facilities and staff who truly understand the meaning of customer care. That was until our flight home. Sharm El Sheikh Airport is an absolute shambles from start to finish. It combines absurd, performative security with rude, surly staff and a level of organisational chaos that would embarrass a provincial bus station. The security theatre is relentless and pointless. Endless queues, repeated bag checks, arbitrary rules applied differently every five minutes, and officials who seem far more interested in asserting authority than keeping anyone safe. You’re screened, re-screened, and then screened again. Not because it makes sense, but because no one appears to know (or care) what the process actually is. Staff attitude is consistently hostile and rude. Basic courtesy is absent. Questions are met with scowls, shrugs, or barking orders. Any notion that passengers are even human beings has clearly been abandoned. The default tone is irritation, as though your presence is an inconvenience rather than the entire reason the airport exists. Organisation is nonexistent. Queues merge into other queues with no signage, no explanation, and no accountability.  We queued in one lengthy line for ages only to be told that our printed easy jet boarding passes which Easy jet said should be used were refused and we had to go back for and old fashioned flight ticket and queue again. There is no technology whatsoever.Gates change without warning. It is chaotic, unfriendly, and deeply unpleasant, and it leaves visitors with the unmistakable impression that hospitality, and basic professionalism are entirely optional here. Easy jet were equally hopeless as by the time we got to the lounge it had overbooked the flight and left two hours late.

Chaos. No queue management for check in desks. Hardly any staff and desks open. No information. People in the queues whose flights were leaving in literal minutes. Flights held. Then one cancelled due to pilot going over flying hours. Once checked in, hardly any staff or departure boards. Hold ups at security checks. No one in a rush. No one to ask about flight departure. By this point passports checks 5 times. Get to gate, can’t get into  gate. Only one person checking passports for 4 flights. Two more passport checks. Once through, no information. No one to ask. Followed by conflicting or misinformation followed by nothing! Eventually a British guy did some investigation, stood on a seat and shouted which gates and queues were which. Got on the bus and have just been taken to the wrong plane! Driver seems to have no idea where we should be going Still in Sharm. If we get out it’ll be a miracle. Oh and no WiFi.

Worst experience ever.  1 hour before departure we were not even allowed to enter in the airport. Instead of helping they made us to miss our flight along with other passengers. Luggage check up is done twice , passport check up 3 times, also security and immigration expectations are very confusing. It ruined the last day our holiday. Inside is no drinking water and half liter bottled water is 5 euro. Also is never stated that the online boarding pass is not valid (this is also carrier mistake).

I had a very disappointing experience at this airport. The security lines were extremely long, and there was little communication from staff about delays. The terminal felt overcrowded, seating was difficult to find, and several areas were not as clean as expected.

One of the cleanest, most efficient airports I have ever been through. I have been through this airport twice (terminal 2) and it's been fairly quick, and friction free. Plenty of shops, restaurants, and coffee shops. Staff are efficient. Maybe not overly friendly as some people might want but they get things done.

My experience in terminal 1 was generally pretty good. Other than a rude member of staff at Subway (not really the airport's fault) and some unfriendly customs staff (which seems to happen at a lot of airport), everything went pretty smoothly. Lines were short; there were plenty of places to get water; the terminal wasn't too crowded and it was easy to find quiet spots in which to relax before my flight; there was a good range of shops and restaurants; and toilets were plentiful and clean. Perhaps I was just lucky and it is always hard to judge an airport from just one experience, but I found the airport to be functional and easy to use.

Worst airport I've been to. Dirty, people rude, toilet with no paper. I had a priority ticket, when I asked they didn't even reply to me. Nobody was is the priority line to validate the tickets. When I reached there from the normal line, the guy in the control ironically told me "it doesn't matter".

Very clean, though lines at immigration can be slow due to excessive paperwork. It’s big and spacious, but quite far from town, expect at least an hour by car. There are plenty of ATMs to choose from. Snack bars and restaurants are overpriced, so come prepared. Security is tight; they were fussy about my power bank and a 50 ml deodorant. Apart from that, it was a good experience.

I lost my bag at Incheon Airport on January 15. After I returned to Singapore and realized it, I immediately contacted the airport’s Lost & Found via email. At the same time, I also reached out to Singapore Airlines for assistance. Singapore Airlines was extremely helpful and proactive. They arranged for a staff member to go to the airport with a copy of my passport and an authorization letter to collect the bag on my behalf, and even offered to send it back to Singapore for me. However, the Lost & Found at Incheon Airport refused to release my bag to them. They requested that I email them the passport details of the Singapore Airlines staff, which I promptly did. After that, there was no response at all. As of today (April 10), I have still not received any reply or update. I am very disappointed with the inefficiency and lack of communication. If such a simple matter cannot be handled properly, it raises serious concerns about the overall service standards of the airport.

I can only describe my experience as an unpleasant trip. The people at the airport seemed very rude. They spoke in their own language, and when I tried to communicate in English, they would roll their eyes and respond in a loud, unfriendly manner. At one point, I needed information about passport control. When I approached a staff member, she simply shouted that it was closed and would reopen in two hours, without offering any further help or guidance and totally unpleasant way to say that. Overall, the staff across the airport came across as unhelpful and discourteous. Even though I had priority status, the service I received did not reflect that and was noticeably worse compared to my experiences in other European airports. The overall level of service at this airport was extremely poor they don’t care about nobody and they show it extremely clearly

It is an airport to really avoid if you have an alternative to use inboud and outbound. £60.00 to park a car is simply a rip off, they have all passengers by the short and curlies and they abuse it at every opportunity.
The waiting area is appalling. Two hours waiting for security is appalling. The free Wi-Fi doesn’t work and is connected to advertisers. No wonder the reviews mention the same things

Extremely disappointed. I have visited Changi on many occasions and to date it has always been a pleasant experience. Today I am in transit for over 8.5 hours. First 5 mins I order large coffee at T3 The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf. I have a small macaroon with me to have with coffee and am told I'm not allowed to eat at the table. The coffee was not good, plastic was used, and it wasn't reasonably priced. I leave coffee and with still 8 hrs to go I go to Free Singapore Tour desk. when my turn on queue comes, I move forward and a boy walks in front of me to the counter. The young man serves him straight away without acknowledging me at all. When the boy finally leaves, the young man calls me over, sights my boarding pass, and says I don't have enough time to take tour. Really? Disgusted. Transit via Malaysia in the future.
This airport clearly falls short. Limited facilities on departure side in the Public Area, with uncomfortable seating and amenities. Wayfinding can be difficult.
The worst security staff I have ever experienced. Utterly rude.  The person I dealt with was literally shouting without any reason.

I had a fractured leg in a plaster cast and was unable to walk, so wheelchair assistance had been requested in advance. Upon arriving at the airport entrance, I was informed that wheelchair assistance would be available after reaching the check-in counter. My friends had to search to find someone willing to help. The first staff member they approached refused assistance because my friends were not travelling with me. Eventually, another staff member helped us locate a wheelchair. Unfortunately, the wheelchair had no safety belt, no armrests, and no support to elevate my injured leg.  At the IndiGo check-in counter, my friend politely asked whether I could be assigned a seat with extra legroom so I could elevate my injured leg but the IndiGo staff appeared irritated by the request and said that the seat could not be changed because it had already been auto-assigned.  We were asked to return to the counter again at 6:30 PM for wheelchair escort to the gate. When we returned, the wheelchair operator refused to assist with my backpack and insisted that I keep it on my lap. When I requested a brief stop to refill my water bottle before boarding, this request was ignored.  Overall, this was a very distressing experience.

I have been to Changi airport so many times I have lost count, but to me it is always of a very high standard in every way. Finding your way around is very easy. Staff are very approachable and helpful. The airport is always very clean, including the bathrooms, which seem to have staff monitoring them all the time. There is a great choice of shopping, and transit between the terminals on the Skyrail is quick, and the trains are frequent. There is an excellent choice of foods available, although I think sometimes the signage to the food hall on Level 1 could be a little better. Still one of my favorite airports.

Sphinx International Airport is near the Sphinx and the pyramids on the east side of the city, so if you stay in Giza or go towards Alexandria this airport is much better located than the main airport. It's used by low cost airlines like Easyjet or Pegasus. Terminal is nicely decorated with ancient Egyptian figures and it's easy to navigate since it's not very big. Before passport control there are several bank and money exchange offices where you can buy the visa if needed and also several atm. Immigration took quite long so try to be in front of the queue. When taking uber from the airport they will charge more than what app suggest since airport is outside city limits

St. Thomas airport has to be one of the worst airports. The long lines due to TSA funding aside, the airport itself is old, does not have enough seating for the number of people going through it, and does not have AC, so you will sit, or stand due to lack of seating, and sweat. There are some fans but not enough for all the people crammed together as one could barely move around. It would be nice to have a cold drink while you sit/stand and sweat, but the only cold drinks to be found in the airport, at least on the day I departed, were alcoholic beverages. The water, while priced similar to other airports, was warm, as were many of the non-alcoholic drinks. Maybe the airport is better in months others than March, but while St. Thomas was nice, and the people were super friendly, I wouldn’t recommend this destination unless you arrive and depart by cruise ship.

Terrible infrastructure, inefficiency in the planning and layout of the airport, poor signage, understaffed security. It is more like a shopping mall rather than an airport. If you have a flight from the C gates, plan for at least 25 to 30 minutes walking.

The only positive thing about Terminal 2 at Stockholm Airport was that it was relatively easy to get to the gate and it is relatively clean though number of seating available is not great. Unfortunately, almost everything else about the experience was stressful and disappointing. The biggest issue is that the terminal simply does not appear to have enough security screening positions available for the number of passengers using it. The process moved extremely slowly, partly because almost every other bag was being manually searched — including for very ordinary items like an electric toothbrush. What made this even worse was that these searches were happening directly on the main belt instead of in a separate inspection area, causing delays for everyone behind. Some of the security staff were also unnecessarily rude during searches, not just to me but to several people around me. On top of that, the scanners are still not the newer 3D scanners used in many modern airports. Because of this, I had to throw away several items simply to make everything fit into the small liquids plastic bag requirement that many other European airports have already removed with updated scanners. I was told I could instead go back and check in my bag, but given the already massive queues, the slow-moving process, and the fact that my flight was already delayed with a connection to make, that simply wasn’t realistic. Things got even more frustrating at the gate for my British Airways flight. The gate agents forced everyone in groups 4 and 5 to check in their cabin bags, making it compulsory even after I explained that I had already thrown items away specifically to keep my bag with me because of my delayed connection and onward travel plans. They insisted there was no overhead space left because the flight was full. However, once onboard, it was obvious that this was not true. Around half of the overhead bins were completely empty. This flight also had the newer larger overhead bins designed to accommodate more luggage, so clearly not everyone needed to check their bags. The whole process felt disproportionately aggressive and poorly managed. Overall, the experience felt unnecessarily stressful from start to finish and left a very negative impression of both the terminal and the handling of passengers.
Just waited 45 mins to get through passport control and we are on EU passports. Took that long just to get to the long part of the corridor that had a sign for separate EU and non EU.

Terminal 2 currently offers a tired and worn experience that feels neglected compared to the rest of the airport. The primary issue is a security process that lacks the logical flow expected of a major hub. The main friction point is the Fast Track merging system. Unlike terminals with a dedicated conveyor belt for priority passengers, Terminal 2 forces a merge at the very end of the line. This requires staff to constantly interrupt the standard queue to allow priority travelers through, creating a frustrated and tense atmosphere for everyone involved. The process feels arbitrary and inefficient rather than a premium service. Until the infrastructure is updated to include a dedicated screening flow, the current setup remains a significant deterrent. It is a disappointing start to a trip and makes it difficult to justify choosing carriers like KLM or Air France that are restricted to this terminal.

Extremely bad experience upon arrival at Arlanda. I was traveling alone with a 3-month-old baby and received basically no help at all. At other airports in the EU – especially in Athens – the staff do their best to help, especially when traveling with small children. Here it was the opposite. When I asked for help, the staff instead started picking up other luggage on the same trolley and made no attempt to even check if my stroller was on the special baggage belt. The service was unprofessional and completely without understanding the situation. Traveling alone with a baby is already challenging enough – then you expect at least basic service. Arlanda is far behind other airports when it comes to customer service. Take a lesson from how it works in Athens. Very disappointed Extremt dålig upplevelse vid ankomst till Arlanda. Jag reste ensam med en 3 månader gammal bebis och fick i princip ingen hjälp alls. På andra flygplatser inom EU – särskilt i Aten – gör personalen sitt bästa för att hjälpa till, särskilt när man reser med små barn. Här var det tvärtom. När jag bad om hjälp började personalen istället plocka med annat bagage på samma vagn och gjorde inget försök att ens kontrollera om min barnvagn fanns på specialbagagebandet. Bemötandet var oprofessionellt och helt utan förståelse för situationen. Att resa ensam med en bebis är redan tillräckligt utmanande – då förväntar man sig åtminstone grundläggande service. Arlanda ligger långt efter andra flygplatser när det gäller kundservice. Ta lärdom av hur det fungerar i Aten. Mycket besviken.

The departure experience has improved (queueing) and facilities are good. Free WiFi. There are plenty of shops which have reasonable prices. Lots of eating options. Lots of seating and toilets. Few runway delays.

Security at Terminal 2 in Stockholm was one of the most unprofessional airport experiences I’ve had. The staff were cold, dismissive, and unnecessarily rude. There was no calm explanation of rules — just abrupt instructions and an attitude that made an already stressful process worse. Several of my very expensive skincare items were confiscated, despite not being liquids in the typical sense and never having been an issue at other airports. When I tried to understand what rule they were applying, I was completely shut down instead of being given a clear explanation. What made this even more frustrating was the inconsistency. My husband had items over 100ml that were not questioned at all, while my belongings were closely scrutinized and removed. It’s hard not to feel singled out when rules appear to be applied selectively depending on the person or the item. I respect security regulations and am happy to follow them when they’re explained properly. What’s unacceptable is the combination of rude behaviour, poor communication, and inconsistent enforcement. It leaves passengers feeling frustrated and unfairly treated. A little professionalism and basic courtesy would go a long way

I believe disability badges should be a huge priority as in London it is taken very seriously. I had come to the front with my mother and asked kindly to be let through because of her disability with proof of her badge in hand. The workers at the desk caused a pointless fuss and a horrible attitude for no reason. After 5 mins they let us through and the staff started giving comments about how this is Sweden and not London when blue badge signs are all over the airport? Poor behaviour this is such a horrible airport.

I gave a great review last week as passport control to exit had improved last time but today it was back to the understaffed with long lines again. It was so bad that flights got delayed as passengers stuck, in particular in the non EU lane. Other wise the airport is okay WiFi has been reduced to one hour per 24 hours unless you pay for the premium option.

Surigao is a small regional airport in the Mindinao region of the Philippines. I believe that it only handles a few flights each day. Despite this, I was more than welcomed on my last visit. Don't expect too much of the airport, because as I say it is small. Staff were very polite, fast, and welcoming. These were people who are obviously proud of their city, and happy to see tourists. Everybody was especially happy and welcoming for the Christmas period. It's a lovely airport to arrive and depart from.

Taipei Taoyuan Airport signs and instructions are often not clear and easy to understand. Using easily recognizable colors would help passengers find their way quickly. The existing signs are white with black text. I suggest they be changed to black with white text or black with yellow text.

This is an excellent airport. Recently the airport has added a new boarding concourse and this upgrade makes a remarkable difference. The new concourse is modern, spacious, and well designed, with clearer signage, smoother passenger flow, and a much more comfortable atmosphere compared to before

TSA at Tampa airport is an absolute joke. Made me throw away my water bottle for having a little water in it. They had almost no water emptying stations said I could either go back through security or throw away the bottle.

I genuinely enjoy traveling through this airport. Getting to and from the airport is excellent. Drop-off and pick-up areas are close to the terminal, well-organized, and security doesn’t rush drivers to leave. There are also designated handicap drop-off and pick-up spots, which is a big plus. Signage throughout the airport is clear and easy to follow. Check-in and security are generally smooth. There are self-service kiosks, and the staffed counters are usually efficient—though this can depend on the airline. I’ve personally had issues with JetBlue staff and counters in the past. Security wait times aren’t terrible; while lines can look long, they move consistently. Overall, TPA has the smoothest security process of any airport I’ve been to. Staff attitude is usually good. You might occasionally encounter a bad staff member, but that happens everywhere. The airport itself is very well organized and thoughtfully designed. After check-in, you take an elevator up to a central hub with restaurants, seating, and artwork. Each terminal is clearly marked with large letters in each corner, making it very easy to find the correct sky tram. Terminal layout and navigation are excellent. Gates are easy to find, walking distances are shorter than most large airports, and the sky trams are efficient and convenient. The airport is very clean, restrooms are well maintained, and seating availability is great. There’s plenty of comfortable seating throughout the terminals. Food and shopping options are good overall. There’s a decent variety of food, but as a vegetarian, I find the options somewhat limited at many restaurants. Food prices are high, which is expected for an airport. Shops are typical airport stores with souvenirs and essentials—nothing special, and everything is pricey like most airports. Wi-Fi quality is excellent and easy to connect to. Charging outlets are available throughout the airport, though they tend to fill up quickly. Delays do happen, but they’re usually weather-related due to frequent Florida storms. When delays occur, departures are paused for safety reasons. Gate changes and delays due to poor airport management are rare, which is a big positive. Baggage claim is very well designed. There’s plenty of space around the belts so people aren’t crowded, and the belts are low to the ground, making it easier to lift heavy bags. Overall, Tampa International Airport is modern, efficient, and well structured. The entire process feels smooth and organized, and I consistently have good experiences here. I highly recommend this airport.

My most recent experience at Tashkent airport was absolutely unacceptable and deeply offensive. Upon arrival, I purchased a SIM card and was told that my phone had to be registered with the authorities. I was directed to a specific counter for phone registration. The officer who attended to me was rude and hostile. When I asked for the registration form, he handed me a form written entirely in Russian. As a foreign tourist, I asked politely if there was an English version. Instead of responding professionally, he shouted at me and aggressively told me that there was no English form.  The telecom staff later confirmed that an English form did exist and helped me complete it. When I returned to the same officer, his behaviour became even worse. He shouted at me again when asking for my passport. After entering my details into the system, he threw my passport back at me. The staff show no sense of professionalism, accountability, or human courtesy. There is a serious lack of service culture, and incidents like this make it very clear why many tourists leave with a negative impression. If Uzbekistan genuinely wants to attract international tourists, the country must urgently address the behaviour, attitude, and training of airport staff.
Again only one counter open for two flight arrivals - unbelievable. They can’t open a second counter. And the person at the desk is so rude. The worst airport I have ever experienced.
The new airport is modern, light-filled, with excellent infrastructure and lovely staff. Everything is easy to navigate, and it is spotless.

Techo International Airport is a new airport built with Chinese assistance. Very clean, with short lines if you have an approved eVisa. It’s big and spacious, though quite far from town—expect at least an hour by car. There are lots of ATMs to choose from. Taking into consideration landing, immigration, customs, SIM card purchase, and money exchange, I was outside the airport in a maximum of 30 minutes. Totally recommended.

We flew into Sydney Airport on 28th January 2026 after a 10-hour overnight from Bangkok. I had booked a wheelchair for my elderly mother who is unable to walk long distances or has difficulties using stairs due to a bad knee. We landed at 8am and we, along with 4 groups of passengers who had also booked wheelchair support, did not leave the aircraft until 9.30am. In effect, we did not clear customs until 11am. The disability and mobility support at Sydney international airport is a disgrace and made me feel embarrassed of the welcome or lack of welcome Australia extends to arrivals. Although I had booked the wheelchair service several days ahead of the journey, our request felt like a nuisance and a burden. Whilst the grounds staff were polite and trying to do their best, we kept hearing the same excuses being used - the airport deals with 30-40 flights every morning (due to the curfew), we only have one wheelchair bus, we don't have enough wheelchairs, and the list of excuses goes on. The whole process feels uncoordinated, and some aspects don't make sense, e.g., elderly passengers had to walk (or rather slowly shuffle) off the bus into the building where staff and wheelchairs were waiting. Why not meet the passengers with the wheelchairs at the exit of the bus? This is the usual practice at other airports. If this is a daily occurrence, then it is inexcusable to say that the airport is caught unaware. Why not use the booking data to ensure there is adequate surge capacity to support the requests?  The whole experience is so avoidable. Australia can do better and must do better given its significantly ageing population.

This airport does not provide an adequate service for people with mobility difficulties. I arrived at Sydney after a domestic flight from Cairns and as requested was helped with a wheelchair. But when we got to the baggage reclaim area I was told that I had to get up as it was not allowed to take the wheelchair any further. I was told that to get to Terminal 1 for my next flight I had to walk up a ramp and leave the terminal, cross a road and walk to the bus stop. There was no interest in could I do this!, nor of how to cope with the luggage. I did manage to get to the bus stop with some difficulty and the bus took us to Terminal 1 but instead of stopping in the middle it went to the extreme end near check in H. There was no assistance desk at this entrance, there were 2 wheelchairs but they were locked together. My check in was C and it is a very long building. Eventually near F we found an abandoned wheelchair and some passers by helped push our trolley while my husband pushed me. I think the management board should spend a day in their airport acting as people who are disabled. Why couldn't the first wheelchair take me to the bus stop? Why couldn't the bus stop at the main entrance? Why wasn't there an assistance reception desk at the entrance?
Flew with AC to Canada. Terminal was in ok condition but the never ending duty free department was intimidating. Nice gate lounge and food was expensive but good.
Flew with AC to Canada. Terminal was in ok condition but the never ending duty free department was intimidating. Nice gate lounge and food was expensive but good.

Sydney Kingsford airport was by far the best airport in Australia in my opinion. Flight landed at 8am on 29/08/2013 walked through immigration smoothly. Collected my luggage from the conveyer after only a ten-minutes wait. The custom was one of the most efficient one I have ever encountered no time wasted and most importantly with a smile. I was outside the airport 20-25 minutes after I walked off of my plane.

Collected my luggage from the conveyer after only a ten-minutes wait. The custom was one of the most efficient one I have ever encountered no time wasted and most importantly with a smile. I was outside the airport 20-25 minutes after I walked off of my plane.
Landed from KUL at 2015 left the terminal at 2035! The place was totally deserted quite a comparison to the morning rush of arrivals. Totally recommend evening arrivals if at all possible.
Landed from KUL at 2015 left the terminal at 2035! The place was totally deserted quite a comparison to the morning rush of arrivals. Totally recommend evening arrivals if at all possible.

Arrived from Melbourne at domestic terminal. Relatively short walk from gate to exit and going downstairs to await luggage. Late change of luggage carousel had everyone scurrying. Unimpressed though that there were no signs up saying that airport train was only going to central and that you then needed to take a bus to your final station if we'd know that we'd have taken a taxi straight to hotel. Different story though when flying out to NZ. Taxi dropped us off near Air NZ check in desks so that part was a breeze then headed through to the horror of passport control and security. I'll never moan about queuing in the UK/US again after what we faced here 12 lanes of snaking back and forth to get through passport control (4 lanes) and security (7 lanes). I'm so glad we had checked in early enough unlike others around us who hadn't and were panicking they'd miss their flight. Then we had a very long hike through duty free/other shops to where our gate was.

My latest arrival here was pretty ordinary. Long queues for immigration a mess with smart gate. The long queues for customs were also a dog's breakfast. 50 minutes to get out then there was the would experience of the transfer bus. The queue there sneaked right outside the buses were irregular and very inefficient waiting 20 minutes. No apologies and the usual curt comments from staff.

My latest arrival here was pretty ordinary. Long queues for immigration a mess with smart gate. Arrived in Sydney on 8th June (morning). We followed the sign to the immigration counter. We saw a long queue inside the immigration area. Having arrived from London we were treated to chaos in the customs area. Having been in London for 3 years I was shocked but the lack of forethought that had gone into the redesign of the area. Signs did not give accurate indications of where to stand particularly when there were crowds doors opens into queues the microchip scanning only works 50 percent of the time and seemed to have been designed by someone who assumed only 4 or 5 people would be using the service at one time. Staff couldn't care less that the scanning area was ineffective and that people were wandering around looking for assistance when the automatic machine wouldn't allow them to pass through. After queuing for the auto machines I was told the queue for assistance I then had to join wouldn't take long. Having seen the people in the standard queue who exited the plane with me leave the customs area I then had to stay for another 15 minutes. When I got to the front of the queue there was no apology or explanation for the delay or malfunction of the equipment in fact the woman was chatting to the other woman next to her about her weekend. Se was rude and when I didn't utter a word when my passport was handed back she commented to her friend that I wasn't very happy in a sarcastic tone. Out in the baggage collection the same issue with snaking queues and lack of movement was evident. The entire design seemed to be based on creating collisions with no forethought to the fact that people had to push huge trolleys throw queues of people with huge trolleys. Unsurprisingly the woman directing us to aisles for baggage checks was equally obnoxious. There seemed to be no supervision of the staff who couldn't have cared less about providing any sort of service. ve no customer service aptitude to employ.

I used SYD last month for flights to and from the U.S. As a departure airport Sydney International is an airport of contrasts. For example the nice leather lounges with the recharging stations and the high ceiling in the central space feels just great. However as you near your gate the ceiling becomes really low and you will find many people just standing around because the seating is far from adequate given the number of passengers. The free wifi has a fairly strong signal throughout the terminal. As an arrival airport the new SmartGate system definitely speeds up the immigration part of the process. After that it all becomes a bit more interesting. The problem seems to be that there is not enough floor space between the end of the baggage claim carousels and the customs area. When a couple of jumbos are on the ground there are long lines wrapped all along the backside of the baggage claim area. To combat the confusion I looked for the least busy carousel and then picked a customs line close to it. That strategy paid off though it took some creative weaving around other passengers and walking the long way around nearly all of the carousels to make it happen. It was all worth it in the end. I was on my Route 400 bus outside an hour and fifteen minutes after my plane's arrival. The bottom line: Sydney is one busy airport that services a large percentage of Australia's 20 million people. Be prepared to wait and go with the flow. What the airport may lack in affordable parking it more than makes up for in its CityRail train station downstairs and even handier bus stops upstairs.

I use Sydney on a regular basis and I like the airport but it does have its drawbacks. I have to mention the staff Check in and passport staff have always been friendly and helpful however that cant be said for the security staff who always are surly and unhelpful. International departures can get crowded and its not helped by a needless shopping area. There's far too many of them and they are all of the expensive variety including the food outlets. Once checked in you head for security and line up via a maze of lanes that are roped off. Fine when its busy but when its quiet why they don't provide a more direct route to the desks is beyond me. Once through security you head through yet more expensive shops to the gates. Your departure gate will dictate how much walking you have to do. If you need food or drinks be prepared because it is expensive. International arrivals is much the same but in reverse. You head through a shopping complex to reach passport control via another roped off maze and then onto the baggage hall. I've always been lucky and got my bags swiftly. Arrivals hall is always busy and its not helped by more shops! Depending on your destination will dictate what happens next. Buses / taxis etc are within easy reach and the hall is underneath International departures. If you have arrived off an International flight and want domestic its not so easy as the domestic terminals are the other side of the airport. These can be reached in a variety of ways and this is where Sydney lets itself down (other than the shops!). There is a train that you pay for that takes two minutes but you have to walk the length of the terminal and down a set of escalators because of where the arrival exit has been placed. You can also get a bus which are often crowded. The third option is a taxi. Whatever option you choose try and give yourself plenty of time it gets very busy at peak times. I should also mention that the approaches to the airport like the rest of Sydney can get very busy so also leave yourself plenty of time. In summary I like Sydney but there's far to many shops and arrivals especially if you need to transfer could definitely be improved. Walking the length of the terminal to get to the bus / train is not ideal - maybe they designed it that way to get you to walk past the shops!
