This airport needs some serious work. At almost every juncture, rude staff, stressful and poorly instructed queues, terrible security with staff arguing amongst themselves with no regard for customers, and passport control staff screaming completely unintelligible instructions and then becoming aggressive when no one understands them. We watched families being split up as the automated passport terminals didn’t work repeatedly, people falling over each other and the border control leaving their booths to scream at people to “get back”. Once eventually through, food services ran out of food and the seating was littered with families trying to console upset children and console themselves after the trauma of the whole process.  A lively Island but would we come again or go somewhere else? Probably go somewhere else where the are welcomed coming in and thanked going out for choosing this beautiful place as your holiday of choice. Utterly terrible for your reputation and that’s not something I say lightly.

Totally inadequate staffing levels to process passengers both in and out of passport control. Massive queues entering and leaving. I saw only 1 person trying to organise thousands of passengers queuing the length of the airport leading to chaotic scenes and unacceptable amounts of time in queues, a total of around 4.5 -5 hours wasted just queuing. If this situation isn’t resolved then I for one will not go back again.

Extremely chaotic, biometric machines that are constantly breaking down, no staff members for help and staff don't speak good enough English to communicate. As well as that, extremely rude border control staff. Completely unprofessional. TFS needs investigating.

The airport is these days more modernized, especially the security and bordercheck. Staff is generally friendly amd speaks English well enough. There's the usual duty-free overpriced stores and a large food & beverages section. Prices there are lower compared to EU countries. Transport to the city is done by taxis or busses, beware of taxi scams. Travel time to town van easily take 1hr or more during rush hour.

This airport is located far away from the city centre. The walk from gate to immigration was long and queue for arrival was very long. The automated gates for customs were closed when I visited. Departure offered a better experience with shorter queues for security.
Worst airport immigration line. Very chaotic lines and no difference if having pre filled the arrival QR. It should have been a fast process but it took about 1 hour 30 mins in total.

My recent experience landing at terminal 3 was awful. The difficulties started at immigration. For some reason those who were residents (foreign residents) had to join a much longer line than those who were tourists. It is usually the opposite (as it should be since residents pay tax and Japan is their home). It felt quite bad for tourists to whiz through while residents had to wait in a long and fairly slow moving line. When I asked why this was the case, the staff were not able to understand my question. This was an issue every step of the way - immigration, customs, and baggage claim. I don't understand why an airport would assign staff to work at the international terminal who cannot understand English. Given that I had waited so long at immigration, and knowing that Haneda is usually very quick with getting luggage to the baggage claim area, I expected that my bags would be waiting for me when I got there. However, it was another long wait before my bag arrived. I know this may seem normal for most airports. However, as I have said, bags are usually very quick at Haneda - which prides itself on being a 'five-star' airport. Given that I had already waited a long time at immigration, a further lengthy wait is not normal for Haneda, nor was it five-star service. I have no idea why the wait was so much longer than usual since the airport was no busier than usual. The real drama began at customs which was absolute chaos. I had completed my customs form online, which normally means a very quick and smooth progression through customs. However, I was met with crowds of people and utterly confusing signage. There were also some staff yelling incomprehensible messages. Many people were very confused. I asked one member of staff which line I should join. However, she rudely pointed at the sign and muttered something incomprehensible. I wouldn't have asked her if I understood the sign! I therefore joined the line that seemed to be for those who had completed their forms online. However, when I got to the front, I was told to go to a machine (which had yet another long line) and to scan my passport and check some information on the screen. What was the point to complete the customs form online to just have to do it all again at the airport? I then had to come back and join the long line that I had been in previously, and, once I got to the front, I was finally allowed to enter the country. One saving grace was that the customs officer at the check was very friendly and gave a nice welcome. To conclude, the whole procedure from getting off the plane to getting through customs was a complete shambles. It left me feeling stressed and unhappy. I have no idea what went wrong since Haneda is usually a pleasure to use. I sincerely hope it was just a temporary blip and that things get back to their usual level of efficiency soon. However, if I was a first time visitor to Japan, everything would have made an extremely bad first impression. Also, the fact that residents were treated much more poorly than tourists left me with a very bad feeling.

At check in, the conveyer belt shut down multiple times so the staff eventually shut it off and gave up (no communication about these issues with the customers, we were left clueless for an hour). So they decided to get everyone to check in and get baggage tags and to load our bags on crates promising they would end up loaded on the planes. At this point our flight is already delayed as no one was able to board until the original departure time. Then we sat on the plane for 45 minutes as the flight crew said we were “waiting for the bags”. We were then informed that the bags weren’t able to be transported from the building and onto the plane so we have to take off without them. The staff are expecting us to now arrive in Dublin airport and report our luggage as lost and see if we can get the bags shipped to our addresses, no further help from the airport. I would recommend avoiding Turin Airport.

The method of transferring from outside Schengen (Svalbard) into Schengen is clumsy at best and clumsy and slow at worst. There were not enough people to take in the transferred luggage and luggage could not be scanned with the self-scanners. In addition, the security line was a mess! There were hundreds of people trying to get to flights and only two security lines. The staff working there were not good about pushing people through and there seemed to be a lot of many manual scans. It was the worst security line I’ve ever been through.

Varna is clean, tidy and efficient with a good duty free shop considering its size. The one major thing that let's it down for me, is the complete lack of drinking water for refills. Instead they expect you to pay an over exuberant price for another plastic bottle to end up in landfill. Come on Varna, get your act together! One more slight disappointment was the attitude of the 2 young women on the entrance to departures, far more interested in chatting to each other than carrying out their duties. Shame.

No complaints from me. Departure and arrival were stress free, breezed through security both legs, found staff polite and efficient. The UP express train is an excellent service to and from Pearson, fast and sensibly priced. I wasn't totally sold on the city of Toronto itself but the airport was a joy to use.

The airport was well connected to the city by public transportation such as UP Express and bus. Generally, it was clean. The lounges were badly located at the end of Concourse C, we had to travel all the way from Concourse B to there and back.  The Infield Concourse was too far from the main Terminal 3 without any train connected. The food at the Infield Concourse was very expensive.

So we fill up our info on the ArriveCan app, thinking we just zip through the express lane. When we line up for the Express lanes there is a staff who supposedly is there to assist people she kept yelling at some older folk, then she started yelling at the general public that the kiosk was meant for each individual. This staff had no manners, terrible customer service skills. I am not even sure how or why she was employed. When were finally exited the CBS agent at the final exit said why do you guys have two forms you could have just used one. Well that is not what the very bright staff who was supposed to assist at the kiosk was telling people.

My husband and I were flying from Mexico City to Ottawa, where we live. We normally avoid transiting through Pearson whenever possible, but this time we had no choice. Our flight from Mexico City was delayed due to aircraft issues, leaving us with just two hours to make our connection. In theory, this should have been manageable. In reality, it was not. We were required to clear customs, collect our luggage, recheck it, go back through security, and then reach our gate — an extremely inefficient and time-consuming process. To make matters worse, baggage delivery was delayed because multiple flights arrived simultaneously, overwhelming the system. It quickly became clear that we would not make our connection. Given the high likelihood that rechecking our suitcase would result in us being stranded overnight, we made the difficult decision to have a family member drive four hours from Ottawa to pick us up.

I missed my flight after having to spend more than 1H30 in the queue to get to the security check point, because only 2 check points were opened.  The staff that was there absolutely didn't do their job and didn't communicate to the plane staff this delay at security, causing half of the passengers of my flight, and many other passengers from other flights to just miss their flights. A serious change needs to be made at this airport, so the clients can get a decent service.

Its eponymous town is quite small but it's the entrepot for the famous falls. Thus it's a good airport, with all the usual facilities. Wifi, escalators sufficient gates, and jetbridges, not to mention its long runway. I had an easy passage from checkin to departures. No modern scanners, so liquids, shoes etc rules apply. Good staff. Downside: absence of departure/arrival boards.

Security / police rudest people I have ever encountered. For some reason my passport had an issue after passing through the scanner. Do I know the issue? No because at no point did the police officers told me. They just walked around with different scanner when I asked if there was an issue I was told 'we will let you know" - clearly they didn't. I smiled while watching them scanning and I was told not to laugh in a very rude way. What was I supposed to do when no information was given. Honestly love Italy, but probably the last time I'm coming to Verona

Extremely small airport, not enough connections through the main airports of Madrid and Barcelona. Not enough flights to main cities in Europe, waiting time for baggage delivery are the worst. Valencia deserves a much larger and better Airport with a lot more connections and direct flights.

We landed at the International arrivals section of the Vancouver Airport and began a very dysfunctional process. We came home from Puerto Vallarta, and that the document process with passport and declarations was much better than years gone by. The electronic scanning and declaration kiosks are excellent, and efficient. However that is where the efficiency stops. When you leave Mexico you go through the entire security process being scanned and your carry on bags are inspected. You are effectively examined and processed. So when you arrive, you are behind the security screen. In Vancouver though, there is a huge walk from international arrivals to domestic departures. That in itself is unavoidable, and understandable, That however is where the efficiency stops and the circus begins. There was a point where the airport instructs you to come from behind the security screened sites and you have to leave that area, and then go through security again to the domestic departure area.  When we left the secured area and arrived at the Security for section A B and C there was only one Security station out of six open. There were many many employees standing around the one station, and more could easily have been open. There were many people watching their flights on the screens while we stood in line for for the one station. We had to allow people that had flights leaving in 5 minutes to jump the line up and everyone in the line up allowed at least 25 people and I believe many more to go ahead for the one screening station. Remember that these people were international arrivals and were already behind the security screen before the inefficient process made them come out. If they were not already behind the security wall it is understandable that they would be screened before a flight, however because they were behind the screen this was a stupid and unnecessary duplication of services, and a waste of time, and delayed flights. Then they finally answered the crowd who were yelling at them to get more security screening stations opened and opened one more. This is a rude and unnecessary duplication of screening and it made flights delayed and people angry. This has been going on for many years. It is time for the Airport to fix this.

It is the slowest and most inefficient airport in Canada. Claiming your baggage might take more than 40 minutes close to 1h to get to the carousel. You need to plan your time accordingly, as it takes longer waiting to claim your baggage than in traffic on your way to you final destination.

This airport is located very close to the city center — and that’s about the only positive. It feels very outdated, like a model from the 1990s, and is in serious need of renovation. Check-in lines get long, so make sure to arrive early. Security and immigration can also be stressful, as you’re required to fill out a form. The staff in the shops seem extremely bored and often come across as rude or dismissive. Overall, this was my first and definitely my last visit.

I am required to use Vienna Airport quite a lot as a business class traveller and find it to be user friendly, modern and efficient apart from one exception. As I use Austrian Airlines regularly, I am disappointed by the frequent arrivals and departures relegated to a bus gate. That means that the aircraft parks at a position away from the terminal which results in a tedious bus transfer. No exception is made for business class travellers and although I may be able to embark or disembark from the aircraft as one of the first passengers, the experience is tedious. Passengers are jammed into busses like sardines. It is not fitting for an international airport with many connections. Upon arrival, one needs to wait until all passengers have disembarked before the bus actually makes its way to the terminal via a non-requested sightseeing tour of the airport.
It is clean and easily accessible by train about 20 minutes. The efficiency of check-in and security is high. Employees are friendly. The WiFi connection is good. Signposts are clear.
The lines at this airport are ridiculously long (check in and security). For a major tourist destination like Vienna, this really makes for a sour last experience. Some staff could be nicer as well.

We were supposed to depart from this airport on a connecting flight, but because the first flight was delayed, we had to leave the airport and change our tickets. LOT changed the tickets and told us that we should show them at the security check and we would be let through, or something along those lines. However, at the security check a guy told us to put our tickets in a tray and show what we had. We went through the entire security control that we had already gone through in Germany. When we told him that, he said, “This isn’t Germany,” and told us to throw away the cosmetics that were in the bag.

Do yourself a big favour and avoid this airport! We missed our flight due to queues at the security. Totally inefficient and chaotic. 5 flights leaving within a timeframe of 30 minutes and no capacity to handle the crowd. Rude employees barking at passengers. This is the worst airport I experienced in over 40 years of travel.

Terrible airport. There was complete mismanagement at the security which caused that many passengers of our flight missed it. No help at all from the airport and still not any reaction on our complaint about this. There was just one scanner available and this in peak holiday season. Our holiday was completely ruined by this Airport.

After flying in and out of IAD for 5 years the conclusion is plain - IAD is the worst airport in America. Pilots regularly abort landings. If you manage to land you have to wait 1-2 hours on average before the plane is ready to deboard. And that’s the best of it. The inside, and the remaining infrastructure of the airport is unchanged since the 60s. Looking for a water fountain, forget about it.

The worst customer service that I experience during my visit to Yerevan. If you ask any questions to airport employee no one knows anything. Not enough people to assist during TSA check in, they just announced cancellation of the flight and no one show up at the counter to assist customers with instruction what to do. Terrible customer service.

A nicely designed modern airport which generally operates smoothly in terms of staff and security checks. Food and beverages and duty-free shopping were abundant but overpriced. Transport to town is by frequent busses. All in all a great experience.

The airport, under this management, is practically fit for closure! Flights are crammed into one hour, followed by a two-hour layover. This causes massive congestion, lack of oxygen, and stress. There aren't enough seats at the gates. People are crammed together, and elderly people almost faint from standing in a stuffy crowd for two hours. Ground staff don't care about the well-being and safety of passengers. On January 10, 2025, after a Wizz Air flight from Malta landed, we waited half an hour for someone to clear the icy stairs. Two men arrived one after another, and the last one claimed they were somehow leaving Ryanair. We didn't know whether to laugh or cry. The staff clearly didn't want to clear the snow, as they chased us several hundred meters across the ice and snow to the airport entrance (no buses!). The lady who "led" us was walking from one foot to the other, as she was having a social phone conversation. She didn't let us overtake her by threatening her – it's 18 degrees Celsius on an icy airport, after all, and you can walk around.  Lotnisko w zasadzie przy takim zarządzie nadaje się tylko do zamknięcia!!! Loty są skomasowane w jedną godzinę, po czym następuje dwugodzinna przerwa w lotach. Powoduje to ogromny tłok, brak tlenu i stres. Nie ma wystarczającej ilości miejsc siedzących przy bramkach. Ludzie tłoczą się, a starsi prawie mdleją stojąc dwie godziny w tłumie o duchocie. Obsługa naziemna ma w nosie dobro i bezpieczeństwo pasażerów. W dniu 10.01.2025 po wylądowaniu samolotu z Malty Wizzair oczekiwaliśmy pół godziny żeby ktoś z obsługi uczynił oblodzone schody zdatnymi do zejścia. Przyszło po kolei 2 facetów i ostatni stwierdził, że jakoś z Ryanair wychodzą. Nie wiadomo było czy śmiać się czy płakać. Obsłudze najwyraźniej nie chce się odśnieżać, bo przegonili nas kilkaset metrów po lodzie i śniegu do wejścia do lotniska (autobusów brak!). Przy czy pani, która nas „prowadziła” szła z nóżki na nóżkę, bo prowadziła towarzyską rozmowę telefoniczną. Nie pozwalała się wyprzedzić strasząc - na oblodzonym lotnisku jest przecież 18 stopni i można sobie spacerować

What a horrible planning at this airport! Four of the sixteen security checks open on a Friday evening before Bank Holiday! The lines are immense, no air conditioning and people missing their flights. Seems management clearly forgot what to do in this case

Me and my husband arrived into Naples airport last evening at 8pm to a chaotic experience and on arrival we were herded into a makeshift tent-like construction to join a long queue to reach the automated machines, not all of which were operational. There were people to help, and a lot of people needed help to navigate the screen. We managed to complete my husbands and he was directed to the passport e-gates, he was through in 30 minutes. My attempt failed even with help and I had to go to manual passport check. I was greeted by a queue of hundreds of passengers. There was 1 kiosk open with 2 customs officials checking passports.  I shuffled along that queue for 3 hours with long periods not moving at all. The airport ‘closed’ at 10:30pm but at the time I got through there were still probably over 200 people waiting to be processed, that was 11:30pm. I love Italy and have visited many many times, but we won’t be coming any more unless this situation is resolved.

May 2026. When we landed we had to immediately join a queue of people waiting. Not knowing what the holdup was, I assumed it was just a short queue. Absolutely the opposite. When we turned around the corner we were met with what I can only describe as a holding pen. A massive snake of people, I would estimate around 300 people all waiting to get their passports checked and fingerprints scanned. Boiling hot. No toilets. Air conditioning units that didn't work. And staff that clearly were overwhelmed. It took an hour to get through. When we then went to collect our suitcase, it was nowhere to be seen. No staff, and due to the fact that it took so long to get through, all the suitcases were stacked up on top of each other. It took 30 minutes to locate our suitcases. I dont moan about many things. But I felt like a sheep being herded in a pen. When I complained to staff it was a simple shrug of the shoulders. The reason why we had to wait because of the new EES.

This is probably the worst organized airport I have ever been in. Once you walk in the main doors, there is only a screen to show you your flight with no additional information - no gate, no boarding time, not even an area to head towards. The staff look miserable and no staff available for directions or questions either. There is minimal seating and people are crowded in areas just standing. You are only given a gate number 25 minutes before boarding. The train station in Naples is much more organized and less crowded - take the train if possible!

I have been standing in a queue to board the plane for over 2 hours. My flight has not been delayed or cancelled and no one will tell us anything 1 person has managed to make it through so far I am not a parent but I have watched as multiple families struggle to take care of their children as there is no seats for anyone. This ridiculous.

Awful in every way. Fast track security is a joke. Too crowded generally and if you try to minimise your time sweating in the departure lounge sweating like everyone else don't but fast track as it is unmonitored and you have to fit with people in the normal queue who think you are pushing in. Very stressful.

This is the worst airport I have been in for the last 10 years. Total shambles at arrival with 2 hours to clear passport, 2 staff on duty shouting at passengers to do this, then stop, don’t do that. Border agent taking 3 minutes to slowly flick through a passport despite using an electronic machine to take biometric pictures and finger prints. Same shambles coming back, lengthy queue at passport control to again take biometric pictures and fingerprints for everyone. I have never know an airport to be this slow, disorganised and rude. The terminal itself is dirty, lounge is dirty with very poor choice and standard of food. I would give Pisa Airport a wide berth and fly anywhere else

Chicago O’Hare (ORD) continues to be one of the most frustrating airports I’ve ever traveled through. What should be a major international hub often feels like a constant exercise in chaos and poor organization. The airport’s size would be manageable if the infrastructure and operations kept pace, but too often passengers are left scrambling across terminals with little support. Customer service is a major issue, and communication is often inconsistent, leaving travelers to figure things out on their own. For an airport that handles millions of passengers each year, the overall experience frequently feels disorganized and reactive rather than efficient and proactive. Delays appear to be a near-daily occurrence, connections are missed. O’Hare has the potential to be a world-class airport, but until there is significant improvement in operations, communication, and passenger movement throughout the terminals, it remains a source of frustration for far too many travelers. Unfortunately, when I see ORD on my itinerary, I now expect delays, confusion, and unnecessary stress rather than a smooth travel experience.

Very crowded airport mid-morning. Arrived at Terminal 1 C concourse and Departed from Terminal 5. Since the Terminal Transfer Bus starts operation at 11:30. This meant taking the Airport Transit System Train from Terminal 1 to Terminal 5 for our 11:25 departure. This is a major inconvenience as one is required one to clear TSA security again. The lines were a bit long but we got through in less than 15 minutes. No consistency in TSA operations. At DFW I was not required to remove my laptop and iPad. At ORD, I was required to remove my laptop and iPad. ORD needs to have their Terminal Transfer Bus start operations earlier than 11:30.
